fix upstream tracking not being unset when using --base

When creating a branch with --base pointing to a remote-tracking branch
(e.g., origin/main), git automatically sets up upstream tracking. The code
tried to unset this, but the detection logic used git rev-parse which can

dashboard: add patch mode for hunk-by-hunk staging

Add git add -p style patch mode to the diff view:
- Press 'a' in WIP diff view to enter patch mode
- Navigate hunks with j/k
- Stage hunks with 'y', skip with 'n'
- Uses git apply --cached to stage individual hunks
- Diff refreshes after staging to show remaining changes

This allows selective staging of changes without leaving the dashboard.

dashboard: fix patch mode by using clean diff without ANSI colors

Remove --color=always from git diff commands so hunks are clean for
git apply. Delta will add syntax highlighting anyway. This fixes the
"patch does not apply" error that occurred because git apply couldn't
parse ANSI escape codes in the patch content.

dashboard: add manual diff coloring in patch mode

Since we removed --color=always from git diff (to fix staging), patch
mode now needs to color diff lines manually: green for additions, red
for deletions, cyan for hunk headers.

dashboard: fix patch mode to show only unstaged changes after staging

After staging a hunk with 'y', the diff now reloads using `git diff`
(without HEAD) which shows only unstaged changes. Previously it used
`git diff HEAD` which includes both staged and unstaged changes, so
the just-staged hunk would still appear and 'y' seemed to have no effect.

dashboard: fix filename parsing for diff.mnemonicPrefix

Git's diff.mnemonicPrefix option uses c/, w/, i/ prefixes instead of
the standard a/, b/. The filename parsing now handles any single-char
prefix by taking the last part of the diff --git line and stripping
the prefix.

Also shows the file header (diff --git, ---, +++) in patch mode for
context, matching git add -p behavior.

dashboard: render patch mode hunks through delta

Each hunk now has a pre-rendered version processed through delta for
syntax highlighting. The raw content is still kept for git apply.

dashboard: add basic diff coloring fallback when delta unavailable

When delta is not installed, falls back to basic ANSI coloring:
green for additions, red for deletions, cyan for hunk headers.

dashboard: add hunk splitting support in patch mode

Press 's' in patch mode to split a hunk into smaller hunks if there
are context lines between changes, similar to git add -p's split feature.

The split logic:
- Finds gaps where context lines separate change groups
- Creates new sub-hunks with recalculated @@ headers
- Each sub-hunk can be staged independently

dashboard: fix hunk splitting to include overlapping context

Split hunks now include overlapping context lines between change groups:
- First sub-hunk includes trailing context (up to next change)
- Second sub-hunk includes leading context (from after previous change)

This ensures git apply can locate and apply each sub-hunk correctly.

dashboard: preserve split hunks after staging

After staging a hunk, remove it from the in-memory list instead of
reloading from git. This preserves manually split hunks - git would
otherwise recombine the remaining changes into its own hunk structure.

Only reload from git when all in-memory hunks are exhausted, to check
for any remaining unstaged changes.

fix race condition when agent runs merge from inside worktree

When an agent (like Claude Code) runs `workmux merge` from inside a worktree's
tmux window, the previous code would rename the worktree directory to trash
synchronously before returning. This invalidated the agent's shell CWD, causing
subsequent hook invocations to fail with ENOENT when spawning /bin/sh.

The fix defers the entire destructive cleanup phase (rename, git worktree prune,
branch delete, trash removal) until after the tmux window is killed. This keeps
the worktree path valid while the agent runs its hooks. The deferred operations
are executed via tmux run-shell as part of the window close script.

Key changes:
- Add DeferredCleanup struct to carry cleanup state across the async boundary
- When running inside target window, skip synchronous destructive operations
- Pre-remove hooks and prompt file cleanup still run synchronously (harmless)
- Build shell script that runs mv, git prune, git branch -D, rm -rf after kill

feat: add WezTerm backend implementation

Add WezTerm as an alternative multiplexer backend alongside tmux.

  Key features:
  - Full parity with tmux backend (add, open, close, merge, remove,
list)
  - Workspace-based isolation (analogous to tmux sessions)
  - Named pipe handshake for shell synchronization
  - Cross-workspace navigation via OSC escape sequences

use nix::unistd::mkfifo instead of shelling out

Replace std::process::Command("mkfifo") with nix::unistd::mkfifo for
the Unix pipe handshake used by the WezTerm backend.

Benefits:
- Proper error handling (returns Result with errno)
- No subprocess spawn overhead or PATH dependency
- More reliable than shelling out to external binary

check read() return value in pipe handshake

Previously the return value of libc::read() was discarded, meaning the
handshake would succeed even if the writer closed the pipe without
sending data (EOF) or if read() returned an error.

Now we verify bytes_read > 0 before considering the handshake
successful, returning an error if the pipe was closed prematurely.

use serde_json for cross-workspace switch payload

Replace manual JSON string formatting with serde_json::json!() to
properly escape special characters in workspace and tab_title values.

Previously, values containing quotes or backslashes would produce
malformed JSON that the WezTerm Lua handler couldn't parse.

- remote.rs: remote operations (fetch_remote, ensure_fork_remote, etc.)

fix race condition in test exit code file polling

The test helpers (run_workmux_command, run_workmux_remove, run_workmux_merge,
run_workmux_close) had a race condition when checking for command completion.
They polled until the exit code file existed, but shell redirection creates
the file before writing content to it. This caused sporadic ValueError when
reading an empty file and trying to parse it as an integer.

Added poll_until_file_has_content() helper that waits for both file existence
AND non-empty content. Updated all four affected functions to use this new
helper, eliminating the flaky test failures.

log agent reset due to inactivity

Add tracing::info log message when an agent is reset in the dashboard
due to inactivity detection. This helps with debugging by making it

are automatically cleared.

preserve agent timer when status unchanged

When set-window-status is called with the same status the agent already
has (e.g., repeatedly setting "working"), the status_ts timestamp is now
preserved instead of being reset to the current time.

Previously, every call to `workmux set-window-status working` would reset
status_ts to now, causing the dashboard timer to restart from 0 even
though the agent was continuously working. This was confusing because the
timer would appear to reset randomly during a work session.

Now the code checks for an existing agent state with the same status and
reuses its timestamp, so the timer accurately reflects how long the agent
has been in that state.

fix tmux window not closing after merge in worktree agent

When running /merge from inside a worktree's tmux window, the deferred
cleanup script (executed via `tmux run-shell`) was failing to kill the
window while the directory cleanup succeeded.

Root cause: `tmux run-shell` executes commands in a detached context that
doesn't inherit the current session. When targeting windows with just
`-t '=window_name'`, tmux couldn't find the window because it was looking
in the wrong session (or no session at all).

Fix: Include the session name in tmux targets when building the deferred
cleanup script. Changed from `-t '=window_name'` to `-t 'session:=window_name'`.

This explains the intermittent behavior: direct `kill_window` calls (when
running outside the target window) worked because they ran in the current
shell's tmux context. Only the deferred `run-shell` path was broken.

- Add `current_session()` implementation to TmuxBackend
- Modify `navigate_to_target_and_close` to include session prefix in targets

handle read-only config file in nerdfont setup

allow symlinks pointing outside the repository

The path traversal check used canonicalize() which resolves symlinks,
rejecting any symlink inside the repo whose target was outside it.
This broke legitimate use cases like `.claude/skills/jira` symlinking
to a shared directory.

- Verifies the glob-matched path starts with repo_root
- Rejects any ".." components in the relative path portion

direct "../" pattern escapes and symlink-boundary traversal attacks
(e.g., `symlink_to_external/../secret`).

Key implementation details:
- Uses KITTY_WINDOW_ID for pane detection and KITTY_LISTEN_ON for instance ID

- Reuses UnixPipeHandshake for shell synchronization

kitty: fix split direction mapping

Kitty's split naming refers to the divider line orientation, which is

(top/bottom panes), while vsplit creates a vertical divider (left/right
panes). The mapping was inverted, causing horizontal splits to produce

fix window close and deferred cleanup for non-tmux backends

The deferred scripts in navigate_to_target_and_close hardcoded tmux

Also fixes kitty-specific issues:

kitty: fix agent status not showing by using stable foreground process

When set-window-status captured the foreground process via kitten @ ls,
it picked the first entry in foreground_processes which was often a
transient child process like "kitten" (from the ls query itself). During
reconciliation, the live foreground would be "claude" or "node", causing
a command mismatch that deleted the agent state immediately.

Use min_by_key on PID instead, which picks the most stable process (the
original user command) rather than short-lived children with higher PIDs.

The dashboard sends tmux-style key names like "BSpace", "Enter", "Up"
