Soften the tone and split into two paragraphs for readability.
First paragraph explains what the feature is, second covers the
security implications.

docs: move sandbox below dashboard in sidebar

Sandbox is a more advanced topic than dashboard, so it makes
sense to present it later in the navigation.

fail closed when bwrap missing on Linux host-exec

Previously, when bubblewrap was not installed on Linux, host-exec
silently fell back to unsandboxed execution with only a warning log.
This was a security issue -- commands ran without filesystem isolation.

Now host-exec refuses to run when bwrap is missing (fail closed).
Users who understand the risk can opt in to unsandboxed execution by
setting `sandbox.dangerously_allow_unsandboxed_host_exec: true` in
their global config. This skips the filesystem sandbox on both macOS
and Linux (only environment sanitization is applied).

Also resolves bwrap from a set of trusted absolute paths
(/usr/bin/bwrap, /usr/sbin/bwrap, /usr/local/bin/bwrap,
/run/current-system/sw/bin/bwrap for NixOS,
/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/bwrap) instead of relying on PATH
resolution, which could be hijacked via writable directories like
.cargo/bin.

Spawn failures now send an ExecError message to the guest before
the exit code, so agents see a meaningful error instead of a bare
exit 126.

make rpc_host global-only to prevent token exfiltration

A malicious .workmux.yaml could set rpc_host to redirect RPC traffic
to attacker infrastructure and harvest the session token. Apply the
same global-only pattern already used for host_commands: ignore the
project-level value and use only the global config value.

If a project config tries to set rpc_host, a warning is logged telling
the user to move it to their global config.

add missing credential paths to host-exec sandbox deny list

A poisoned build script running inside the sandbox could read sensitive
credential files and exfiltrate them via network access. This adds
several missing paths to the deny lists:

DENY_READ_DIRS: .claude (agent credentials), .config/gh (GitHub CLI),
.config/op (1Password CLI), .password-store (pass password manager)

DENY_READ_FILES: .claude-sandbox.json, .gitconfig, .bash_history,
.zsh_history, .vault-token (HashiCorp Vault)

DENY_READ_PATHS_MACOS: Library/Application Support/Arc (Arc browser),
.zsh_sessions (macOS zsh session data)

Also fixes the misleading "absolute" comment on DENY_READ_PATHS_MACOS
(they are HOME-relative) and replaces the individual-assertion test
with a comprehensive loop that verifies all deny paths appear in the
generated macOS Seatbelt profile.

lima: support non-Claude agents in VM provisioning

Lima provisioning previously hardcoded Claude CLI installation. Now the
configured `agent` setting drives which CLI gets installed during VM
creation, matching how the container backend already handles per-agent
images.

Key changes:
- Add `lima_install_script_for_agent()` with install snippets for claude,
  codex, gemini, and opencode (mirroring their respective Dockerfiles)
- Thread canonical agent name through `generate_lima_config()`,
  `generate_mounts()`, and `ensure_vm_running()`
- Gate Claude-specific state on agent: `seed_claude_json()` and the
  `~/.claude` mount only run when agent is "claude"
- Unknown agents get a no-op comment directing users to use the
  `provision` config for manual installation

lima: fix codex and opencode provisioning paths

Codex install script extracted to ~/.local/bin/ without creating the
directory first, which would fail on a fresh Debian image where that
directory does not exist. OpenCode installer places the binary under
~/.opencode/bin/ which is not on PATH in the Lima environment.

- Add `mkdir -p` before codex tarball extraction
- Symlink opencode binary to ~/.local/bin/ after installation

lima: cache gemini credentials on host filesystem

Mount ~/.gemini/ from host to guest VM so Gemini CLI credentials
persist across VM recreations. Authentication done inside the VM
is written to the mounted host directory.

This matches the existing behavior for Claude credentials.

docs: document credential caching for lima agents

Add a "Credential caching" section explaining which agents have
their credentials automatically mounted from the host, allowing
authentication to persist across VM recreations.

lima: skip nix/devbox install when toolchain is off

When toolchain: off is configured, skip installing Nix and Devbox
during VM provisioning. This speeds up VM creation and reduces disk

docs: rewrite credential caching as authentication section

Clarifies the auth behavior difference between agents: gemini
reuses host credentials from ~/.gemini/ since it stores auth as
files, while claude requires separate in-VM authentication because
it uses macOS Keychain on the host. Renamed section from "Credential
caching" to "Authentication" and updated the table to reflect actual
reuse behavior.

lima: fix codex binary installation

- Use musl build instead of gnu (avoids glibc 2.38/2.39 requirement)
- Rename extracted binary from codex-<arch>-unknown-linux-musl to codex

lima: skip nix/devbox install when project doesn't need it

When toolchain is auto (the default), nix and devbox were installed
unconditionally during VM provisioning even if the project had no
devbox.json or flake.nix. This added significant time to VM creation
for projects that don't use nix-based toolchains.

Now generate_lima_config takes a needs_nix flag, and the caller in
instance.rs resolves the toolchain against the actual project
directory. Nix/devbox are only installed when the project has
devbox.json or flake.nix, or when the user explicitly sets
toolchain to devbox or flake.

lima: cache codex credentials on host filesystem

Mount ~/.codex/ from host to guest VM so Codex credentials persist
across VM recreations. This matches the behavior for Claude and Gemini.

agents: add --yolo flag for gemini and codex in sandbox

Enable auto-approve mode when running Gemini and Codex in sandboxed
environments, matching Claude's --dangerously-skip-permissions behavior.

lima: mount opencode credentials into VM

OpenCode stores OAuth credentials (auth.json) at
~/.local/share/opencode/. Mount this directory into the Lima VM
guest so authentication persists across VM recreations and host
auth is reused automatically, matching the pattern used for
claude, gemini, and codex credential directories.
remove rosetta on arm64 documentation

sandbox: stop blocking ~/.gitconfig in host-exec sandbox

The sandbox-exec Seatbelt profile denied reading ~/.gitconfig because it
can contain credentials (e.g. inlined tokens in URL configs). However,
this breaks any tool that uses libgit2 for repository discovery, since
libgit2 loads ~/.gitconfig during git repo initialization.

Most notably, `cargo clippy --fix` (cargo fix) refuses to run with
"no VCS found" because libgit2 fails silently when the sandbox blocks
the gitconfig read.

In practice, macOS users typically use credential helpers
(osxkeychain) rather than inline tokens, so the actual secret
exposure risk is low. The tradeoff of breaking all git-dependent
tooling is not worth it.

- Add main worktree to security model access list (was mounted but not documented)
- Clarify Lima credential sharing is agent-dependent (Claude uses Keychain, others use files)
- Update comparison tables to reflect agent-specific auth behavior
- Change "Claude Code" references to generic "Agent" where appropriate

Addresses documentation gaps identified during Docker Sandboxes comparison analysis.

Previously the container backend only mounted Claude-specific paths

- claude: ~/.claude/ and ~/.claude-sandbox.json

- codex: ~/.codex/

For file-based agents (gemini, codex, opencode), the host directory is

This matches the behavior already implemented in the Lima backend.

Claude's ~/.claude-sandbox.json mount is now gated to claude agent only,

Add ~/.gemini, ~/.codex, and ~/.local/share/opencode to the list of

not just Claude.

When `container.runtime` is not explicitly set, detect which container

Native Linux builds linked against the host's glibc, which could be

docs: remove Devbox/Nix mention from host command proxying

Host command proxying works with any tools on the host, not just

The "Claude Code's built-in sandbox" section was part of the sandbox
overview page. It's tangential to the main guide content, so move it
to a dedicated "Alternatives" page under the sandbox section.

Also refines wording: workmux itself doesn't provide isolation -- it's
Docker/Podman containers and Lima VMs that do. Drops the redundant
"What this means" section since the comparison table already covers
the key points. Adds a note that unsandboxed retries go through the
normal permission flow.

decouple sandbox tests from OS sandbox availability

RPC exec pipeline tests (streaming, exit codes, env sanitization, arg
passing) were failing in Nix builds because they required bwrap to be
available and functional. These tests never tested sandbox enforcement
-- they tested the RPC protocol mechanics. Now they use
allow_unsandboxed_host_exec=true so they run everywhere.

The actual sandbox enforcement test (test_exec_sandbox_blocks_ssh_read)
now probes bwrap usability instead of just existence, and uses
platform-correct assertions: macOS expects ls to fail (deny), Linux
expects ls to succeed but return empty (tmpfs mask).

The freshness test_cache_file_path now uses a tempdir instead of
creating directories under real $HOME, fixing failures in read-only
build sandboxes.

add configurable network restrictions for container sandbox

Two-layer enforcement to restrict outbound network access from sandboxed
containers to only user-whitelisted domains:

1. Host-resident HTTP CONNECT proxy with domain allowlist, private IP
   rejection (RFC1918, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, IPv4-mapped IPv6),
   DNS TOCTOU prevention (resolve once, connect to validated SocketAddr),
   port-443-only, Basic auth with timing-safe comparison, and hardening
   limits (5s auth timeout, 8KB request cap, 16 connection cap).

2. In-container iptables with default-deny egress. Only proxy and RPC
   ports are whitelisted. IPv6 blocked entirely (ip6tables or sysctl
   fallback, fail-closed). Privileges dropped via gosu after firewall
   setup. network-init.sh resolves all IPs for proxy/RPC hosts to
   handle multi-A DNS and round-robin.

Configuration is global-only (project config cannot weaken restrictions):

  sandbox:
    network:
      policy: deny
      allowed_domains: ["*.anthropic.com", "github.com"]

Domain validation runs at config load time, rejecting IP literals,
trailing dots, malformed wildcards, and empty entries.

The sandbox shell command also applies network restrictions when starting
new containers (exec into existing containers inherits existing rules).

Sensitive values (proxy tokens, RPC tokens) are redacted in debug logs.

fix iptables not found in deny mode PATH

The container PATH env var (/tmp/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin)
did not include /usr/sbin where iptables lives on Debian. The
network-init.sh script failed with "iptables: command not found".

In deny mode, append /usr/sbin:/sbin to PATH so iptables, ip6tables,
and gosu are all reachable. Allow mode keeps the minimal PATH unchanged.
accept case-insensitive proxy-authorization header

allow DNS and use REJECT in network deny iptables rules

The iptables default-deny policy (OUTPUT DROP) silently blocked DNS
queries (UDP/TCP 53) to configured nameservers, causing any hostname
resolution inside the container to hang until timeout. Whitelist
nameservers from /etc/resolv.conf.

Also switch the catch-all from relying solely on the DROP policy to an
explicit REJECT rule at the end of the chain (both IPv4 and IPv6). This
makes blocked connections fail immediately with "connection refused"
instead of silently hanging, which is much easier to debug.

fix gosu breaking PTY and HOME in network deny mode

Two issues with the gosu privilege drop in network-init.sh caused Claude
Code to hang silently inside containers:

1. gosu resets HOME via getpwuid(), which returns "/" for UIDs that don't
   exist in /etc/passwd (the container runs as an arbitrary host UID).
   Claude then tries to use /.claude/ instead of /tmp/.claude/, can't
   write there, and hangs. Fix by wrapping with `env HOME=/tmp`.

2. Docker allocates the PTY as root. After gosu drops to the target UID,
   the user has no read access to /dev/pts/0 (owned root:tty, mode
   crw--w----). Fix by chowning the PTY before dropping privileges.

log proxy rejections at warn level

Proxy domain/port/IP rejections were logged at debug level, making it
impossible to diagnose which domains were being blocked without
explicitly enabling debug logging. Promoting to warn makes blocked
requests visible in default log output, which is critical for
discovering which domains need to be allowlisted (e.g. OAuth endpoints).
add network section to sandbox comparison table

fix BufReader data loss in HTTP CONNECT proxy

BufReader::into_inner() discards any bytes that were buffered but not
yet consumed. When a client pipelines the CONNECT request and TLS
ClientHello in the same TCP segment, the TLS bytes sit in BufReader's
internal buffer and get silently dropped, causing connections to hang
or reset.

Drain any remaining buffered bytes into the target stream before
starting the bidirectional tunnel. This ensures pipelined data (most
commonly the TLS ClientHello) is correctly forwarded.

Add a unit test that sends CONNECT headers + extra bytes in a single
write and verifies the extra bytes arrive at the target.

disable git native hooks in RPC-spawned commands

The RPC handler already passed --no-verify --no-hooks to suppress workmux's
own pre_merge hooks, but these flags have no effect on git's native hooks.
A malicious sandbox guest could write a script to .git/hooks/post-merge (the
.git directory is bind-mounted RW), then trigger a Merge RPC -- the hook
would execute on the host with full user privileges, escaping the container.

Fix by setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null via GIT_CONFIG_* environment
variables on the Command objects spawned by handle_merge and
handle_spawn_agent. These env vars propagate to all child git processes,
disabling post-merge, post-rewrite, post-checkout, and all other native
hooks. Also removes GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS to prevent it from overriding
the hook suppression.

The same fix is applied to handle_spawn_agent since `workmux add` runs
`git worktree add` which triggers post-checkout hooks.

make image, env_passthrough, and extra_mounts global-only

These three sandbox config fields were previously overridable by project
config via .workmux.yaml, which is inconsistent with other
security-sensitive fields (network, host_commands, rpc_host) that are
already global-only.

A malicious .workmux.yaml in a cloned repo could:
- Use a custom image without security tooling (iptables/gosu)
- Request passthrough of host env secrets (AWS keys, tokens)
- Mount over critical host paths (e.g. /usr/local/bin/network-init.sh)

Now all three fields use the same global-only pattern: the global value
is always used, and a warning is logged if the project config tries to
set them, telling the user to move the setting to their global config.

Tests updated to verify project values are ignored for all three fields.
Docs updated to mark these fields as global-only in container, Lima,
and shared features pages.

default env_passthrough to empty list

GITHUB_TOKEN was previously passed through to sandboxes by default.
This changes the default to an empty list, requiring users to
explicitly configure any environment variables they want passed

credentials without explicit opt-in.

fix skip-permissions flag injected into non-agent panes

When `sandbox.target` is `all`, the skip-permissions flag (e.g.
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) was injected into every sandboxed
pane's command, not just agent panes. This caused non-agent commands
like `just check` to fail with unexpected argument errors.

Now the flag is only injected when the pane is detected as an agent
pane.

When an agent commits inside a sandbox (container or Lima VM), git
operations fail because there's no git user configuration. The sandbox
intentionally does not mount ~/.gitconfig (security concern).

remove stall detection from dashboard

The stall detection (added in df8c5a3) was resetting timers spuriously for
agents that appeared idle. It monitored Working agents for unchanged terminal
output and after only 4 seconds would clear their status and reset status_ts.

During normal Claude Code operation, there are frequent gaps in output (waiting

fix stale sandbox image hint persisting after pull

The freshness cache stored is_fresh: false for 24 hours and never
re-checked, so the "newer image available" hint kept appearing even
after the user pulled the latest image.

- Call mark_fresh() after sandbox pull to immediately update the cache
- Store local_image_id in the cache so that when cached as stale, a
  cheap local docker inspect can detect if the image changed (e.g. via
  docker pull directly), triggering a re-check instead of blindly
  showing the hint

The local_image_id field uses #[serde(default)] for backward
compatibility with existing cache files.

fix backend detection priority for nested multiplexers

When running tmux inside kitty (or wezterm), workmux incorrectly
detected kitty as the backend because $KITTY_WINDOW_ID was checked
before $TMUX. This caused failures for users who run tmux inside kitty
without kitty remote control configured.

Detection order is now: $TMUX > $WEZTERM_PANE > $KITTY_WINDOW_ID,
prioritizing session-specific env vars (set only when inside the
multiplexer) over ambient ones (inherited from the parent terminal).

surfaced from the command's own config load.

nerdfont wizard when config_ok is true. The actual parse error still
surfaces when the command loads config with proper error propagation.

sandbox: create shim tempdir under ~/.cache for Colima compatibility

Colima (Docker Desktop alternative for macOS) only mounts the home
directory into its VM by default. The previous tempfile::tempdir()

which Colima's VM cannot see, causing bind mount failures:

Move shim tempdir creation to ~/.cache/workmux/shims/ which is
guaranteed to be under ~ and accessible to all container runtimes
(Docker Desktop, Colima, Podman). Uses tempfile::Builder::tempdir_in()
to retain RAII cleanup semantics.

fix list command to show session-mode worktrees

fix --wait flag for session mode

The --wait flag was polling window names instead of checking session
existence. Now uses wait_until_session_closed for session-mode

Use current_session() instead of current_window_name() when detecting
if we're inside the session being closed. Previously, session mode
would never detect current target correctly because window name
(e.g., "zsh") doesn't match session name (e.g., "wm-feature").

fix session cleanup target format in navigate_to_target_and_close

fix remove to use resolved handle for session mode detection

fix session mode detection in remove and merge

fix dashboard worktree name for session-mode worktrees

default shell (e.g. "zsh"). The dashboard's extract_worktree_name only

add shell_switch_session_cmd and shell_kill_session_cmd to Multiplexer trait

fix session cleanup to use kill-session instead of kill-window

fix misleading --session flag reference in open error message

The open command doesn't have a --session flag (only add does), so

fix mixed-mode navigation in navigate_to_target_and_close

The target existence check and select command were using the source
worktree's mode, which breaks when source and target are different
modes (e.g. removing a session-mode worktree navigates to a
window-mode main branch).

Now probes both session_exists and window_exists_by_full_name to
detect the target's actual type, and uses that for the select command
while keeping the source mode for the kill command.

defer worktree metadata removal until after cleanup script

Previously, worktree metadata (mode) was removed unconditionally at
the end of cleanup(), even when destructive cleanup was deferred to
a shell script. If the deferred script failed, the worktree would
remain but its mode metadata would be lost, causing follow-up
commands to mis-detect mode.

Now metadata is only removed immediately in the synchronous path.
For deferred cleanup, the removal is included in the shell script
after the destructive operations.

fix open command not passing stored mode to setup options

The open workflow resolved the stored worktree mode but never assigned

Now it returns an explicit error explaining that the host controls the

batch-load worktree modes in list workflow

git config --get-regexp call that fetches all worktree modes at once.

becomes noticeable with many worktrees.

rename created_windows to created_targets in add command

The variable tracks both windows and sessions for --wait, so the old
name was misleading now that session mode exists.

switch to last session before killing on session removal

When removing a session-mode worktree from inside it, tmux would pick
an arbitrary session after the kill. Now the deferred script runs
`switch-client -l` first, returning the user to the session they were
on before switching into the workmux session.

remove unused MuxHandle methods

Remove 5 instance methods (mode, kill, schedule_close, shell_kill_cmd,

static variants since they already have a resolved full name string.

release v0.1.121

prefix fork ref local branch names with owner

When using `workmux add user:branch`, the local branch name is now
derived as `user-branch` instead of just `branch`. This prevents
conflicts when the fork's branch name matches an existing local branch
(e.g., `workmux add sundbp:main` would fail because `main` already
exists as a worktree).

The owner:branch syntax already signals the branch belongs to someone
else, so including the owner in the local name is both informative and
deterministic -- the same command always produces the same local branch
name regardless of local repository state.

Examples:
- `sundbp:main` -> local branch `sundbp-main`
- `owner:feature-branch` -> local branch `owner-feature-branch`
- `user:feature/foo` -> local branch `user-feature-foo` (after slugify)

add schedule_cleanup_and_close trait method for multiplexer-agnostic cleanup

The previous implementation of deferred worktree cleanup in cleanup.rs
used tmux-specific commands directly, which broke cleanup for non-tmux
backends like zellij. When running `wm rm` from inside a worktree's
window, the worktree would not be removed because the tmux commands
failed silently.

operation. Each backend now implements this method appropriately:

- ZellijBackend: Uses `trap '' HUP` to survive PTY destruction
- WezTermBackend: Uses nohup to detach the cleanup process

calls the trait method, removing the direct dependency on tmux.

zellij: fix focus handling to respect configured pane focus

The default zellij behavior automatically focuses newly created panes.
When splitting panes, the most recently created pane gets focus,
which doesn't respect the `focus: true` configuration in panes.

This commit overrides setup_panes() for ZellijBackend to:
1. Track which pane index should have focus during creation
2. After all panes are created, navigate to the correct pane using
   focus-previous-pane/focus-next-pane commands

This ensures that when a user configures:
```yaml
panes:
  - command: <agent>
    focus: true
  - split: horizontal
```

The first pane (agent) maintains focus as expected, rather than
focus shifting to the second pane.

use Option types in LivePaneInfo instead of sentinel values

LivePaneInfo.pid was u32 (with 0 meaning "unsupported") and
current_command was String (with "" meaning "unsupported"). This
relied on callers remembering to check for sentinel values, which
the compiler couldn't enforce.

Changed pid to Option<u32> and current_command to Option<String> so
backends that don't expose PIDs (Zellij) or commands use None, and
reconciliation uses is_some_and() instead of != 0 / !is_empty()
guards. The compiler now enforces handling the "unsupported" case.

add window_hint to switch_to_pane, remove StateStore dependency from Zellij

ZellijBackend::switch_to_pane previously created a StateStore and
called load_reconciled_agents(self) just to find the tab name for
a pane ID. This inverted the dependency direction (backend -> state)
and triggered side effects (stale agent deletion, disk I/O).

All callers already have the window/tab name available from AgentPane
or AgentState, so pass it as an optional hint parameter. Backends
that can switch by pane ID directly (tmux, WezTerm, Kitty) ignore it.

add supports_preview guard to update_preview, remove dashboard UI hack

update_preview() was missing the supports_preview() check that
refresh_preview() already had, causing Zellij to spawn dump-screen
+ temp file I/O on every selection change even though the UI hides
the preview pane.

To compensate, contains_dashboard_ui() used brittle string matching
("Preview:", "[i] input") to detect self-capture. This would false-
positive on any agent working with files containing those strings.

With the guard in place, capture_pane is never called when preview
is unsupported, so the hack is no longer needed.

remove unused cached_data parameter from validate_agent_alive

The cached_data: Option<&[String]> parameter was added to
validate_agent_alive for Zellij to receive pre-fetched tab names,
but the Zellij implementation never used it (prefixed with _).

Meanwhile, store.rs was spawning a `zellij action list-tabs`
subprocess to build this cache on every reconciliation pass.
Remove the parameter and the unused cache-building code.

simplify to_agent_pane to use arguments directly

to_agent_pane() was overriding caller-provided session/window_name
with stored values when present. This defeated reconciliation: the
caller in store.rs computed fresh values from live pane info, but
to_agent_pane silently discarded them if stored values existed.

Now the method uses arguments as-is. Callers already handle the
fallback logic (live values -> stored values -> defaults).

fix PaneKey doc comment for Zellij pane_id format

The doc said Zellij uses tab names (e.g., "wm-feature") as pane IDs,
but the actual implementation uses terminal pane IDs (e.g., "terminal_5").

docs: mention Zellij alongside kitty and WezTerm

Add Zellij references everywhere kitty and WezTerm are mentioned as
alternative backends: README, guide pages, quick start, session mode
limitations, contributing guide, and homepage meta description.

Links point to the existing /guide/zellij doc page. Detection uses
$ZELLIJ env var consistent with the actual backend detection code.

zellij: override should_exit_on_jump to keep dashboard alive

ZellijBackend was inheriting the trait default (true) but callers
in diff_ops.rs and app.rs were written assuming Zellij returns false.

The dashboard runs in a persistent tab, so jumping to an agent tab
just switches tabs without destroying the dashboard. Returning true
was causing the dashboard to exit on every jump, commit, and merge
action, contradicting the comments in diff_ops.rs.

remove heartbeat mechanism from dashboard refresh loop

The heartbeat system wrote N disk reads + N disk writes per dashboard
refresh cycle for backends without stable pane IDs. However, no backend
ever overrode stable_pane_ids() to return false, making the entire
heartbeat update block dead code.

Worse, Zellij's validate_agent_alive used stale heartbeat timestamps
(only set at agent creation, never refreshed) to falsely declare agents
dead after 5 minutes.

Removal is safe because get_all_live_pane_info() already fetches all
panes in a single batched query. The None branch in reconciliation
(where validate_agent_alive is called) only fires when a pane genuinely
doesn't appear in that result, so the heartbeat fast-path provided no
value even if it had been kept up to date.

Changes:
- Remove last_heartbeat field from AgentState
- Remove heartbeat update block from dashboard refresh
- Remove stable_pane_ids() from Multiplexer trait (unused by all backends)
- Simplify Zellij validate_agent_alive to pane existence + command check

Existing state files with last_heartbeat are handled gracefully by
serde's unknown-field tolerance.

fix dashboard commit/merge actions quitting for tmux/WezTerm

The Zellij integration incorrectly used should_exit_on_jump() in
send_commit_to_agent, trigger_merge, and their *_selected variants.
This caused tmux/WezTerm to quit the dashboard when sending commit or
merge commands, instead of the original behavior of closing the diff
modal and staying in the dashboard.

The root issue was conflating two concepts: "needs focus to send input"
vs "should exit dashboard on jump." Add requires_focus_for_input() trait
method so only Zellij switches tabs before sending keys, while all
backends preserve the original post-action behavior (close_diff or stay).

fix close command handle resolution when handle differs from branch name

close.rs was deriving mode and constructing MuxHandle from raw CLI input
instead of resolving through git::find_worktree first. When a user ran
'workmux close feature/foo' but the worktree handle was 'api-foo', it
would look up the wrong mode (workmux.worktree.feature/foo.mode instead
of workmux.worktree.api-foo.mode) and construct an incorrect target name
(wm-feature/foo instead of wm-api-foo).

Now find_worktree is called during handle resolution. The actual handle
is extracted from the worktree path basename before mode lookup and
MuxHandle construction. This matches the pattern already used in
workflow::open.

and closes it using the branch name to verify resolution works correctly.

which handles VitePress SPA route changes automatically without

replace fs_extra with std::fs for file/directory copying

fs_extra was used in a single file (setup.rs) for copying files and
directories into new worktrees. Replaced with std::fs::copy for files
and a small copy_dir_recursive helper for directories.

The helper properly handles:

add Apple Container as a sandbox runtime

Add Apple Container (`container` binary) as a third container runtime
alongside Docker and Podman. This enables sandboxing on macOS using
Apple's native container/VM technology (macOS 26+, Apple Silicon).

Key changes:

- Add `AppleContainer` variant to `SandboxRuntime` with serde name
  `apple-container` (alias `apple`)
- Add capability methods on the enum (`binary_name`, `needs_add_host`,
  `needs_userns_keep_id`, `needs_deny_mode_caps`, `pull_args`,
  `supports_file_mounts`) to replace match blocks throughout
- Auto-detection prefers `container` > `docker` > `podman` on macOS
  (gated behind `cfg!(target_os = "macos")` to avoid false positives)
- Skip freshness checking for Apple Container (no Docker-buildx
  equivalent available)
- Store runtime in StateStore marker files for cleanup correctness,
  so containers are stopped with the correct binary even if config
  changes between start and stop
- `stop_containers_for_handle` groups by stored runtime, no longer
  takes a config parameter
- `list_containers` returns `Vec<(String, SandboxRuntime)>` with
  tolerant parsing (empty marker files default to Docker for backwards
  compatibility)
- `sandbox shell --exec` reads stored runtime from state instead of
  current config
- Apple Container only supports directory mounts (virtiofs), so Claude
  config uses `~/.claude-sandbox-config/claude.json` with a directory
  mount and in-container symlink, while Docker/Podman keep the existing
  `~/.claude-sandbox.json` file mount
- `rpc_host` defaults to `192.168.64.1` for Apple Container
- Apple Container uses `image pull` subcommand (vs `pull` for others)
- Skip `--cap-add=NET_ADMIN` and `--security-opt` in deny mode since
  Apple Container VMs already have full capabilities as root

remove flex-direction and align-items from ed-hero-actions

add self-update command

Add `workmux update` that downloads and installs the latest release
binary from GitHub Releases. Uses curl/tar subprocesses to avoid adding
HTTP or archive dependencies.

The update flow:
- Fetches latest version from GitHub API
- Downloads the platform-appropriate tar.gz and .sha256 checksum
- Verifies SHA-256 integrity before installing
- Replaces the binary atomically with rollback on failure
- Detects Homebrew installs and directs to `brew upgrade` instead

Spinner shows progress through each phase and cleanly reports
success or failure.

add background update check with throttled notifications

On CLI startup, workmux now reads a local cache file to check if a
newer version is available and shows a one-line stderr notice at most
once per 24 hours. A detached background process (`_check-update`)
refreshes the cache by querying the GitHub API, keeping the main
command non-blocking.

Design choices:
- Detached subprocess avoids blocking the main command
- Cache at ~/.cache/workmux/update_check.json prevents repeated API calls
- Numeric version comparison (not string equality) handles 0.1.10 > 0.1.9
- Suppressed in non-interactive contexts (piped stdout/stderr)
- Background curl has 5s connect / 10s max timeout
- Spawn failure doesn't suppress future checks (no silent blackout)

Disable via config (`auto_update_check: false`) or environment
(`WORKMUX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`).
docs: document automatic update check and how to disable it

limit update check to workmux add

Only check for updates during `workmux add` to avoid unexpected
output on other commands. This is the most common entry point and
keeps the notification surface minimal.

jq is a fundamental CLI tool that hooks and scripts commonly depend

(claude, codex, gemini, opencode) have it available without needing

increase test timeouts to fix flaky tmux tests

Under parallel pytest load (12 workers), tmux pane startup and script
execution can exceed the previous 2-second timeouts. Bump wait_for_file

add clipboard proxy for sandbox image pasting

Allow TUI agents (Claude Code, opencode) inside sandboxed containers/VMs
to paste images via Ctrl+V by proxying clipboard reads to the host.

Built-in wl-paste and xclip shims translate Linux clipboard tool CLIs
into `workmux clipboard-read` calls. A ClipboardRead RPC request triggers
the host to read the clipboard (osascript on macOS, wl-paste/xclip on
Linux), write the PNG to the shared worktree filesystem (.workmux/tmp/),
and return the absolute path. The guest reads the file, writes raw bytes
to stdout, and deletes it. No binary data travels over JSON-lines RPC.

Key details:
- Only image/png supported for v1
- Clipboard shims use separate ClipboardRead RPC, not host-exec Exec RPC
- Shims are regular script files (not symlinks to _shim dispatcher)
- 20 MB size limit, stale file pruning >1 hour
- xclip write mode rejected with error message

fix install-dev container build with Apple Container

Apple Container's `container build` doesn't resolve "." correctly when

context path as a positional argument instead, which works with both
Apple Container and Docker/Podman.

SOPS stores age secret keys and PGP material in ~/.config/sops/.
A compromised guest build file could exfiltrate these via an
allowlisted host command. Add the directory to DENY_READ_DIRS so

fix _1x image generation race in docs dev server

The retina images plugin's buildStart hook fires async but Vite's dev
server doesn't block module resolution on it. When index.md gets
processed, the transform hook injects /_1x/ image references before
generateRetina1x has finished creating the files, causing import
resolution errors on first run in a new worktree.

markdown processing is blocked until images exist.

support tmux color codes in dashboard status icons

The dashboard rendered tmux style codes like #[fg=#a6e3a1] as literal

the tmux status bar handled them correctly since tmux interprets its own
format codes natively.

Add a tmux style parser (parse_tmux_styles) that converts #[...] blocks

already used by git and PR column formatting.

Supported tmux attributes: fg=, bg=, default/none. Color formats: hex
(#RRGGBB), named colors (red, blue, etc.), indexed (colour0-colour255).
Malformed or unknown directives are handled gracefully.

release v0.1.128

fix: zsh completions not working with fpath autoloading

The previous architecture defined _workmux (clap-generated) and
_workmux_dynamic (wrapper), relying on `compdef _workmux_dynamic workmux`
inside the autoloaded function to swap the completion handler. This
reassignment didn't reliably take effect for subsequent completions
when loaded via zsh's fpath autoloading mechanism.

Restructure so the dynamic wrapper IS the _workmux function:

- Post-process clap's zsh output via prepare_zsh_base() to rename
  _workmux -> _workmux_base and strip clap's autoload/eval block
- The dynamic wrapper is now _workmux itself, delegating flag
  completion to _workmux_base and positional args to the dynamic
  helpers (_workmux_handles, _workmux_git_branches)
- _comps[workmux] stays _workmux throughout -- no compdef swap needed

Works correctly with both `eval "$(workmux completions zsh)"` and
file-based fpath autoloading.

fix: zsh completions fall back to file completion for handle/branch args

Commands like open, remove, merge, add only accept worktree handles or
branch names, never file paths. Previously _workmux_base was called
alongside the dynamic completers, which dragged in _default (file
completion) via clap's generated _arguments positional specs.

Stop calling _workmux_base for positional args on these commands. Flag
completion still delegates to _workmux_base when the current word
starts with -.

fix: phantom whitespace completion when no candidates exist

\`"${(@f)$(cmd)}"\` on empty command output produces a single-element
array containing an empty string. compadd then offers that empty string
as a completion candidate, resulting in phantom whitespace.

Filter empty strings from the array with \`${handles:#}\` and skip
compadd entirely when there are no candidates.

remove stale worktree locks before pruning during cleanup

git worktree prune silently skips locked worktrees. If git worktree add
was interrupted, it leaves a "locked" file (containing "initializing")
in $GIT_COMMON_DIR/worktrees/<name>/ that never gets cleaned up. This
caused wm rm to fail with "cannot delete branch used by worktree"
because prune didn't remove the metadata.

Before pruning, the cleanup now resolves the worktree admin directory
(by reading the .git file's gitdir pointer, with a fallback to the
conventional path) and removes any lock file. This applies to both
the synchronous and deferred cleanup paths. Relative gitdir paths
are normalized to absolute, and parse failures are logged.

add auto_name.command config field

Allow users to configure a custom command for LLM-based branch name
generation instead of the hardcoded `llm` CLI. The command string is
parsed with shlex into program + fixed arguments, and the composed
prompt (system prompt + user input) is appended as the final argument
at execution time. For example, `command: "claude -p"` becomes
`claude -p "<prompt>"`.

When `command` is set, the `model` option is ignored since it is
specific to the `llm` CLI. When `command` is absent or empty, behavior
is unchanged and `llm` is used as before.

Implementation splits the monolithic generate_branch_name into a
dispatcher (run_generator_command) that routes to either
run_custom_command or run_llm_command, with shared prompt composition
and branch name sanitization.

infer auto_name command from agent profile

When no auto_name.command is configured, automatically use the
configured agent's CLI for branch name generation with a fast/cheap
model. The resolution order is:

1. auto_name.command (explicit config)
2. Agent profile default (claude, gemini, codex, opencode)
3. llm CLI fallback

Agent profile defaults:
- claude: claude --model haiku -p
- gemini: gemini -m gemini-2.5-flash-lite -p
- codex: codex exec --config model_reasoning_effort="low" -m gpt-5.1-codex-mini
- opencode: opencode run

Additional improvements from review feedback:
- auto_name.command is now global-only for security (prevents RCE
  via malicious .workmux.yaml)
- Deep merge for auto_name config (project can override model,
  system_prompt, background but not command)
- Custom commands now pipe prompt via stdin instead of argv
  (avoids E2BIG and process listing exposure)
- Spinner shows which tool is being used ("Generating branch name
  with claude")
- Error messages fall back to stdout when stderr is empty
- Whitespace-only command no longer bypasses agent inference

auto-suffix window name on cross-repo collision

When creating worktrees with the same branch name across different
repositories in the same tmux session, workmux now auto-suffixes the
handle with the project directory name instead of failing with
"window already exists".

Detection uses `target_exists && !worktree_exists` to identify that
the mux target belongs to a different repo. The suffix uses the
project directory name (e.g., `wm-feature-auth-frontend`), with
guards for empty and purely-numeric slugs to avoid colliding with
cleanup's `base(-\d+)?` regex used for `open --new` duplicates.

Key changes:
- Add `resolved_handle` field to `CreateResult` so callers use the
  actual handle for --wait tracking and rollback cleanup
- Add `is_explicit_name` to `CreateArgs` so --name collisions produce
  a hard error instead of silent auto-suffixing
- Move window name tracking in add.rs to after create() returns
- Print info message to stderr when auto-suffixing occurs

`kiro-cli chat` starts the interactive session, unlike other agents where
the bare executable starts chat mode directly.

prefix fork PR local branch names with owner to avoid conflicts

When checking out a fork PR with `--pr` whose branch is named "main" (or
any other name that conflicts with an existing local branch), the worktree
creation would fail because the local branch name was set directly to the
PR's head_ref_name without any prefix.

The `owner:branch` syntax already handled this by prefixing with the fork
owner (e.g., `sundbp-main`), but `resolve_pr_ref` did not apply the same
logic for fork PRs.

Now fork PRs automatically get prefixed with the fork owner (e.g.,
`forkowner-main`), consistent with the `owner:branch` behavior. A shared
`fork_local_branch_name()` helper is used by both code paths. Custom
branch names via `workmux add custom-name --pr 123` are still honored.

add container memory and cpu config for Apple Container

Apple Container VMs default to 1 GB RAM which causes OOM kills for
real workloads (e.g. cloning node_modules). Since --memory sets a
ceiling (not upfront allocation), a generous 16G default is safe.

Add container.memory and container.cpus fields to ContainerConfig.
Apple Container gets --memory 16G by default when unconfigured.
Docker/Podman skip these flags unless explicitly set by the user.
Empty string values are treated as unset to prevent invalid args.

strip ANSI escape sequences from auto-name generator output

kiro-cli emits ANSI color codes and bell characters in its output even
when piped (e.g. "\x1b[38;5;141m> \x1b[0m...branch-name\x07"). This
caused sanitize_branch_name to mangle the escape bytes into the branch
name, producing names like "38-5-141m-0minvestigate-zero-report".

stops emitting ANSI in the future, the regex is a no-op.

add delay between paste and enter in paste_multiline

When sending multiline content to an agent via bracketed paste, the
Enter keystroke to submit was arriving before the application (e.g.
Claude Code) finished processing the paste event, causing the Enter
to be swallowed. The user would have to manually press Enter.

Add a 100ms delay between paste-buffer and send-keys Enter in all
three backends (tmux, wezterm, kitty) to let the application process
the bracketed paste before submitting.

Verified by testing against a live Claude Code instance: without the
delay, pasted text shows up but isn't submitted; with the delay, it
submits correctly.

fix structured theme block corruption in save_theme_scheme

The previous logic used a flawed alphanumeric check to detect structured
theme blocks, which always evaluated false for "theme:" since "theme"
contains alphanumeric characters. This meant indented sub-keys (scheme:,
mode:) were never removed, producing invalid YAML like:

  theme: glacier-signal
    scheme: emberforge
    mode: dark

Rewrite to use a peekable iterator that correctly detects block-style
theme config (bare "theme:" with nothing after the colon) and skips
all indented sub-keys before inserting the new flat value.

fix theme save edge cases and add comprehensive tests

Fix three issues found in code review:

1. Save now preserves explicit mode override. When config had
   theme: { scheme: X, mode: dark }, cycling would lose the mode
   and emit a flat theme: Y. Now emits structured block when mode
   is explicitly set.

2. Prefer uncommented theme: over # theme: when both exist. The
   previous matcher treated commented examples as equivalent to
   active config entries, which could activate a comment and leave
   the real entry as a duplicate.

3. Skip blank lines within structured theme blocks. A block like
   theme:\n  scheme: X\n\n  mode: dark would leave orphaned keys
   after rewrite.

Extracts save logic into a pure update_theme_in_config() function
for testability. Adds 16 persistence tests covering: simple/structured
blocks, blank lines in blocks, mode preservation, commented vs active
lines, empty files, default commenting-out, and trailing newline
handling. Adds 12 config deserialization tests covering: string scheme,
legacy dark/light, structured maps, unknown values, full config files,
and missing theme defaults.

add --prompt-file-only flag for embedded agent workflows

Users who run editors with embedded agents (e.g., neovim with an agent
plugin) cannot use workmux's prompt features because validate_prompt_consumption()
requires an agent pane to be configured.

The new --prompt-file-only flag (and prompt_file_only config option) writes the
prompt to .workmux/PROMPT-<branch>.md without requiring an agent pane or injecting
the prompt into pane commands. The editor can then detect and consume the file on
startup.

Key implementation details:
- In create.rs, the prompt file is always written, but prompt_file_path is set to
  None in SetupOptions when file-only mode is active, bypassing both validation
  and injection
- In open.rs, the prompt is passed into workflow::open so the file is written
  before pane commands start (avoiding a race with editor startup)
- The add -o (open-if-exists) delegation path also passes the prompt through
- Config merging includes the new field so project config can override global

In session mode, select_pane + switch_to_session(session_name) always
landed on the first window. This is because tmux select-pane only sets

the pane ID directly. tmux resolves this to the correct session, window,

state store cleanup happens automatically on the next reconciliation.

list: add --json flag for machine-readable output

Adds a `--json` flag to `workmux list` that outputs a JSON array of
objects with fields: handle, branch, path, is_main, mode,
has_uncommitted_changes, is_open. This provides a stable API for
external tooling (e.g., custom tmux session switchers) that previously
had to parse the human-readable table output.

Key implementation details:
- has_uncommitted_changes is only computed when --json is used to
  avoid spawning extra git subprocesses on regular list calls
- PR fetch is short-circuited when --json is set since PR data is
  not included in the JSON schema
- WorktreeInfo gains handle, is_main, and mode fields populated
  from already-computed values in the workflow list function
- Empty results output [] instead of "No worktrees found"

dashboard: use theme-consistent colors for kill confirmation popup

Use help_border, dimmed, and help_muted from the palette instead of
the warning color. Matches the style of the help overlay.

dashboard: highlight y and n keys in kill confirmation popup

Use text+bold for the key letters and dimmed for the suffixes so
the actionable keys visually stand out.

dashboard: add worktree view as second tab

Add a Worktrees tab to the dashboard, toggled with Tab (jump-to-last
agent remapped to Backspace). The worktree view shows a flat table of
all git worktrees with columns for project, handle, branch, PR status,
and agent summary.

Key features:
- Background worktree loading via mpsc channel (same pattern as git/PR
  fetchers) to avoid blocking the UI
- Delete worktrees with x; confirmation popup when uncommitted changes
  or unmerged commits exist, immediate delete for clean+merged
- Enter jumps to worktree's agent if one exists, falls back to
  MuxHandle for correct session/window mode dispatch
- Preview pane shows git log --oneline for selected worktree
- Separate filter state per tab (/ key works in both views)
- Worktrees sorted by project name then handle
- Tab-aware filter actions, quit behavior, and footer rendering
- Confirmation popup styled consistently with kill popup (help_border,
  text, dimmed colors)

dashboard: fix layout constraint overflow and ANSI fallback

Use Fill constraints instead of Percentage/Min to prevent layout
overflow when the tab header, table, preview, and footer compete
for space. Nest the layout so the tab header and footer always get
their 1 line each.

Strip ANSI escapes in the preview fallback path to prevent raw
control sequences from corrupting the terminal when into_text()
parsing fails.

Use Fill(1) instead of Min(0) in footer horizontal layouts for
consistent constraint behavior.

dashboard: disable PR spinner in worktree background fetch

Pass fetch_pr_status=false to workflow::list() when called from the
dashboard background thread. The dashboard fetches PR status
separately via spawn_pr_status_fetch(), and workflow::list's
spinner::with_spinner() writes progress characters to stderr which
shares the terminal with the TUI, corrupting the display.

dashboard: unify background channels into AppEvent with input thread

Replace 4 separate mpsc channel pairs (git_tx/rx, pr_tx/rx,
worktree_tx/rx, worktree_log_tx/rx) with a single AppEvent enum
and event channel. Move terminal input to a dedicated background
thread that forwards crossterm events as AppEvent::Terminal.

The main loop now blocks on recv_timeout() instead of
event::poll(), waking instantly when any background thread sends
data. This eliminates polling entirely: git status, PR status,
worktree list, and git log preview all appear on the next frame
as soon as they're ready instead of waiting for a 2-second refresh
cycle.

Background events are coalesced by draining the channel after the
first event wakes the loop, preventing redundant redraws when
multiple threads complete simultaneously.

dashboard: skip rendering empty worktree table to avoid blink

Don't render the table headers when the worktree list is empty.
The first frame after switching tabs has no data yet (background
fetch is in flight), and rendering headers with default column
widths causes a visible jump when the data arrives and column
widths adjust. A blank area that fills with the complete table on
the next frame is visually seamless.

dashboard: add divider line between tab header and table

Render a thin horizontal rule below the Agents/Worktrees tab
labels to visually separate the tab bar from the table content.
The tab header area grows from 1 to 2 lines to accommodate the
divider.

dashboard: add space between agent icon and spinner in worktree view

The agent status column in the worktree table was rendering the
robot emoji and spinner dots without spacing, unlike the agents
view which separates them.

dashboard: improve worktree table columns

Remove the redundant Branch column since it's identical to the
Worktree handle for most rows. When the branch differs (e.g. the
main worktree), show it inline with an arrow: "workmux ->main".

Add a Git column with diff stats, reusing format_git_status from
the agents view, including the spinner indicator during fetches.

Hide the PR column when no worktree has a PR, matching the agents
view behavior. This avoids a column of dashes taking up space.

dashboard: make 1-9 keys jump to worktree instead of selecting

In the agents view, number keys jump to the agent and close the
dashboard. The worktree view was only selecting the row. Now it
calls jump_to_selected_worktree() for consistent behavior.

dashboard: rename worktree preview title to "Git Log"

The preview pane in the worktree view shows git log output, not a
terminal capture. Label it accordingly.

dashboard: fetch git status for worktrees without agents

The git status fetch only included agent pane paths, so worktrees
without a running agent showed a perpetual spinner in the Git
column. Include worktree paths in the fetch so all worktrees get
their diff stats resolved.

dashboard: show Tab key in agents footer

Replace Commit and Merge shortcuts with Tab Worktrees in the agents
footer bar. This makes the tab switching action discoverable and
matches the worktree footer which already shows Tab Agents. The commit
and merge actions remain accessible via their keybindings.

dashboard: replace x delete with r remove and context-aware modal

Replace the simple x/delete worktree action with r/remove that always
shows a confirmation modal, even for clean worktrees. The modal is
context-aware and shows different states:

- Clean: y to remove, k to toggle keeping the branch
- Unmerged commits: warning shown in dimmed text
- Uncommitted changes: danger-colored warning, requires f to arm
  force mode before y becomes available
- Main worktree: r is a no-op (blocked)

The RemovePlan struct tracks handle, path, dirty/unmerged state,
keep-branch toggle, and force-armed flag. This replaces the previous
pending_delete_worktree which was just an Option<PathBuf> with a
simple y/n confirmation that silently removed clean worktrees without
any confirmation.

The underlying removal still calls workflow::remove which handles
the full lifecycle: kill agent, remove worktree, delete branch, and
clean up tmux window/session.

dashboard: show branch name for main worktree

The main worktree's handle is the repo directory name which is the
same as the project column, making the display redundant (e.g.
"workmux  workmux →main"). Show just the branch name ("main") for
the main worktree since that is what identifies it.

dashboard: add R key for bulk sweep cleanup of worktrees

Adds a sweep modal (R key) in the worktree view that identifies
worktrees ready for cleanup and lets the user bulk-remove them.

Candidates are detected by four signals in priority order:
- PR merged (from GitHub API)
- PR closed (from GitHub API)
- Upstream gone (remote tracking branch deleted)
- Merged locally (no upstream, branch fully merged into base)

The modal shows a selectable list with checkboxes. Non-dirty
candidates are pre-selected. Dirty worktrees appear greyed out
and cannot be selected. Navigation with j/k, Space to toggle,
Enter to remove all selected, Esc to cancel. Shows an empty
state message when no candidates are found.

dashboard: open worktree window on Enter when no agent exists

Previously, pressing Enter on a worktree with no agent pane or existing
mux window did nothing. Now it falls back to workflow::open which
creates the tmux window/session if needed, matching the behavior of
`workmux open <handle>`. The agent pane is still preferred when one
exists for direct pane targeting.

dashboard: add Mux column to worktree table

Shows whether each worktree has an active tmux window/session with a
green dot indicator. Helps identify which worktrees need a window
opened before jumping to them.

dashboard: make sweep (R) available from agents view

The sweep modal operates on worktree data which is independent of the
active tab. Binding R in the agents view too makes it accessible
without switching tabs first. If worktree data hasn't been loaded yet
(user never visited worktree tab), triggers a background fetch
on-demand rather than polling every 5 seconds regardless of tab.

dashboard: improve sweep empty state message

Change "Nothing to sweep." to "No merged or gone worktrees found."
so the user understands what sweep looks for when no candidates
are detected.
release v0.1.145

changelog: add dashboard prefix to v0.1.145 entries

The v0.1.145 changelog entries for worktree view, bulk sweep, kill
agent, and worktree remove were all dashboard features but lacked
a clear scope prefix. Added "dashboard:" to each entry so readers
can immediately tell these are dashboard-specific changes.

dashboard: add Age column to worktree table

Show worktree creation time as a compact relative string (e.g. "2h",
"3d", "1w") using filesystem birthtime. Adds created_at field to
WorktreeInfo populated via std::fs::metadata().created(). Derives
Clone on WorktreeInfo and AgentStatusSummary to support the
all_worktrees baseline pattern used by sorting.

dashboard: add s key to cycle worktree sort mode

Adds sort mode cycling (Natural/Age) to the worktree view with s key.
Natural shows git worktree list order, Age sorts newest first by
directory creation time. Sort mode persists to settings.json.

Uses an all_worktrees baseline (like agents have all_agents) so
apply_worktree_filters always starts from the full unmodified list.
This ensures switching from Age back to Natural instantly restores
the original order instead of keeping the previous sort.

dashboard: fetch PR status per branch instead of bulk

Replace the slow `gh pr list --state all --limit 200` (fetching all
PRs in a repo) with `gh pr list --head <branch> --limit 1` for each
worktree/agent branch. For large repos like epicenter with thousands
of PRs, this is dramatically faster (~1s per branch vs timing out).

Also collects branches from worktrees (via main worktree paths) so
PR status is fetched for projects without running agents. Returns
bool from spawn_pr_status_fetch so the timer only resets when a
fetch actually starts.

dashboard: show PR status in worktree table

Merge PR data from the dashboard's own PR fetching into the worktree
list. Previously, workflow::list was called with fetch_pr_status=false
to avoid spinner corruption, so worktree pr_info was always None.

Now apply_worktree_filters merges pr_statuses into worktrees by
matching branch names. PrStatus events trigger a worktree filter
re-apply so new PR data appears immediately. Worktree fetch runs
at startup so repo roots are available for the first PR fetch.

Also moves the PR column to appear right after Git (before Mux/Age)
for better visual grouping.
dashboard: show R Sweep in worktree footer bar

dashboard: batch PR status lookups with GraphQL

Replace N separate `gh pr list --head <branch>` calls with a single
GitHub GraphQL API query using aliased pullRequests fields. For a
project with 12 worktrees this reduces PR status fetching from 12
process spawns to 1.

The GraphQL function builds one alias per branch, pipes the query
as JSON via stdin to `gh api graphql --input -`, and deserializes
the batched response. Owner/name are passed as GraphQL variables
(not string-interpolated) to avoid injection. Repo context and
GHES hostname are resolved via `gh repo view` so fork conventions
and `gh repo set-default` are respected.

Falls back to per-branch REST calls if GraphQL fails.

dashboard: add close mux window action (c) to worktrees view

Pressing `c` on a worktree row closes its tmux window/session without
removing the git worktree or deleting the branch. Useful for stopping
an agent while keeping the worktree around for later.

The action is a no-op on the main worktree or worktrees without an
active mux window. After closing, triggers a refetch so the Mux column
updates immediately.

dashboard: add project picker to worktree view

Add a 'p' key in the worktree view that opens a project picker modal,
allowing users to switch which project's worktrees are displayed without
leaving the dashboard.

The picker shows all known projects (discovered from cached repo roots),
supports type-to-filter, and highlights the currently active project.
Selecting a project sets an override that scopes the worktree list to
that repo's worktrees only.

Required adding workdir-aware variants of git functions
(list_worktrees_in, get_all_worktree_modes_in, etc.) and a new
workflow::list_in that accepts an optional repo path.

dashboard: split worktree preview into info panel and styled git log

Replace the plain git log preview in the worktree view with a two-panel
layout: an info panel on the left showing worktree metadata, and a
styled git log on the right.

The info panel displays branch name, base branch with ahead/behind
counts, committed and uncommitted diff stats, PR status with CI checks,
agent status, and mux window state. All data comes from already-cached
state so no extra fetches are needed.

The git log uses a structured format (%h, relative date, subject) parsed
and rendered with colored spans instead of plain --oneline output.

dashboard: polish project picker and worktree preview

Resolve repo roots before applying the session scope filter so the
project picker discovers all projects even when session filtering is
active. Add 'p Project' to the worktree footer bar. Remove the brief
"(loading...)" flash from the git log panel.

remove unused list_prs_in_repo function

The GraphQL-based list_prs_for_branches (with REST fallback) fully
replaced the old bulk PR fetching approach. list_prs_in_repo fetched
up to 200 PRs with `gh pr list --state all --limit 200` which was
too slow for large repos. No callers remain.

dashboard: highlight current worktree in worktree table

Apply the same current_worktree_fg highlight used in the agents view
to the worktree table. Compares each worktree path against the
directory the dashboard was launched from, with canonicalized path
comparison to handle symlinks.
release v0.1.146

dashboard: parallelize PR status fetching with priority ordering

PR fetches were sequential across repos, causing slow updates when
multiple projects were configured. Now uses bounded thread pool (max 4
workers) with a shared queue. The current project's repo is fetched
first so its PR data appears sooner.

Also fixes stale PR state: clears pr_statuses when a repo returns no
PRs, and clears all_worktrees on project switch so the PR re-fetch
triggers correctly for the new project.

fix sweep popup showing "---" for dirty worktrees

The sweep modal used "---" as a prefix for dirty (non-selectable) worktree
entries, which looked like a broken placeholder symbol. Replace it with "[ ]"
to be visually consistent with the checkbox used for selectable entries.
The dimmed styling and "(dirty)" label already communicate that these
entries cannot be toggled.

Before: > --- test (merged locally, dirty)
After:  > [ ] test (merged locally, dirty)

dashboard: split app.rs into focused submodules

The 1961-line app.rs monolith was difficult to navigate and maintain.
Split it into an app/ module directory with 8 focused files while
preserving all behavior:

- mod.rs: App struct definition, new(), refresh()
- types.rs: AppEvent, DashboardTab, ViewMode, sweep/picker/remove types
- agents.rs: agent filtering, sorting, navigation, kill, display helpers
- worktrees.rs: worktree tab navigation, removal, sweep, project picker
- appearance.rs: theme cycling, persistence, update_theme_in_config + tests
- background.rs: background thread spawning for git/PR status fetches
- preview.rs: preview pane update, refresh, scrolling, sizing
- events.rs: AppEvent dispatching

Uses inherent impl App blocks in child modules (not extension traits)
since Rust's module visibility lets children access parent-private
fields naturally. This avoids trait import churn in actions.rs and
mod.rs while keeping the same flat access pattern.

dashboard: pre-select current project in project picker

The project picker always started with the cursor at the top of the
list regardless of which project was active. Now it finds the current
project's position in the sorted list and sets the initial cursor
there, so the user immediately sees which project they're on.

dashboard: add open PR in browser action

Add `o` keybinding in both Agents and Worktrees views to open the
associated pull request in the default browser.

- Add `url` field to PrSummary, fetched via GraphQL and REST queries
- Use platform-appropriate browser opener (open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux)
- Show status message in footer when no PR exists or URL isn't loaded yet
- Report spawn errors instead of silently swallowing them
- Add transient status_message field to App with 3-second auto-clear
release v0.1.147

patch crossterm to fix mouse coordinate overflow panic

crossterm 0.29.0 panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in
parse_csi_sgr_mouse when a terminal sends mouse coordinate 0. This
started happening after updating to tmux 3.6a.

Patches crossterm via a fork that uses saturating_sub(1) instead of
plain subtraction for mouse coordinates, preventing the u16 underflow.

See: crossterm-rs/crossterm#590
docs: clarify rust target directory caveat

dashboard: add open PR checks in browser action

When PR checks fail, you often want to open the checks page to see why.
Add `O` (shift-o) keybinding to open {pr_url}/checks in the browser,
complementing the existing `o` to open the PR itself.

Refactored open_pr_for_selected into a shared open_pr_url helper that
accepts a URL transformer, avoiding duplication between the two actions.
Available in both agents and worktrees views.

use live tmux pane title during agent reconciliation

The reconciliation code already prefers live session and window names
over stale stored values, but was ignoring the live pane title. Claude
Code dynamically updates pane titles with task descriptions, so the

Apply the same prefer-live-fall-back-to-stored pattern for pane_title:

dashboard: add base branch picker to worktree tab

Press `b` in the worktree tab to open a filterable modal picker that

the top and highlighted.

Implementation details:
- New git helpers: `list_local_branches_in(workdir)` and
  `set_branch_base_in(branch, base, workdir)` for worktree-scoped ops
- `BaseBranchPicker` modal follows the same pattern as `ProjectPicker`
- `base_branch` field added to `WorktreeInfo`, populated from git config
- On confirm, both `WorktreeInfo` and `GitStatus` caches are updated
  immediately so the UI reflects the change without waiting for the
  background refresh cycle
- Guards against main worktree, detached HEAD, and branch-list failures

dashboard: make base branch picker work from agents tab too

The `b` shortcut now opens the base branch picker from both the agents
and worktrees tabs. In agents view, the branch is resolved from the
selected agent's working directory via git.

Also fixes the picker popup to use a fixed height (based on total branch
count, up to 15) with a scrolling window, so the UI doesn't shift as
the filter narrows results.

Display PR check elapsed time and failing check details across all

Add an AGE column to the list command showing how old each worktree is

add --continue flag to workmux open

When passed, injects the appropriate "continue last conversation" flag
for the configured agent CLI:

- gemini, kiro: --resume

release v0.1.150

dashboard: fix immediate exit on startup from stray Enter key

When launching `workmux dashboard` from the shell, the Enter keypress
used to execute the command could linger in the terminal input buffer.
The input thread would consume this stray Enter before the user saw
anything, triggering JumpToSelected on the auto-selected first agent
and immediately switching tmux to that agent's window.

Fix by reordering startup: create App state and apply CLI overrides
before spawning the input thread, then drain any buffered terminal
events with a non-blocking poll loop. This ensures stray keypresses
from the shell launch are discarded before the TUI starts processing
input.
release v0.1.151

show animated spinner for pending PR checks

Replace the static pending check icon with an animated braille spinner
that cycles on each dashboard tick (250ms). This gives clear visual
feedback that CI checks are still running.

- Use existing spinner_frame counter from App state for the animation
- Pass spinner_frame through format_pr_status and format_pr_details
- Apply spinner in all three locations: agent table, worktree table,
  and worktree info panel
- Remove unused pending field from CheckIcons since it's replaced by
  the spinner
- Use palette.accent instead of palette.warning for pending color

tests: use adaptive polling in poll_until()

Replace fixed 0.1s polling interval with adaptive backoff schedule
[0.0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1]. This checks the condition immediately
on the first call (0.0s), then ramps up the interval. Most poll_until
calls resolve quickly (file exists, pane has output), so the immediate
check and fast initial intervals avoid unnecessary waiting.

Also switches from time.time() to time.monotonic() for more reliable
timeout tracking.

The poll_interval parameter is kept for API compatibility but the
adaptive schedule is always used.

Baseline: 97.95s -> 97.63s (modest, main gains expected from sleep removal)

replace time.sleep() with deterministic readiness checks

Replace all fixed time.sleep(1.5) and time.sleep(0.5) calls in test
files with polling-based readiness checks. This eliminates arbitrary
waits that are either too long (wasting time) or too short (causing
flakes under load).

Add wait_for_window_ready() helper to conftest.py that polls until a
tmux window exists and has visible pane content, replacing the pattern
of sleeping 1.5s after run_workmux_add().

Specific replacements:
- 16x time.sleep(1.5) after run_workmux_add -> wait_for_window_ready()
- 1x time.sleep(0.5) after echo -> wait_for_pane_output()
- 1x time.sleep(0.5) between status updates -> removed (redundant)
- 1x time.sleep(DEFERRED_SCRIPT_WAIT) -> poll_until(worktree removed)

Files changed: test_agent_state, test_workmux_capture, test_workmux_run,
test_workmux_send, test_workmux_status, test_workmux_wait,
test_session_navigation, conftest

cache template git repo across test session

Create a session-scoped template git repository that is initialized once
and copied per test, replacing 5 git subprocess calls (init, config x2,
add, commit) with a fast filesystem copy.

The git config (user.name, user.email) is stored in .git/config and
survives the shutil.copytree, so copied repos work identically to
freshly initialized ones.

fix flaky agent tests with absolute paths and increased timeouts

Two integration tests (test_add_with_agent_flag_overrides_default and
test_global_agent_starts_in_default_pane) intermittently failed because
the fake agent's output file wasn't created within the 5s timeout.

The handshake mechanism signals readiness before exec'ing the login
shell, so agent commands are sent while the shell may still be
initializing. On macOS, /etc/zprofile runs path_helper which reorders
PATH, and the shell initialization timing is variable under load.

Fix by using absolute paths for both agent commands and output files,
removing dependencies on PATH resolution and working directory. Also
increase timeouts from 5s to 10s for these tests to handle slow shell
initialization under parallel test load.

suppress noisy success output from just check

Quiet the check pipeline so it only prints meaningful output:
- Add @ prefix to suppress recipe echoing for fmt, ruff, clippy
- Add --quiet to clippy and ruff check to suppress progress/success lines
- Buffer unit-tests output, only show summary line (full output on failure)
- Buffer pyright output, filter "0 errors" success line (full output on failure)
- Remove "All docs have descriptions" echo from docs-check

On success, `just check` now produces a single line (test summary)
instead of 28+ lines of progress noise.

merge clippy-fix and clippy into single pass

The rust pipeline previously ran clippy twice: once with --fix to
auto-fix warnings, then again with -D to fail on remaining warnings.
This is redundant since a single invocation with both --fix and -D
will fix what it can and fail on the rest, eliminating a full
duplicate build/lint cycle.

dashboard: add 'a' hotkey to create worktree in worktrees view

Add an "a" hotkey in the worktrees tab that opens a two-phase modal:
1. Name input for the new worktree/branch name
2. Optional base branch picker (Esc to skip, Enter to select)

The worktree is created via workflow::create in a background thread,

Follows existing modal patterns (project picker, base branch picker)

dashboard: refactor add-worktree to unified fzf-style picker

Replace the two-step flow (name input -> base branch picker) with a

- Cursor 0 shows "Create <query>" when filter is non-empty

dashboard: add tab completion cycling in add-worktree picker

Tab fills the first matching branch into the input. Subsequent Tab

Arrow keys (not j/k) handle navigation in the picker so all

dashboard: exclude occupied branches from add-worktree picker

Branches that already have worktrees are filtered out of the picker

dashboard: sort occupied branches last and make them unselectable

Occupied branches (already have worktrees) are shown at the bottom

dashboard: replace base branch step with inline Ctrl+b toggle

Remove the separate BaseBranch phase from add-worktree flow. Instead,
