dashboard: add emacs keybindings to add-worktree inputs

Add Ctrl+w (delete word) and Ctrl+u (clear line) to both the main
filter input and the base branch input. Word boundaries split on
slash, dash, and whitespace to match branch name conventions.

dashboard: use prefix matching for tab completion

Tab completion now uses starts_with instead of contains, matching
shell-like behavior. Typing "work" + Tab completes to "workmux-run"
instead of "add-worktree" which only had "work" as a substring.

Removes the now-unused base_filtered() method since both tab
completions compute prefix matches inline.

dashboard: show add worktree hotkey in footer bar

Add "a Add" to the worktrees view footer alongside the other
hotkey indicators.

dashboard: use fixed-size modals with base branch on border

Replace dynamic modal sizing with a fixed height based on terminal
size (~40% height, clamped 10-25 rows). Prevents distracting layout
shifts while typing.

Move the base branch indicator to the bottom border of the add
worktree modal for cleaner visual separation. Ensure consistent
blank line between footer and bottom border.

Apply the same fixed sizing to the base branch picker modal.

dashboard: dim background behind modal overlays

Add a dimming effect to the entire buffer when any modal is open
(help, pickers, confirmations, add worktree). Fades the background
content to draw visual focus to the popup.

dashboard: reorder worktrees footer to match agents view

Group actions first (Add, Remove, Sweep, Close, PR), then navigation
and view controls (Jump, Sort, Project), then Tab switch and Quit.
Only show filter when active to save space.

dashboard: add PR checkout to add-worktree modal

Two ways to checkout a PR from the add-worktree popup:

1. Smart detection: type a PR number (e.g. "123" or "#123") and the
   "Create" row changes to "Checkout PR #123". Enter triggers checkout.

2. PR list mode: Ctrl+p toggles to a filterable list of open PRs
   fetched async from GitHub. Filter by title, branch, number, or
   author. Enter checks out the selected PR.

PR checkout uses get_pr_details directly instead of resolve_pr_ref
to avoid stdout/spinner output that would corrupt the TUI. Fork PRs
are handled by setting up the remote quietly in the background thread.

The modal title changes to "Checkout PR" in PR mode, base branch
editing is hidden (PRs ignore base), and the footer updates to show
mode-appropriate keybindings.

dashboard: use fuzzy subsequence matching in add-worktree picker

Replace substring matching with fuzzy subsequence matching so that
typing "mergefail" matches "merge-fail-delete" (each character must
appear in order in the target). Applied to branch filter, PR filter,
and tab completion.

dashboard: add contextual hints to add-worktree modal

Show a dimmed hint line above the footer describing the current
action: "New branch from main" when creating, or "Worktree for
existing branch 'name'" when selecting an existing branch.

add workmux resurrect command with crash-safe reconciliation

Adds a new `resurrect` command that restores worktree windows after a
tmux or computer crash. Uses persisted agent state files to detect which
worktrees had active agents before the crash.

Key implementation details:

- Reads raw (non-reconciled) agent state files and matches workdir to
  git worktrees using canonical descendant path matching
- Calls workflow::open directly with focus_window=false (no focus stealing)
  and continue_session=true (resumes agent conversations)
- Partial failure handling: continues on error, reports all results
- Repo-scoped: only considers worktrees in the current git repo

Crash-safe reconciliation via per-state boot IDs:

- Adds server_boot_id() to Multiplexer trait (tmux: #{start_time})
- Each AgentState now stores the server's boot_id when written
- Reconciliation skips deletion when boot_id doesn't match current
  server, preserving state files for resurrect to use
- Legacy state files without boot_id get deleted as before
- Eliminates the need to run resurrect before list/dashboard

Also fixes workflow::open to respect focus_window option on the
existing-target fast path (previously called target.select()
unconditionally).

resurrect: add tracing for plan and execution phases

Logs each agent state file processed (pane_id, workdir, boot_id,
status), the action determined per handle (restore/skip and why),
and the outcome of each restoration attempt. Enables debugging
with RUST_LOG=workmux=info when resurrect doesn't work as expected.

cli: group commands by category in help output

The flat list of 20+ commands was overwhelming for new users.
Replace the default clap-generated command list with a custom
help_template that organizes commands into logical groups:

- Worktree lifecycle (add, remove, merge, open, close, resurrect)
- Monitoring (dashboard, list, path, status)
- Setup and configuration (init, setup, config, sandbox, sync-files, claude)
- Agent interaction (send, capture, wait, run)
- Help and updates (docs, changelog, update, completions)

Clap doesn't support multi-heading subcommand groups natively,
so this uses a manual help_template. The tradeoff is that command
descriptions are duplicated between doc comments and the template,
but the list rarely changes and the UX improvement is significant.
release v0.1.152

docs: add multiple Claude configurations section

Document how to use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with direnv to maintain
separate work/personal Claude configurations. Also covers the
wrapper script approach using .direnv/bin/claude for full control
over per-project Claude launch behavior. Added in response to
PR #95 discussion about managing multiple agent profiles.

reduce log spam for preserved resurrect agents

The "preserving agent from previous server lifecycle" message logged at
info level on every reconcile tick for each stale agent, causing massive
log spam. Downgrade to debug since this is expected recurring state that
persists until `workmux resurrect` is run.

show spinner on PR column header while fetching

When PR statuses are being refreshed in the background, the PR column
header now shows a braille spinner animation, matching the existing
Git column behavior. This gives users a visual indicator that PR data
is being updated.

use static pending icon instead of spinner in info panel PR line

The info panel was showing two spinners for pending checks: one on the
PR line and another on the detail line below with elapsed time. Added a
dedicated pending icon to CheckIcons (nerdfont: timer_sand, fallback:
◷) and use it on the PR line, keeping the animated spinner only on the
detail line where it shows elapsed time.

fix nix build: add outputHashes for crossterm git dependency

The nix build was failing because flake.nix didn't include outputHashes
for the git dependency crossterm-0.29.0 (from raine/crossterm fork).
Nix requires explicit hashes for git dependencies when using cargoLock.

Adds the SRI hash for crossterm-0.29.0 at commit f99eeae4.

add `r` hotkey to remove worktree from agents tab

The `r` key previously only worked in the worktrees tab. Now it also
works in the agents tab by finding the worktree matching the selected
agent's path and triggering the same removal flow (confirmation modal,
dirty check, force arm). If no matching worktree is found (e.g. orphaned
agent), the key press is silently ignored.

Also adds the key to the agents tab help overlay.

fix incorrect guest home directory with Lima 2.1.0

Lima 2.1.0 changed the guest home directory from
/home/<user>.linux to /home/<user>.guest. workmux had
the .linux suffix hardcoded, so mounts targeted the wrong
path and Claude couldn't find .claude.json.

Detect the installed Lima version via `limactl --version`
and use .guest for >=2.1.0, .linux for older versions.
Falls back to .linux if limactl isn't available.

Existing VMs need to be recreated for the fix to take effect.

release v0.1.153

add Codex status tracking support

Codex hooks API supports the same event structure as Claude Code,
enabling working/done status tracking via UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse,
and Stop hooks. No waiting state is possible since Codex has no
permission prompt event.

The setup command detects ~/.codex/, merges hooks into
~/.codex/hooks.json (with deduplication), and auto-enables the
codex_hooks feature flag in ~/.codex/config.toml. If the flag was
already set to false, it gets replaced rather than duplicated.

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2109
release v0.1.154

include .codex/hooks in cargo package

The Codex hooks config is embedded at compile time via include_str!
and needs to be in the published crate tarball.
release v0.1.155

include waiting agents in last-done navigation

The last-done command now considers both "done" and "waiting" agents,
navigating to whichever was most recently updated. This lets users
quickly jump to agents that need their input, not just ones that
have finished. Repeated invocations cycle through all matching agents
in reverse chronological order as before.

fix PR status fetch delayed 30s on dashboard open

spawn_pr_status_fetch() iterated self.agents to collect branches, but
on the first call to refresh(), self.agents was still empty because
apply_filters() (which populates it from all_agents) runs at the end
of refresh(). The fetch found no branches, returned true (resetting
the 30-second timer), and the real first fetch was delayed by a full
interval.

Two fixes:
- Iterate self.all_agents instead of self.agents so branches are
  collected before apply_filters() has run. The name/stale UI filters
  should not affect which PRs get fetched.
- Return false when repo_branches is empty so the caller does not
  reset the timer. This allows retry on the next 2-second tick once
  git statuses or worktree data arrive from their background threads.

use configured main_branch for dashboard diff base detection

When main_branch is set in .workmux.yaml, the dashboard now uses it as
the preferred fallback for diff base detection instead of auto-detecting
via refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. This fixes spurious diffs on the main
worktree when the configured main_branch differs from the remote's
default branch (e.g. using dev/latest instead of main).

The fallback chain is now: per-branch workmux-base > configured
main_branch > auto-detected default branch > "main". The same fix
applies to both git status calculation and the diff modal's base branch
resolution. Empty main_branch values are treated as unset.

release v0.1.156
reorder supported agents in status tables

improve last-done sort stability and add debug tracing

The sort by status_ts had no tiebreaker, causing non-deterministic
ordering when multiple agents changed status in the same second.
This could make the cycling behavior inconsistent across invocations.

Changes:
- Use sort_by_key with (status_ts, updated_ts, pane_id) tuple for
  deterministic descending order
- Extract sort and pick_target into testable functions
- Add debug tracing for active pane, cycle position, and each
  switch attempt to aid diagnosis
- Add unit tests for sort ordering, tiebreaker behavior, None
  handling, mixed status types, and cycling logic

fix last-done navigating to wrong agent

The stateless cycling logic couldn't distinguish "I'm on this done agent
because my agent finished here" from "I'm on this done agent because
last-done brought me here." If you were already sitting on a done agent,
pressing last-done would skip the most recent one and cycle to the next.

Fix by persisting cycle state in settings.json: store which pane
last-done navigated to and the status_ts of the list head when the
cycle started. A cycle continues only when the current pane matches the
saved target AND no new agent has finished (head_ts unchanged).
Otherwise the cycle resets to index 0 (most recent done agent).

add last-done command reference doc

Document the last-done command which switches to the most recently
completed or waiting agent, with cycle behavior on repeated
invocations. Add entry to the commands index page and sidebar
navigation.
release v0.1.157
update picomatch to 4.0.4 in docs/package-lock.json

add sidebar command for compact agent status view

Add a lightweight sidebar TUI that shows agent status in a narrow tmux
pane, toggled via workmux sidebar. Uses the same agent state and theme
system as the dashboard but in a compact always-visible format.

Features:
- Left-side tmux split with configurable width
- Live status icons with spinner animation
- j/k navigation, Enter to jump to agent
- Auto-refresh every 2 seconds
- Toggle on/off with the same command
- Per-window (tagged via @workmux_role pane option)

sidebar: show all agents globally across all windows

Previously the sidebar was per-window and session-scoped. Now it creates
a sidebar pane in every existing tmux window when enabled, and uses an
after-new-window hook to auto-create in new windows. Toggle off kills
all sidebar panes and removes the hook.

Changes:
- Toggle stores @workmux_sidebar_enabled and @workmux_sidebar_width as
  tmux global options for state tracking
- Create sidebars in all windows on enable, kill all on disable
- Install after-new-window hook with _sidebar-sync command
- Remove session filter so all agents from all projects are shown
- Display names as project/worktree (e.g. "myproject/fix-bug") instead
  of just the worktree name, using shared extract_project_name helper
- Remove layout save/restore (let tmux reflow naturally)

sidebar: improve toggle behavior and pane management

- Save and restore window layouts when creating/killing sidebars to
  prevent progressive pane shrinking on repeated toggle
- Fix toggle not working on first try after manually killing sidebar
  by checking if any sidebar panes actually exist
- Use numeric hook index [99] for tmux 3.4+ compatibility (named
  hook indices cause "ambiguous option" on some hook names)
- Auto-quit sidebar when it becomes the last pane in a window
- Add Ctrl-C as quit shortcut

sidebar: fix icon alignment and spinner animation

- Pad all status icons to a fixed 2-column width so emoji (2 cols)
  and braille spinners (1 col) align consistently
- Replace single-char braille spinner with 2-char orbiting dot
  animation across a 4x4 braille grid
- Remove bold from list selection highlight style

sidebar: highlight active window and sort by recency

- Detect the currently active tmux window and bold-highlight agents
  belonging to it, updating every 250ms on tick
- Sort agents by recency (most recent status change first) instead
  of priority, which is more useful for a compact status view

sidebar: add after-new-session hook for new sessions

The after-new-window hook only fires for windows within existing
sessions. New sessions need their own hook to get a sidebar pane
automatically.

sidebar: fix sync targeting wrong window for new windows

The after-new-window hook fires in the context of the new window, but
_sidebar-sync was checking the client's current (old) window for an
existing sidebar. Since the old window already had one, it did nothing.

Now the hook passes #{window_id} as an argument so sync targets the
correct window. Also refactored create/find functions to accept an
explicit window ID, and simplified create_sidebars_in_all_windows to
reuse create_sidebar_in_window.

sidebar: match active highlight on session and window name

Previously only matched on window_name, causing agents in different
sessions with the same window name to all highlight. Now matches on
both session_name and window_name.

sidebar: fix toggle requiring double-run after manual close

Toggle now checks the current window instead of global state to decide
intent. If the current window has a sidebar, toggle OFF globally. If
not, enable/repair globally (idempotent, skips windows that already
have one). Removes the any_sidebar_panes_exist check that caused the
double-run issue when some windows still had sidebars.

sidebar: auto-select active window agent on window switch

Move the list selection to match the currently active window, but only
when the active window actually changes. This prevents the 250ms tick
from overriding j/k navigation within the same window.

sidebar: add tile layout mode with status stripe

Add an alternative tile/card layout for the sidebar toggled with 'v'.
Each tile shows the worktree name with status icon and elapsed time on
the first line, project name on the second, and an optional pane title
(task description from Claude) on the third when available.

Tiles use a colored left stripe (info/accent/success) to indicate agent
status and horizontal separators between items. The layout mode is
persisted to a tmux global option so all sidebar instances stay in sync.

Also extracts shared status_icon_and_style helper, removes the redundant
right border (tmux pane border suffices), and adds ellipsis-aware
truncation for tile content.

sidebar: add bottom separator after last tile

Without this the last tile had no bottom border, looking incomplete
compared to the separators between other tiles.

sidebar: show "main" for main worktrees and disambiguate multi-pane windows

Previously, main worktrees showed the project name as the worktree
name in both compact and tile views, making it look like
"workmux / workmux". Now shows "main" instead.

When multiple agents share the same tmux window (multi-pane), append
numbered suffixes like "main [1]", "main [2]" matching the dashboard's
existing behavior.

sidebar: quit all sidebar panes globally when any instance exits

Previously quitting the sidebar in one window only closed that single
pane. Now pressing q/Esc/Ctrl-C kills all sidebar panes across every
window and session, restores saved layouts, removes tmux hooks, and
unsets global options. The quitting pane's layout restore is deferred
via a background run-shell so it fires after the process exits.

sidebar: use fixed tile height even when title is unavailable

Tiles without a pane title were shorter than those with one, causing
uneven visual rhythm. Now an empty third line is rendered when no
title is available so all tiles have consistent height.

sidebar: make width responsive to terminal size

Replace the fixed 30-column default with a dynamic width computed as
10% of terminal width, clamped between 25 and 50 columns. A
client-resized tmux hook recomputes and applies the width whenever the
terminal resizes (e.g. switching between internal and external
monitors). Explicit --width override still works.

sidebar: show MM:SS timer for agents under one hour

Replace the compact "5m", "30s" format with a MM:SS countdown-style
timer (e.g. "05:30", "00:12") for agents less than one hour old.
Agents older than one hour still show "4h", "2d" etc.

sidebar: use normal text color for elapsed time on non-stale agents

The elapsed time was rendered in dimmed color for all agents. Now
non-stale agents use the regular text color for better readability,
while stale agents remain dimmed. Applies to both compact and tile
views.

sidebar: clear done/waiting status using tmux window option as source of truth

The done checkmark was blinking in the sidebar because refresh()
reloaded status from StateStore every 2 seconds, overwriting the
in-memory clear. Instead of writing state, the sidebar now observes
tmux's @workmux_status window option which is already auto-cleared
by a pane-focus-in hook when the user switches windows. On each
refresh, agents with Done or Waiting status are suppressed if the
tmux option no longer matches the expected icon.

sidebar: replace per-pane polling with daemon + Unix socket architecture

Replace N independent sidebar processes each polling tmux every 2s with a
single daemon process that pushes state snapshots to render-only clients
via Unix domain socket. This eliminates redundant tmux queries and enables
instant window-switch response through SIGUSR1 dirty-signal hooks.

Architecture:
- daemon.rs: headless process that runs one batched tmux query, builds a
  SidebarSnapshot, and broadcasts to all connected clients via
  length-prefixed JSON over Unix socket. Uses signal-hook for SIGTERM
  (clean shutdown) and SIGUSR1 (immediate refresh on window/session changes).
  Falls back to 2s polling interval for non-hook changes (status transitions).
- snapshot.rs: SidebarSnapshot and SnapshotAgent data types plus a pure
  build_snapshot() function extracted from the old SidebarApp::refresh().
- client.rs: SnapshotReceiver with background reader thread, exponential
  backoff reconnect, and Arc<Mutex<Option>> latest-snapshot handoff.
- app.rs: SidebarApp becomes a render-only client. new_client() constructor
  does config + host detection only (no tmux polling). apply_snapshot()
  replaces refresh()/update_active_window()/sync_layout_mode(). Adds
  FollowHost/Manual selection mode and stable window_id for active-window
  detection.
- mod.rs: Main loop uses 50ms tick with socket receiver instead of 2s
  polling. ensure_daemon_running() called from toggle(), sync(), and
  run_sidebar() for crash/auto-exit recovery. SIGUSR1 dirty-signal hooks
  at priority [98] for after-select-window, client-session-changed,
  after-kill-pane, after-kill-window.

Safety:
- Socket bound with 0600 permissions to prevent other local users from
  reading snapshot data (paths, pane titles, session metadata).
- broadcast() uses append-based merge to avoid dropping clients that
  connect during a write cycle.
- ensure_daemon_running() uses socket-connect as health check (not kill -0)
  to avoid PID recycling issues, and cleans stale sockets before respawn.
- Daemon auto-exits after 10s with no clients as a safety net.

sidebar: remove invalid after-kill-window tmux hook

after-kill-window is not a valid tmux hook name. Removing it from both
install_hooks() and remove_hooks(). The after-kill-pane hook already
covers window destruction since killing a window kills all its panes.

sidebar: use window_id for host agent matching instead of session+name

Selection and is_active styling now match on the stable tmux window_id
(e.g. @42) from snapshot data instead of session_name + window_name
string comparison. This is computed once per snapshot as host_agent_idx
and used by both sync_selection() and the UI rendering.

The window_id is assigned by tmux and never changes for the lifetime of
a window, making the match immune to any session/window name format
differences between detect_host_window() and the agent state store.

sidebar: reduce snapshot delivery latency on window switch

Move snapshot application before terminal draw in the client loop so
the first render after receiving a snapshot shows current state instead
of stale data from the previous frame.

Skip the daemon's 50ms sleep after processing a dirty signal so
back-to-back signals are handled immediately. Rust's thread::sleep
retries on EINTR, so SIGUSR1 cannot interrupt it mid-sleep, but
skipping the post-processing sleep avoids adding unnecessary delay
between consecutive updates.

sidebar: reduce highlight switch latency to ~30ms

Reduce daemon and client poll intervals from 50ms to 10ms, cutting
worst-case wakeup jitter from ~100ms combined to ~20ms. The hot path
is an atomic bool load and a sleep syscall, so 100 wakeups/sec has
negligible CPU impact.

Signal the daemon directly from jump_to_selected() via SIGUSR1,
bypassing the tmux hook round-trip (hook dispatch + shell spawn +
tmux option read + kill). This makes sidebar-initiated Enter jumps
feel near-instant since the daemon gets the signal before the tmux
hook even fires.

sidebar: eliminate "No agents" flash on startup

Signal the daemon immediately after the client connects to the socket,
triggering an instant snapshot broadcast. Previously the client had to
wait up to 2s for the daemon's fallback timer to expire before
receiving its first snapshot.

Also moved signal_daemon() to mod.rs so it can be shared between the
startup path and jump_to_selected() in app.rs.

sidebar: fix resize hook error message flashing in tmux status line

The client-resized[99] hook ran a shell script that piped tmux
list-panes through a while loop testing each pane's @workmux_role.
When the last pane processed was not a sidebar pane, the [ "$role" =
"sidebar" ] test exited non-zero, which became the script's exit
status. tmux displays non-zero run-shell results in the status line,
causing the full script text to flash briefly on every terminal resize.

Fix by appending "; true" to ensure the script always exits 0.

sidebar: fix tmux format expansion in resize hook script

Tmux hooks expand #{...} format sequences in the hook value before
passing it to the shell. The client-resized resize script contained
#{pane_id}, #{@workmux_role}, and #{client_width} which were being
expanded by tmux's hook processor instead of being passed as literal
format strings to the nested tmux commands (list-panes -F,
display-message -p).

This meant list-panes -F received the active pane's literal ID instead
of a format template, so the while loop never matched any sidebar
panes. Sidebar resize on terminal resize has been silently broken.

Fix by doubling the # (## in tmux produces a literal #). In Rust
format strings: ##{{x}} -> ##{x} after Rust fmt -> #{x} after tmux
hook expansion, which is then correctly interpreted by the nested
tmux commands.

sidebar: force exact width with resize-pane after split

split-window -l can produce inexact widths depending on the existing
window layout geometry. Some windows ended up with very narrow sidebar
panes after re-toggling.

Add an explicit resize-pane -x after creating each sidebar pane to
guarantee the target width is applied regardless of tmux's split
behavior.

sidebar: compute width per-window instead of per-client

default_width() used #{client_width} from the calling client's
terminal, then applied that single width to all windows across all
sessions. Sessions attached to terminals of different sizes got
sidebars that were too wide or too narrow proportionally.

Now each window gets its sidebar width computed from #{window_width}
via width_for_window(), both in create_sidebars_in_all_windows() and
in sync() for hook-created windows. This ensures every sidebar is
~10% of its own window's width regardless of which client triggered
the toggle.

Removed the unused sidebar_width() function and @workmux_sidebar_width
global option dependency for width calculation (the option is still
set for the resize hook).

sidebar: clear stale saved layouts before computing sidebar widths

When toggling sidebar ON, stale @workmux_sidebar_layout window options
from previous toggle cycles could contain dimensions from a different
terminal size (e.g. 332x70 vs current 373x79). During toggle OFF,
restore_window_layout applies these old layouts, which can briefly
resize the window to the stale dimensions. If toggle ON then queries
#{window_width} during this transition, it gets the wrong width,
producing incorrectly sized sidebars in some windows.

Fix by clearing all @workmux_sidebar_layout options before querying
window widths in create_sidebars_in_all_windows. This ensures
#{window_width} always reflects the actual current window size.

sidebar: add debug logging for width computation and pane creation

Log window_width, computed sidebar_width, and actual post-resize pane
width for each sidebar creation. This makes it possible to diagnose
width mismatches by running with RUST_LOG=workmux=debug.

Logs cover: width_for_window computation, create_sidebar_in_window
entry/skip/completion, and the stale layout clearing pass.

sidebar: use client width for all sidebars, not per-window width

With window-size=latest, unattached sessions keep their last-seen
client's window dimensions. When create_sidebars_in_all_windows
queried #{window_width} per-window, sessions like claude-history
(last seen on a 332-wide terminal) got sidebars sized for 332 while
the active terminal was 373. Logs confirmed window_width=332 for @30
while all other windows reported 373.

Revert to using the current client's width (#{client_width}) for all
sidebars across all sessions. All sessions will ultimately be viewed
through the same terminal, and the resize hook adjusts sidebar width
when the terminal is resized. Removed the unused width_for_window
function.

sidebar: use window-resized hook instead of client-resized for width snapping

client-resized only fires when the terminal emulator is resized. It
does not fire when tmux resizes windows due to session switching with
window-size=latest. This caused sidebars created in unattached sessions
(with stale smaller window sizes) to get proportionally expanded when
the user later switched to that session, making them too wide.

window-resized fires whenever any window's geometry changes, including
both terminal resizes and session-switch-triggered resizes. The hook
script is now scoped to the specific window that resized (using
#{window_id}) and computes the target width from #{window_width}
rather than #{client_width}, so each window gets its own correct
proportional sidebar width.

Also cleans up the legacy client-resized[99] hook during remove_hooks
in case it was installed by a previous version.
sidebar: show sleep emoji for stale agents

sidebar: harden client and daemon against CPU spike storms

All 12 sidebar-run processes simultaneously hit 22% CPU from event
storms. Four failure modes identified and fixed:

1. Client event loop: non-key events (Resize, FocusGained) used
   `continue` which skipped tick/sleep bookkeeping, making the loop
   unthrottled during event storms. Fix: restructure to match on all
   event types without early continue, and add a `needs_render` flag
   so terminal.draw() only runs when state actually changed (snapshot
   received, key pressed, resize, or spinner tick).

2. Daemon dirty loop: skipped sleep entirely when dirty flag was set,
   so a SIGUSR1 flood caused unbounded rebuild/broadcast cycles. Fix:
   replace with `dirty_pending` bit serviced at most once per 50ms
   debounce interval. Always sleep 10ms regardless of dirty state.

3. Resize hook storm: window-resized hook called resize-pane which
   could retrigger window-resized. Fix: check #{pane_width} against
   target before calling resize-pane (idempotent, breaks the loop).

4. Reconnect churn: if daemon accepted then immediately closed, all
   clients reset backoff to 50ms and reconnected in lockstep. Fix:
   only reset backoff if connection lasted >5s, and add PID-based
   jitter (pid % 100 ms) to prevent phase-locking across clients.

sidebar: add agent navigation hotkeys (next/prev/jump)

Add `workmux sidebar next/prev/jump N` subcommands that let users switch
between agents in sidebar order via tmux keybindings. The daemon writes
the ordered agent list to a tmux global option (@workmux_sidebar_agents)
with caching to avoid redundant tmux calls. The navigate function reads
this list, finds the current window, computes the target using wrapping
arithmetic, and calls switch-client.

- SidebarAction enum with Next, Prev, Jump variants (jump validates >= 1
  via clap value_parser)
- Pure compute_nav_target() helper extracted for unit testing (12 tests)
- Agent list cleared in all shutdown paths (toggle off, shutdown_all,
  daemon cleanup)
- Docs updated with navigation commands section and example tmux
  keybindings, fixed stale architecture description

sidebar: fix navigation matching for same-window agents

Match by pane_id instead of window_id when finding the current agent
position. When multiple agents share a window, window_id matching always
found the first one, making next/prev cycle incorrectly.

sidebar: fix highlight for same-window agents using active pane tracking

The sidebar highlight always selected the first agent when multiple
agents shared a window, because host_agent_idx matched by window_id
alone. Now the daemon includes active_pane_ids in each snapshot
(queried via #{pane_active}), and the sidebar disambiguates by
preferring the active pane among candidates in the same window.

sidebar: add tmux check to navigate function

The navigate() function for sidebar agent hotkeys (next/prev/jump)
was missing the TMUX environment variable check that toggle() already
had. Without this, running navigation commands outside tmux would
produce confusing errors from tmux CLI calls instead of a clear
"Sidebar requires tmux" message.

dashboard: add sidebar tip to tab header

Show a subtle "New: workmux sidebar" tip in the dashboard tab header
(right-aligned) to promote the sidebar feature to tmux users who haven't
tried it yet.

The tip displays when all conditions are met:
- User is inside tmux (TMUX env var set)
- User hasn't used `workmux sidebar` before
- Dashboard has been opened fewer than 5 times since tip became eligible

Persistent state stored in ~/.local/state/workmux/tips.json tracks view
count and whether sidebar has been used. The sidebar toggle marks the
feature as used (fire-and-forget) so the tip disappears permanently.

Tip check runs once at dashboard startup (not every render). All file
I/O errors are silently ignored since tip display is non-critical.

dashboard: disable sidebar tip until ready for promotion

Add early return to should_show_sidebar_tip() so the tip system is
compiled and tested but not visible to users yet. Remove the guard
when sidebar is ready for wider promotion.

sidebar: make tiles default layout and persist preference

The tiles layout is now the default for new users. Layout preference
is persisted to settings.json so it survives tmux restarts. The daemon
reads the tmux global first for instant in-session sync, then falls
back to the persisted setting.

Previously the layout choice was only stored as a tmux global option,
which meant it reset every time tmux was restarted.

cli: add sidebar to --help output

The sidebar command was missing from the hardcoded help template,
making it invisible to users running `workmux --help`. Added it
to the Monitoring section alongside dashboard.

sidebar: remove --width argument

The sidebar width is now always auto-computed as ~10% of terminal
width (clamped 25-50 cols). The --width flag was rarely useful and
added unnecessary complexity. Removing it simplifies the CLI surface.

docs: add sidebar guide page

Adds a dedicated documentation page for the sidebar feature under
the Dashboard section. Covers setup, keybindings, layout modes,
agent navigation hotkeys, and how it works. Also adds sidebar to
the command reference nav and includes a "New" badge in the sidebar
navigation.

sidebar: use braille wave spinner

Replace the perimeter worm spinner with a smoother braille wave pattern.
Each frame carries a phase-offset rotation that creates a fluid cascading
effect. Also reduces from 12 to 10 frames, matching the spinner_frame
wrap value so all frames are reachable.

extract shared utilities from dashboard for sidebar independence

Move ThemePalette and agent display helpers (extract_project_name,
extract_worktree_name) out of the dashboard module into shared
top-level modules. This breaks the sidebar's dependency on
crate::command::dashboard, which was an architectural smell: the
sidebar shouldn't need to import from a sibling command module for
generic utilities.

- ThemePalette moves to src/ui/theme.rs (new shared ui module)
- Agent name extraction moves to src/agent_display.rs
- Dashboard re-exports both for backwards compatibility
- Sidebar now imports from the shared modules directly

sidebar: split god module into focused submodules

mod.rs was ~880 lines mixing five distinct concerns: TUI event loop,
tmux hook management, window layout persistence, daemon lifecycle,
and sidebar pane CRUD. This made it hard to find code and reason
about changes.

Split into single-responsibility submodules:
- runtime.rs: TUI event loop, terminal setup/teardown
- hooks.rs: tmux hook install/remove
- layout.rs: window layout save/restore
- daemon_ctrl.rs: daemon spawn/kill/signal/health checks
- panes.rs: sidebar pane create/destroy/shutdown

mod.rs retains only the public API (toggle, sync, navigate,
run_sidebar, run_daemon) and pure logic (NavAction, compute_nav_target).
Each extracted module uses pub(super) visibility so the sidebar's
internal wiring stays private.

sidebar: add window_id to AgentPane and remove SnapshotAgent

SnapshotAgent existed only because AgentPane lacked a window_id field.
The daemon would convert AgentPane -> SnapshotAgent (adding window_id),
serialize it over the socket, and then the client would convert back
via to_agent_pane(), losing window_id in the process.

Add window_id directly to AgentPane and eliminate SnapshotAgent
entirely. build_snapshot now populates window_id in-place on the
AgentPane vec from the pane_window_ids map, and SidebarSnapshot
holds Vec<AgentPane> directly. The client's apply_snapshot clones
the agents instead of converting them.

AgentPane also gains Serialize/Deserialize derives since it now
goes over the daemon socket as part of SidebarSnapshot.

sidebar: add width and layout config options

Adds a `sidebar` section to .workmux.yaml for configuring the sidebar:

  sidebar:
    width: 40       # absolute columns
    width: "15%"    # or percentage of terminal width
    layout: tiles   # "compact" or "tiles"

Width accepts either an integer (absolute columns) or a percentage
string. Explicit values bypass the 25-50 column clamp applied to the
default 10%. Layout config serves as the base default, overridden by
settings.json (runtime toggle) and tmux globals (current session).

The sync function (tmux hook for new windows) now reads width from the
tmux global first, falling back to config, instead of always
recomputing the default.

docs: document sidebar width and layout configuration

Add configuration examples for the new sidebar.width and
sidebar.layout options across guide, reference, and README.
Also adds the `v` keybinding (layout toggle) to the README
keybinding table and updates descriptions from "compact" to "live".

sidebar: rebalance pane widths via layout tree reflow

When the sidebar is added via split-window, tmux steals width from
only the target pane, leaving other content panes at their original
size. This creates a lopsided layout.

Adds a tmux layout tree parser that reads #{window_layout}, scales
the content subtree proportionally to fill the remaining space, and
applies the result atomically via select-layout. This preserves
existing proportions (a 70/30 split stays 70/30) and handles
arbitrarily nested horizontal and vertical splits.

Replaces the previous resize-pane approach which could only equalize
columns and fought with tmux's constraint solver.

sidebar: handle N-children root HSplit in layout reflow

The previous reflow assumed split-window -hbf always creates a root
HSplit with exactly 2 children. In practice, if the window already
has a root HSplit, tmux inserts the sidebar as an additional sibling
rather than nesting. This caused the reflow to bail out, leaving the
sidebar at whatever tiny width split-window gave it.

Now the reflow finds the sidebar among any number of root children
by pane ID, then scales all other children proportionally. Also adds
logging throughout the reflow path and tests with real tmux layout
strings from a live session.

sidebar: reflow layout on window resize via _sidebar-reflow hook

The old window-resized hook used inline bash with resize-pane to snap
the sidebar width, which stole width from only the adjacent pane and
could crush the sidebar to 1 column when switching to a smaller
client (window-size=latest).

Replaces it with a _sidebar-reflow subcommand that runs the full
layout tree reflow, keeping the sidebar at the correct width and
content panes proportionally balanced. The width is computed from
the target window's width rather than the client's, so windows in
other sessions get the right size even when viewed through a
different-sized terminal.

reduce reconcile log noise from debug to trace

The "preserving agent from previous server lifecycle" messages fire
every 2 seconds per stale agent on the daemon poll cycle, cluttering
debug logs. Moved to trace level since they're only useful for deep
debugging of the resurrect path.
sidebar: deduplicate parse_u16/parse_u32 into generic parse_num
sidebar: use split_once instead of splitn collect in reflow
sidebar: loop-ify hook install/remove

sidebar: extract proportional_widths helper in layout tree

The "round each width, give remainder to last" logic was duplicated
in scale_width and reflow_after_sidebar_add. Extracted into a shared
proportional_widths function.

sidebar: simplify compute_pane_suffixes with HashMap<&str>

Replaced BTreeMap + HashSet with cloned (String, String) keys with a
two-pass HashMap using &str references. Avoids allocating and cloning
session/window name pairs on every render cycle.

sidebar: simplify agent list to space-separated pane IDs

The @workmux_sidebar_agents tmux option stored "pane_id:window_id"
pairs but window_id was never used by the navigate function. Changed
to a plain space-separated list of pane IDs, simplifying both the
daemon serialization and navigation parsing.

sidebar: remove dead version and window_pane_counts fields

These fields were produced by the daemon and serialized in snapshots
but never read by any consumer (app, ui, runtime). Removing them
simplifies build_snapshot from 9 arguments to 7 and eliminates a
per-tick HashMap allocation for pane counts.

sidebar: consolidate tmux global option cleanup

The same three set-option -gu calls for enabled/width/agents were
duplicated in toggle() and shutdown_all_sidebars(). Extracted into
a clear_sidebar_globals() helper.

sidebar: take snapshot by value in apply_snapshot

Avoids cloning the entire agents Vec on every 2-second daemon refresh
cycle. The snapshot is consumed after apply, so ownership transfer
is the natural fit.

sidebar: single-pass host agent lookup in apply_snapshot

Replace Vec<usize> allocation + second scan with a single loop that
short-circuits on the active pane match. Runs every 2s on the
daemon refresh cycle.

sidebar: simplify detect_host_window to return only used fields

Dropped unused window_name return value, replaced Vec allocation
with iterator parsing, and removed the separate target variable.

sidebar: drop unused window_name and Vec alloc in query_tmux_state

Removed #{window_name} from the tmux format string since it was
immediately discarded. Replaced per-line Vec<&str> allocation with
iterator destructuring.

sidebar: extract resolve_target_window helper

Deduplicates the "window_id or current window" resolution that was
repeated in sync() and reflow().

sidebar: collapse two Vecs into indices + widths in reflow

Replaced Vec<(usize, u16)> + separate Vec<u16> extraction with a
Vec<usize> of content indices and a direct Vec<u16> of widths.

sidebar: extract shared list_sidebar_panes helper

Both kill_all_sidebars_and_restore_layouts and shutdown_all_sidebars
duplicated the same list-panes query and parsing logic. Extracted
into a shared helper that returns (window_id, pane_id) pairs, also
replacing splitn().collect::<Vec>() with split_once.

sidebar: share daemon_pid() helper between kill and signal

signal_daemon was shelling out to sh -c to read the pid and send
USR1. Now both kill_daemon and signal_daemon use a shared
daemon_pid() helper and native Rust process::Command, eliminating
the sh subprocess.

sidebar: reduce allocations in status_icon_and_style

Use Cow<'static, str> to avoid String allocations for the most common
cases: spinner frames (Working), stale icon, and blank status. Only
custom working icons and waiting/done with non-default config still
allocate.

sidebar: replace polling loop with event-driven architecture

The sidebar TUI was using a 10ms event::poll() busy loop, causing ~2%
CPU per process (14 processes = ~28% total). Replace with mpsc channels
and blocking recv_timeout for near-zero idle CPU.

Key changes:
- client.rs: SnapshotReceiver replaced with free connect() returning
  SnapshotHandle; reader thread sends () wake signal on new snapshots
- runtime.rs: AppEvent enum (SnapshotReady, Input) with dedicated
  threads for terminal input and snapshot forwarding; main loop uses
  recv_timeout adaptively (250ms when active for spinner, blocks
  indefinitely when hidden); try_recv drain coalesces events before
  rendering
- Last-pane detection now uses window_pane_counts from snapshot data
  instead of shelling out to tmux every 2s, with 3-second startup
  grace period to avoid false positives
- Rendering skipped entirely for inactive windows
- Terminal setup moved before input thread spawn (raw mode required)
- Removed is_last_pane_in_window() from panes.rs
- Re-added window_pane_counts to SidebarSnapshot and daemon TmuxState

sidebar: coalesce wake signals with sync_channel(1)

The unbounded wake channel could queue redundant SnapshotReady events
when multiple snapshots arrived between main loop iterations. Switch to
sync_channel(1) with try_send so at most one wake is pending; subsequent
snapshots overwrite the latest value but their wake is silently dropped.

docs: expand sidebar "how it works" with architecture details

Describes the daemon/client architecture, tmux hooks, layout tree
reflow, and toggle on/off lifecycle.

sidebar: fix deferred layout restore error leaking to user

The deferred layout restore used && chaining, so if select-layout
failed (stale layout string), the cleanup never ran and the error
message was shown in the user's pane. Changed to ; so cleanup always
runs, and added 2>/dev/null to suppress errors from stale layouts.

sidebar: fix blank pane on startup after event-driven migration

The render guard `needs_render && app.host_window_active()` suppressed
drawing when `host_window_active` transiently became false after the
first snapshot. This happened because the daemon's tmux query could
report the sidebar's host window as inactive before tmux had fully
settled the new pane layout.

Under the old polling loop this was masked by constant re-rendering
every 10ms. The event-driven architecture exposed it because renders
only happen on state changes, so a suppressed render left the pane
blank until user input (like pressing j) triggered a redraw.

Fix: remove host_window_active from the render condition. Keep it for
the adaptive timeout (250ms active vs 3600s hidden) and spinner tick
gating where it still serves its CPU-saving purpose.

sidebar: add debug logging to trace blank pane startup

Temporary file-based logging at /tmp/workmux-sidebar-debug.log to
diagnose blank sidebar panes on startup. Logs key events: snapshot
arrival, render calls with agent count and terminal size, key presses,
and host_window_active state transitions.

This commit is intended to be reverted once the blank pane issue is
fully diagnosed.

sidebar: add mouse support for click and scroll

Enable mouse capture in the terminal so the sidebar responds to
pointer events:

- Left click on an agent selects it and jumps to its tmux window
- Scroll wheel moves the selection up/down (enters manual mode)
- Hit testing works in both compact and tile layout modes by
  tracking the rendered list area and computing which item index
  a click lands on

The list_area Rect is stored each frame during render so hit_test
can map screen coordinates back to agent indices, accounting for
scroll offset and variable tile heights.

sidebar: fix layout corruption when panes change while sidebar is open

The old approach saved a layout snapshot at sidebar creation time and
restored it on teardown. If the user split or closed panes while the
sidebar was open, the saved layout was stale (wrong pane count/IDs)
and tmux's select-layout silently failed, leaving lopsided pane sizes.

Replace the save/restore mechanism with live layout tree computation:
on teardown, read the current layout, prune the sidebar node via
recursive tree surgery (prune_pane), scale remaining content to fill
the full window width, then apply atomically. This preserves whatever
pane arrangement the user created while the sidebar was open.

- Add prune_pane() for recursive pane removal with single-child collapse
- Add layout_after_sidebar_remove() to compute post-removal layout
- Update both teardown paths to compute layouts before killing panes
- Remove layout.rs (stale save/restore no longer needed)

sidebar: show git diff stats in tile mode

Add git diff statistics to the sidebar's tile layout, right-aligned
on the project name line (line 2). Shows both committed (dimmed) and
uncommitted (bright) changes using the same color scheme as the
dashboard: success for additions, danger for removals, accent for
the uncommitted diff icon separator.

Architecture: the daemon spawns a background worker thread that
periodically fetches git status for active agent paths via
get_git_status(). Results are stored in a shared cache keyed by
PathBuf with a 5-second TTL. The cache is included in
SidebarSnapshot (with serde default for backwards compatibility)
and applied by clients during apply_snapshot().

The formatter follows the dashboard's logic: when all changes are
uncommitted, only bright stats are shown with the diff icon. When
there's a mix of committed and uncommitted, committed stats appear
dimmed followed by the diff icon and bright uncommitted stats.

sidebar: dim git stats on stale tiles, add right padding

Fix two issues from review:
- Git stats now respect the stale tile state, dimming all colors
  to match the rest of the tile when an agent has been idle for
  over an hour
- Add 1 space right padding after git stats so they don't butt
  against the tile edge

sidebar: optimize git watching with mtime detection and instant broadcast

Replace the naive TTL-based polling with mtime-based change detection
on git internal files (.git/index, .git/HEAD, branch ref files). The
worker now stat()s these files every 1s and only runs the expensive
get_git_status() pipeline when mtimes actually change.

Key improvements:
- Instant broadcast: git worker sets dirty_flag when cache changes,
  triggering the daemon's existing immediate-refresh path. Previously
  cache updates waited up to 2s for the next daemon cycle.
- Smart skipping: stat() calls are ~microseconds vs ~50-100ms for
  the full git subprocess pipeline. Idle worktrees cost almost nothing.
- Linked worktree support: resolves .git file pointers to the actual
  gitdir for correct mtime tracking on linked worktrees.
- Branch ref tracking: watches the branch ref file (e.g. refs/heads/main)
  to detect commits immediately.
- 30s full sweep fallback: catches uncommitted file edits and any
  edge cases missed by mtime checks.

This was informed by a three-way debate between Gemini, Codex, and
MiniMax. All three agreed on fixing the broadcast gap. The mtime
approach was chosen over filesystem watchers (notify crate) as it
achieves similar latency for git operations without adding deps.

cli: filter hidden subcommands from typo suggestions

When mistyping a command like "wm isdebar", clap suggests internal
underscore-prefixed subcommands (_sidebar-reflow, _sidebar-daemon, etc.)
alongside the actual "sidebar" command. These internal commands are marked
hide=true but clap still includes them in "similar subcommands" hints.

Workaround for https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues/4853: intercept
the clap error via try_parse(), use Error::get/insert to filter
underscore-prefixed entries from ContextKind::SuggestedSubcommand, then
let clap render the error normally with full ANSI formatting preserved.
Clap also auto-adjusts grammar ("a similar subcommand exists" vs "some
similar subcommands exist") based on the filtered count.

sidebar: detect uncommitted file edits with cheap git diff probe

The mtime-based detection only catches .git internal changes (commits,
staging, branch switches). Editing a tracked file doesn't touch .git,
so uncommitted diff stats were delayed until the 30s full sweep.

Add `git diff --quiet HEAD` as a cheap probe (~5ms, single subprocess)
on every poll cycle. For clean worktrees this exits instantly with no
overhead. For dirty worktrees it triggers the full pipeline, giving
~1s latency for seeing updated diff stats after file edits.

All three consulted LLMs (Gemini, Codex, MiniMax) independently
recommended this exact approach as the most efficient no-dependency
fix for the missing signal.

sidebar: reduce git probe cost with diff-files and 3s throttle

Two optimizations to reduce the CPU cost of working tree change
detection:

1. Use `git diff-files --quiet` instead of `git diff --quiet HEAD`.
   diff-files only compares index stat cache vs working tree metadata
   without reading git objects. Staging changes are already caught by
   .git/index mtime checks, so this is sufficient and cheaper.

2. Throttle the dirty probe to every 3 seconds instead of every 1s.
   Mtime checks (free stat() calls) still run every 1s for instant
   detection of commits/staging/branch switches. The subprocess probe
   for uncommitted file edits runs 3x less often.

With 20 worktrees this reduces subprocess overhead from ~300-600ms/s
to ~100-200ms every 3s, while keeping git operation detection at 1s
and file edit detection at 3s worst case.

sidebar: skip git polling for stale worktrees

Stale worktrees (all agents idle > 1 hour) are dimmed in the UI and
unlikely to have git activity. Skip mtime checks and dirty probes
for them entirely, only refreshing on the 30s full sweep.

This means a user with 15 active and 5 stale worktrees only pays
the polling cost for 15 instead of 20, reducing subprocess spawns
by 25% in that scenario.

The daemon now sends stale status alongside paths to the git worker.
A path is considered stale only if ALL agents at that path are stale.

show rebase icon when a rebase is in progress

Detect ongoing rebases by checking for rebase-merge/ or rebase-apply/
directories in the git dir (resolving linked worktree gitdir pointers).

Add is_rebasing field to GitStatus and a nf-oct-git_compare nerdfont
icon (with "R" fallback). The icon appears in warning/yellow color in:
- Dashboard git column (before diff stats)
- Sidebar tile git stats (before diff stats)
- Dashboard info panel (icon + "rebase in progress" text)

sidebar: replace git polling with notify-crate filesystem watching

Replace the 1s polling loop that spawned `git diff --quiet HEAD` per
worktree per tick with OS-level filesystem event detection using the
`notify` crate (FSEvents on macOS).

Key changes:
- Watch .git/ internals and worktree roots via notify::RecommendedWatcher
- For linked worktrees, also watch the common gitdir's refs/ and
  packed-refs to catch shared branch updates
- Per-worktree 300ms debouncing coalesces rapid filesystem events
- Worker thread blocks on recv_timeout (zero CPU when idle) instead of
  busy-polling with sleep(1s)
- Fallback full sweep every 30s for edge cases (NFS, watcher overflow)
- Semantic GitStatus comparison ignores cached_at timestamp to avoid
  unnecessary broadcast triggers
- Dynamic watch management: add/remove watchers as active worktrees
  change, with ref-counted shared watches for common gitdirs
- New worktrees get immediate status fetch (seeded with past timestamp)

This eliminates ~15-30ms of subprocess overhead per worktree per second,
giving near-instant change detection with zero idle CPU cost.

sidebar: fix watcher init fallback and add_watch error handling

Address review feedback:
- Watcher init no longer kills the worker thread on failure. Falls back
  to a 2s polling sweep when RecommendedWatcher is unavailable (e.g.
  unsupported filesystem).
- add_watch() only records the watch mapping after the OS watch
  succeeds. Previously it recorded before attempting, causing silent
  degradation when watch() failed (path marked as "already watching"
  for subsequent worktrees).

sidebar: prioritize project name over diff stats in narrow tiles

When the sidebar is narrow, the project name was being truncated to make
room for git diff stats. Now the rendering is width-aware with clear
priority: project name first, then uncommitted stats, then committed
stats.

format_sidebar_git_stats() now accepts available_width and builds
committed/uncommitted spans separately. When space is limited, it drops
the dimmed committed stats first, keeping the more important uncommitted
stats visible. Only truncates the project name if even uncommitted stats
alone need the space, with a minimum project name width of 5 chars.

sidebar: add right padding to title line ellipsis

The title line (line 3) was truncating to the full body width, causing
the ellipsis character to touch the right edge of the tile. Reserve 1
character so the ellipsis has breathing room matching the other lines.

sidebar: attach ellipsis to last word when truncating

Trim trailing spaces before appending the ellipsis character so it
renders as "Continue previous…" instead of "Continue previous …".

docs: add resource usage section to sidebar guide

Document the memory footprint of sidebar processes (~15 MB per
client, ~16 MB for the daemon, ~90 MB total with five agents)
and note the near-zero idle CPU usage.

sidebar: fix race condition causing empty sidebar on startup

The sidebar client called signal_daemon() from the main thread right after
spawning the background connection thread. If the daemon processed the signal
before its accept loop picked up the new connection (which polls every 50ms),
the snapshot was broadcast only to existing clients. The new client had to
wait up to 2 seconds for the next timer-based broadcast, leaving the sidebar
visibly empty until user interaction.

Now the daemon's accept loop sets dirty_flag when a new client connects,
triggering an immediate snapshot broadcast after the client is already in the
clients list. This eliminates the race entirely. The redundant pre-connection
signal_daemon() call in runtime.rs is removed.

sidebar: use --no-optional-locks for background git commands

Prevent the sidebar daemon's git status monitoring from contending
for index.lock with the user's git operations. Git 2.15 introduced
--no-optional-locks specifically for background tools: it skips
refreshing the index stat cache (an optional write optimization)
so the command never takes index.lock.

Without this, the daemon's 300ms-debounced git commands can collide
with user operations like commit or rebase, producing "Unable to
create index.lock: File exists" errors.

sidebar: use dimmed (N) style for pane suffixes in tiles

Change pane index suffixes from bold "[1]" to dimmed "(1)" for a
more subtle appearance. The suffix is rendered as a separate span
with dimmed styling so it doesn't compete visually with the
worktree name. When the name is truncated with ellipsis, the
suffix is naturally dropped.
sidebar: remove DIM modifier from pane suffix for better visibility

dashboard: use dimmed (N) style for pane suffixes

Match the sidebar's pane suffix styling: change from bold "[1]" to
dimmed "(1)". The suffix is rendered as a separate span with the
dimmed palette color so it doesn't compete with the worktree name.

sidebar: add detailed startup logging to debug empty sidebar

Adds logging at every step of the client-daemon handshake to trace
exactly where the breakdown occurs when the sidebar starts empty:

- Daemon: logs ACCEPT (new client with total count), REFRESH (trigger
  reason and client count), BROADCAST (agents, clients before/after,
  new clients arriving during broadcast)
- Client: logs connection_loop lifecycle (connect success/failure,
  socket close with duration), read_loop (each snapshot received with
  agent count and wake channel state)
- Runtime: logs time-since-start on snapshot events, warns when still
  empty after 1s timeout with host_active and timeout duration

This will reveal whether the issue is the client failing to connect,
the daemon not broadcasting, a snapshot with 0 agents, or the event
channel dropping wakes.

sidebar: fix startup hang caused by terminal_light vs input thread race

SidebarApp::new_client() calls terminal_light::luma() to detect the
terminal background color. This sends an escape sequence to the terminal
and reads the response from stdin. But the input reader thread
(spawn_input_thread) was started before new_client(), so crossterm's
event::read() would race to consume the luma response. When the input
thread won the race, terminal_light::luma() hung indefinitely waiting
for a response that was already consumed, leaving the sidebar blank.

Fix: create the app before entering raw mode and spawning the input
thread. This gives terminal_light::luma() exclusive access to stdin.

Also fixes log interleaving: all debug log functions now format the
entire line first then do a single write_all call, which is atomic
with O_APPEND. Each line also includes the PID for easier correlation.

sidebar: remove debug logging

The terminal_light race condition has been identified and fixed.
Remove all debug log calls from client, daemon, and runtime.
release v0.1.158

Show "1:28" instead of "01:28" for a more natural, less formal look.
Seconds still zero-padded (e.g. "0:20", "5:03").

docs: add sidebar screenshot and changelog link

Add a contextual screenshot showing the sidebar alongside an agent

The "What it shows" section was missing git diff stats and agent

docs: make sidebar tmux binding optional

Lead with the command itself instead of requiring a tmux binding
in the setup section. The binding is a convenience, not a prerequisite.

docs: fix inaccurate toggle-off description

Document click-to-jump and scroll navigation, and note that

update README

add named agents and env-aware command detection

Adds an `agents` config map that lets users define short names for agent
commands, solving the multi-account/multi-profile use case from issue #94.

Names are resolved once at config load time. The rest of the system sees
the expanded command string. Named agents are global-only for security
(project configs cannot define them, only reference them).

Also improves agent profile detection to look past `env` wrappers and
`VAR=value` assignments. Commands like `env -u FOO claude` now correctly
resolve to the Claude profile for prompt injection, flag insertion, and
status tracking.

release v0.1.162

docs: document dashboard sweep feature

Add a Sweep section to the dashboard overview documenting the bulk
worktree cleanup feature (R key). Covers the four detection conditions
(PR merged, PR closed, upstream gone, merged locally), clean vs dirty
worktree handling, and modal keybindings.

detect interrupted worktree agents via pane inactivity

When a user Ctrl+C's an agent, it stays in "working" status forever
because there are no hooks for detecting interruption. This adds
automatic detection by monitoring pane content in the sidebar daemon.

For each agent in Working status, the daemon captures the last 5 lines
of the pane every 2 seconds, hashes the content, and tracks when the
hash was first seen unchanged. If content stays the same for 10 seconds,
the agent is marked as interrupted.

The interrupted state is communicated via two channels:
- Sidebar: included directly in the snapshot broadcast
- Dashboard: written to a per-instance runtime file
  (~/.local/state/workmux/runtime/<backend>__<instance>.json) that the
  dashboard reads on each refresh cycle. Stale files (>15s old) are
  ignored so interrupted indicators don't linger when the daemon exits.

The interrupted status clears automatically when pane output resumes or
when the agent leaves Working status. The runtime file is cleaned up on
daemon exit.

In the dashboard, interrupted agents sort with higher priority (same as
Done) since they need attention, and skip the kill confirmation dialog
since the agent is already stopped.

No changes to the persisted AgentStatus enum - interruption is a
display-only derivation to avoid schema migration issues.

fix runtime file staleness and keep kill confirmation

Review feedback from Gemini and Codex caught two issues:

1. The daemon only wrote the runtime file when the interrupted set
   changed, but the dashboard ignores files older than 15s. If an agent
   stays interrupted without changes, the dashboard would stop showing
   the interrupted icon. Fix: re-write the runtime file every 10s as a
   heartbeat to keep updated_ts fresh.

2. Kill confirmation was bypassed for interrupted agents, but since
   detection is heuristic (content-hash based), false positives on
   legitimately quiet agents could lead to accidental kills. Reverted
   to always showing confirmation for Working agents.

make interrupted status sticky until agent status changes

Once an agent is detected as interrupted, the state persists until the
agent's status changes away from Working (e.g., via an RPC SetStatus
call). Previously, any trivial pane change like cursor movement would
reset the content hash and clear the interrupted indicator, making the
agent appear to be working again.

Now the tracker maintains a confirmed set of interrupted pane IDs that
is only cleared when the agent leaves Working status. This also skips
unnecessary pane captures for already-confirmed agents.

fix interrupted icon width and allow clearing on resumed activity

Three fixes:

1. Change default interrupted icon from ⚠️ to 🛑. The variation
   selector in ⚠️ (U+FE0F) causes display_width miscalculation,
   breaking column alignment in the sidebar (elapsed time shifted).

2. Allow interrupted state to clear when the agent resumes working.
   Previously, confirmed interrupted panes skipped capture entirely,
   so the agent could never be detected as active again. Now the
   tracker continues capturing confirmed panes and clears the
   interrupted state after 2+ consecutive polls with changed content
   (~4 seconds of sustained output), filtering out one-off cursor
   movements.

3. Track activity_streak per pane to distinguish between trivial pane
   changes (cursor movement, single redraw) and sustained agent output.

clear interrupted only on RPC status update, not pane content changes

The interrupted state was clearing when the user typed in the pane,
because content hash changes were interpreted as the agent resuming
work. But typing text is not the same as the agent actually working.

The only reliable signal that an agent is working again is a new RPC
status call (SetStatus), which updates the agent's updated_ts in the
state file.

Now the tracker records each agent's updated_ts at the time
interruption is confirmed. On each check, if updated_ts has increased
(meaning the agent sent a new RPC call), the interrupted state clears.
Pane content changes no longer affect it.

Added updated_ts to AgentPane so the tracker can access it from the
snapshot without loading state files separately.

change default interrupted icon to 🟡

The 🛑 stop sign looked too much like an error. Yellow circle is
subtler and conveys "needs attention" without alarm.

fix sidebar showing all agents as done when one finishes

The @workmux_status tmux option is window-level, so all panes in a
window share the same value. The sidebar's snapshot builder used this
shared option for status suppression (clearing Done/Waiting after the
user focuses the window). With multiple agents per window, this caused
incorrect status display since all agents saw the same window-level
status.

Add a pane-level @workmux_pane_status option that tracks status
per-agent independently. The sidebar daemon now reads this pane option
instead of the shared window option. The window-level @workmux_status
is kept for the tmux status bar (which inherently shows one icon per
window). The auto-clear hook now clears both: the pane option
unconditionally (for the focused pane) and the window option
conditionally (if it still matches).

drop interrupted icon from status_icons config

The interrupted status detection remains (tracking pane inactivity), but
no icon is shown for it since the user already knows when they've
interrupted an agent. The interrupted field is removed from StatusIcons
config rather than just set to an empty default, since there's no
meaningful use case for a custom interrupted icon when there's no
visible indicator.

Supersedes "remove default interrupted icon" which only changed the
default value.

remove interrupted from dashboard priority sorting

Interrupted detection still runs but no longer affects sorting since
there's no visible indicator to match the priority elevation. Agents
with Working status now sort normally regardless of interrupted state.

restore interrupted state display in sidebar

The interrupted detection machinery (InactivityTracker in daemon) was
still running and flowing through the snapshot/runtime system, but the
UI display was removed in 5ae8f72b. This meant the spinner kept
animating for agents that had stopped producing output, giving no
visual signal that the agent was interrupted.

Show empty space (no icon) instead of the working spinner when an agent
is detected as interrupted. This lets the user see at a glance which
agents are waiting for input vs actively working.

docs: remove references to unimplemented --layout flag

The -l/--layout flag was planned but never added to the CLI.
Remove documentation references to avoid user confusion
(reported in #101).

Adds a new `sandbox.env` config option (global-only) that allows setting

to `env_passthrough` which reads values from the host.

Global-only for security: a sandboxed agent could modify .workmux.yaml

Works with both container and lima backends.

sandbox.env is designed for secrets like GH_TOKEN, but redact_env_arg
only masked WM_RPC_TOKEN and proxy vars. Add extra_redact_keys parameter
so all sandbox.env keys are redacted in debug log output.

show time since interruption instead of time since working

The elapsed timer for interrupted agents now resets to 0 and counts up
from when the interruption was detected, matching how Done agents show
time since completion. This gives the user actionable info: "interrupted
2m ago" tells them how long the agent has been idle.

throughout the snapshot/runtime/app pipeline to carry the unix timestamp

Global-only for security reasons.

add named layouts with -l/--layout flag

Allow users to define reusable pane arrangements in a `layouts` map in
.workmux.yaml and select one at add-time with `workmux add -l <name>`.

When a layout is selected, its panes replace the top-level panes for that
worktree. All other config (hooks, files, agent, etc.) comes from the

- layouts field merges like other Option fields (project overrides global)
- validate_layouts_config() reuses existing validate_panes_config()

reset status_ts on every explicit SetStatus call

Previously status_ts was preserved when the status value didn't change
(e.g. Working -> Working), which meant the timer kept showing time since
the original Working start. After an interruption clears and the agent
resumes with a new "working" RPC, the timer should reset to reflect the
new work phase.

Now any explicit SetStatus call resets status_ts to now. The old
preservation logic only applies to implicit updates (title-only) where
no status is provided.

reset timer only when resuming from interruption

The previous approach of resetting status_ts on every explicit SetStatus
call broke working timers because Claude Code sends "working" repeatedly
during normal operation.

Instead, the daemon now detects when an interrupted agent resumes (its
confirmed entry clears because updated_ts changed) and resets status_ts
in the agent state file at that moment. This is the only point where a
Working->Working transition should reset the timer.

Reverts the persist_agent_update change and moves the reset logic into
the daemon where it has the necessary context about interruption state.
release v0.1.163

simplify interrupted state to boolean overlay with hidden timer

The interrupted architecture grew too complex: HashMap timestamps flowing
through every layer, daemon writing to per-agent state files to reset
status_ts on resume, and a dual-return from InactivityTracker.

Simplify to treat interruption as a pure UI overlay:
- interrupted_pane_ids reverts to HashSet<String> everywhere (snapshot,
  runtime state, sidebar app, dashboard app)
- InactivityTracker returns HashSet<String>, confirmed map stores just
  updated_ts (no wall-clock timestamp)
- Daemon no longer writes to per-agent state files on resume
- When interrupted clears (updated_ts changes), entries are also cleared
  so the agent gets a fresh 10s inactivity window
- UI hides both spinner and timer for interrupted agents

The timer naturally returns to its original value when the agent resumes
since status_ts is never modified by the daemon.

fix misleading updated_ts doc comment

The comment said updated_ts is "only updated when status changes" but it
is actually updated on every persisted state write (status, title, or
repeated same-status updates). The interruption tracker depends on this
behavior to detect when an agent resumes.

add unit tests for InactivityTracker

Extract check_with() that accepts an explicit Instant and capture closure
so tests can control time and pane content without mocking the full
Multiplexer trait.

Tests cover:
- no interruption before timeout
- interruption after timeout
- content change resets inactivity window
- sticky: content change does not clear confirmed interruption
- updated_ts change clears interrupted state
- fresh 10s window after resume (not immediately re-interrupted)
- non-working agents ignored
- leaving Working clears tracking
- capture failure skips pane
- multiple agents tracked independently

fix pre-timeout RPC updates not resetting inactivity window

An agent sending an RPC update (updated_ts change) before the 10s
timeout would not reset the inactivity window, causing false
interruption detection. For example, an agent that sends "working" at
5s with unchanged pane content would still be marked interrupted at 10s.

Track updated_ts alongside content hash in the entries map. When either
the hash or updated_ts changes, the inactivity window resets. This was
caught by a test suggested during LLM review.

Also adds tests for:
- RPC update before timeout resets window
- exact timeout boundary (>= not >)
- ANSI codes and whitespace normalization
- capture failure doesn't create a false baseline

reset timer when agent resumes from interruption

When an interrupted agent starts working again, the timer was showing
the old elapsed time from before the interruption instead of starting
from zero. Compare current and previous interrupted sets in the daemon
loop to detect resumed agents, then reset their status_ts in the state
file so the timer starts fresh.

document InactivityTracker behavioral spec

Replace the narrative doc comment with a structured spec covering
detection rules, stickiness semantics, resume behavior, and display
requirements. Serves as the source of truth until full integration
tests exist.

extract process_inactivity_tick for testable daemon logic

Extract the inactivity detection + resume + runtime persistence logic
from the daemon loop into a standalone function that accepts injected
time, capture closure, and StateStore. This enables tick-level
integration tests that exercise the full cycle: tracker state machine,
status_ts reset on resume, and runtime file persistence.

Tests use real StateStore file I/O via tempfile::TempDir, avoiding the
need to mock the 40-method Multiplexer trait. Four new tests cover:
- resumed agent gets status_ts reset
- only the resumed agent gets reset (not still-interrupted ones)
- runtime file reflects the interrupted set across ticks
- missing agent file on resume does not panic

fix stale timer showing on resume from interruption

When an agent resumed from interruption, the sidebar would briefly show
a large elapsed time (as if the timer was never paused) before
correcting to ~0s on the next 2s poll. This happened because the
snapshot's agents were read from state files before the tick wrote the
reset status_ts, so the snapshot still carried the old value.

Patch the snapshot's agents inline after the tick for just-resumed
agents, so the corrected status_ts is broadcast immediately without
waiting for the next file read.

refactor daemon into compute_tick / apply_tick_effects pipeline

Extract the daemon loop body into a deterministic tick core:

- compute_tick: takes explicit inputs (agents, captures, time), runs
  inactivity detection, mutates agents in memory for resumed agents,
  builds the snapshot from already-correct data, returns side effects
- apply_tick_effects: writes state files and runtime file from the
  returned side effects
- gather_captures: hoists pane capture I/O out of the tick

This eliminates the one-tick race where the snapshot was built from
stale state files before the tick wrote the corrected status_ts. Now
agents are mutated in memory before build_snapshot, making it
structurally impossible for the snapshot to have stale timer values.

The daemon loop becomes: gather inputs -> compute_tick -> apply effects
-> broadcast. The snapshot patching hack is deleted.

Deletes try_build_snapshot and process_inactivity_tick. Migrates all
tick tests to use compute_tick directly, adds a new test that proves
the snapshot has the correct status_ts on the resume tick.

restore lazy capture and defer last_interrupted commit

Two fixes from post-refactor review:

1. gather_captures now skips panes already confirmed as interrupted by
   the tracker, restoring the lazy capture optimization that was lost
   when hoisting I/O out of the tick. Added is_confirmed() to the
   tracker to expose this check without leaking internals.

2. compute_tick no longer mutates last_interrupted. Instead it returns
   next_interrupted in TickOutput, and the daemon loop commits it after
   apply_tick_effects. This ensures that if persistence fails, the next
   tick will retry the resume logic rather than silently losing it.
