release v0.1.165

better identify worktrees from session or path

Previously, if tmux session and window names were generic (like '0' or 'zsh'), the worktree name could incorrectly default to 'main'.

Now, worktree identification is more robust:
- Prioritize explicit, non-generic names from tmux windows or sessions.
- As a last resort, derive the worktree name from the agent's directory path.

This ensures more accurate and meaningful worktree labels in the dashboard and sidebar, especially when agents are running in conventionally named worktree directories but generic tmux sessions.

use path components instead of basename for worktree name fallback

The previous derive_worktree_name_from_path used path.file_name() (basename)
to determine the worktree name. This breaks when the agent's cwd is a
subdirectory of the worktree, e.g. /project__worktrees/fix-bug/src/lib would
return "lib" instead of "fix-bug".

Replace with path component scanning that walks components in reverse looking
for __worktrees or .worktrees patterns, correctly extracting the worktree name
regardless of cwd depth.

Also remove the tmux name heuristic (is_generic_mux_name). Plain window/session
names are user labels, not repository metadata. The path is the authoritative
source for worktree identity.

update dependencies

Bump version requirements in Cargo.toml to match latest compatible
releases: clap 4.6, clap_complete 4.6, minijinja 2.18, ctrlc 3.5,
nix 0.31.2, tempfile 3.27, getrandom 0.4.2, terminal-light 1.8.
Also updates 81 transitive dependencies via cargo update.

signal-hook left at 0.3 since crossterm and signal-hook-mio depend
on the same major version.

fix codex binary not found in Apple Container sandbox

The codex tarball extracts as `codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (not `codex`),
and the gnu build requires glibc 2.38+ while Debian Bookworm ships 2.36.

Switch to the musl (statically linked) build, rename the extracted binary to
`codex`, detect arch via `uname -m` instead of relying on TARGETARCH build arg
(which Apple Container doesn't populate), and add a build-time smoke test.

Fixes #106.

suppress sidebar daemon signal error in tmux hooks

The dirty_cmd hook fires kill -USR1 to signal the sidebar daemon on
window/session/pane changes. When the daemon PID is transiently empty
or stale (e.g. daemon not yet started, or after a restart), kill exits
with status 1 and tmux surfaces the run-shell failure as an error in
the focused pane.

Append || true so the hook always exits 0. The signal is best-effort
by design since the daemon also has a 2-second refresh fallback.

Fixes #107

normalize relative worktree_dir paths to resolve ".." segments

When worktree_dir is set to a relative path like "../wm/", Path::join()
preserves the ".." literally, producing paths like
/repo/../wm/handle in sandbox commands. This adds a lexical
normalize_path() utility that collapses "." and ".." components without
requiring filesystem access (unlike canonicalize(), which fails for
paths that don't exist yet during worktree creation).

Applied in workflow/create.rs where worktree_dir is resolved and in
lima/mounts.rs where the worktree template is expanded.

Fixes #105
release v0.1.166

bust docker cache for agent install layers on each CI run

The agent Dockerfiles install binaries via curl (e.g. claude, codex,
gemini, opencode, workmux), but BuildKit's GHA cache reuses the old
layer since the Dockerfile text doesn't change between runs. This means
rebuilt images still contain stale agent versions.

Add a CACHE_BUST build arg (set to github.run_id) that changes every
workflow run, placed right before the install RUN in each Dockerfile.
When the arg value changes, Docker invalidates that layer and all
subsequent layers, forcing a fresh download.

For Dockerfile.gemini, the arg is placed after the Node.js install so
that heavier dependency layer stays cached.

fix sidebar daemon CPU spike and memory growth under heavy file I/O

The daemon would spike to ~97% CPU and grow memory continuously (750MB+)
when running with multiple worktrees under heavy file activity (e.g.
Claude sessions with MCP servers).

Root causes and fixes:

1. Unbounded mpsc channel for filesystem watcher events could grow without
   limit when MCP/Claude sessions generate high file I/O. Replaced with
   sync_channel(256) using try_send - drops are safe since pending events
   already guarantee a git status refresh will happen.

2. Socket accept triggered dirty_flag, forcing expensive full tmux refresh
   just to send current state to new clients. Now caches the last broadcast
   payload and sends it immediately on accept, avoiding unnecessary work.

3. Main loop spun every 10ms checking flags, burning CPU even when idle.
   Replaced with a blocking wake channel (recv_timeout) that sleeps until
   a producer signals or the next refresh timer expires.

4. Socket write timeout of 1ms was too aggressive, causing client
   disconnects under minor OS scheduling delays. Increased to 100ms.

5. Added path filtering in the notify watcher callback to skip
   high-volume directories that don't affect git status (.git/objects,
   .git/logs, node_modules) before they enter the channel.

fix review issues in socket server accept path

Address issues found during review:

- Keep a wake_tx clone alive in the main thread so that if the git
  worker panics, recv_timeout returns Timeout instead of Disconnected
  (which would spin the main loop at 100% CPU).

- Clone cached payload under lock and drop before the blocking write_all
  to avoid holding the mutex during I/O (which could stall broadcasts).

- Only push a client to the tracked list if the initial cached payload
  write succeeds, preventing broken/dead streams from accumulating.

filter gitignored paths from filesystem watcher events

Add the `ignore` crate to parse .gitignore rules per worktree root.
Events for gitignored paths (target/, node_modules/, .venv/, build/,
etc.) are now skipped in the drain loop before they trigger debounce
timers or git status refreshes.

This significantly reduces event processing cost when MCP servers or
build tools generate heavy I/O in ignored directories. The root
.gitignore covers the vast majority of noisy paths; the 30s fallback
sweep handles any edge cases from nested .gitignore files.

The hardcoded path filter in the notify callback (.git/objects,
.git/logs, node_modules) is kept as a cheap first-pass to reduce
channel pressure before the comprehensive gitignore check runs.

recover from filesystem event channel overflow

When the bounded FS event channel fills up, set an overflow flag that
marks all active worktrees as pending for an early refresh. This
prevents one noisy worktree from starving git status updates for others.

Also removes hardcoded node_modules from the notify callback pre-filter
since the gitignore matcher in the worker thread handles it properly,
and hardcoding it caused false positives for repos named node_modules.

avoid synchronous stat syscall per filesystem event

Pass false for is_dir in gitignore matching instead of calling
event_path.is_dir() which triggers a stat syscall per event. Directory-
level ignore rules still match via ancestor component checking in
matched_path_or_any_parents.

rebuild gitignore matcher when .gitignore changes

Detect changes to .gitignore files in the filesystem event stream and
rebuild the corresponding worktree's gitignore matcher so filtering
stays current without waiting for a worktree set change.

log gitignore parse errors at debug level

Aids troubleshooting when a workspace starts thrashing due to a
malformed .gitignore preventing proper event filtering.
release v0.1.167

don't show stale indicator for working or waiting agents

The stale (💤) indicator was overriding working and waiting status
icons in the sidebar. This meant an agent waiting for user input
(plan mode confirmation) or actively working would show as sleeping
after the stale threshold (60 min), hiding the actual status that
requires attention.

Now stale only applies to Done and None statuses. Working agents
that are truly stuck are already handled by the interrupted
detection (10s inactivity check).

add manual sleeping toggle for sidebar agents

Adds a `z` keybinding in the sidebar to manually mark agents as
sleeping. Sleeping agents show the 💤 icon with dimmed colors and
sort to the bottom of the list, regardless of their actual status.
Press `z` again to wake them up.

The sleeping state is stored in a tmux global option
(@workmux_sleeping_panes) so all sidebar clients stay in sync.
The daemon reads this on each tick and applies it to both sorting
and the snapshot broadcast. Dead pane IDs are pruned automatically.

Unlike auto-stale (which skips Working/Waiting agents), manual
sleeping always applies, letting users explicitly deprioritize
any agent they don't need to monitor.

use read-modify-write for sleeping pane toggles

Read the current sleeping set from the tmux global option before
writing back, so concurrent toggles from different sidebar clients
don't clobber each other.

fix git diff stats freezing in linked worktrees

Two bugs introduced by the recent gitignore filtering commits:

1. Worker thread panic in linked worktrees: filesystem events from the
   shared gitdir (outside the worktree root) caused strip_prefix to fail,
   then matched_path_or_any_parents received an out-of-root absolute path
   which panics in the ignore crate. This killed the git worker thread
   silently, freezing diff stats permanently.

2. Debounce starvation under continuous file I/O: the pending_worktrees
   timestamp was reset on every event (.and_modify), so the 300ms debounce
   never cleared during sustained activity. The 30s fallback sweep also
   skipped pending worktrees, meaning a busy worktree would never refresh.

Fix: return false (don't ignore) for paths outside the worktree root,
use leading-edge debounce (first event starts the timer), and let the
fallback sweep clear pending entries instead of skipping them.
release v0.1.168
add title and description to docs index

stop recursively watching worktree roots to fix inotify CPU spike

Perf profiling showed 94.6% CPU in notify-rs inotify thread, confirming
the root cause was inotify event volume from recursive worktree watches,
not our event processing code.

With 5+ worktrees running Claude/MCP sessions, inotify generates tens
of thousands of events per second from file I/O in build dirs, node_modules,
and other high-churn paths. The kernel-level event dispatch alone pegs
the CPU before events even reach our bounded channel or gitignore filter.

Platform-aware fix:

- Linux: only watch .git metadata directories via inotify. .git/ is watched
  non-recursively (HEAD, index, MERGE_HEAD, etc.) and refs/ recursively
  (low volume). Working tree changes are detected by a 5s poll sweep.

- macOS: keep recursive worktree root watches. FSEvents aggregates events
  at the directory level in the kernel and handles heavy I/O efficiently,
  so macOS users get near-instant uncommitted change detection. The 30s
  sweep interval is kept as a safety net.

Trade-off on Linux: uncommitted file edits take up to 5s to appear in
sidebar git stats. Commits, pushes, and branch switches remain instant
via inotify metadata watches.

fix codex sandbox warnings for helper binaries and bubblewrap

Codex in sandbox containers produced two warnings:
1. "Refusing to create helper binaries under temporary dir /tmp" because
   HOME=/tmp causes codex_home to resolve to /tmp/.codex, which is under
   the system temp directory
2. "Could not find system bubblewrap on PATH" because bwrap wasn't installed

Fix the first warning by setting CODEX_HOME=/home/user/.codex in the
container environment, which is a non-temp path that Codex accepts. The
directory is pre-created in the Dockerfile with world-writable permissions
for arbitrary container UIDs. The host config mount target is updated to
match. HOME=/tmp is unchanged for all agents.

Fix the second warning by installing the bubblewrap package in the codex
image. While Codex is already sandboxed by workmux's container and
bubblewrap is redundant, installing it (45KB) cleanly silences the warning.

Closes #110

allow sandbox image in project config

The sandbox.image field was enforced as global-only, but the
init-dockerfile command and docs told users to set it in .workmux.yaml
(project config). This caused custom images to be silently ignored
(warning only visible in log file), falling back to the default
ghcr.io/raine/workmux-sandbox:{agent} image.

Reproduced locally: with image set only in project config, the docker
run args showed the default registry image instead of the custom one.

Unlike env_passthrough, env, extra_mounts, and rpc_host which leak host
information or redirect traffic, the image field only controls what runs
inside the container.

sidebar: fix daemon dropping all clients after 30s

Accepted Unix streams inherited O_NONBLOCK from the non-blocking
listener. This made set_write_timeout ineffective and caused write_all
to fail with WouldBlock when the payload grew after the 30s git sweep
exceeded the socket buffer. All clients got dropped simultaneously,
the daemon exited after 10s with no clients, and sidebar panes stopped
updating.

block properly and respect the 100ms timeout.

Agents like Codex run shell commands via login shell (bash -lc), which
sources Debian's /etc/profile and resets PATH to system defaults. This

serialize parallel .git/config writes with advisory lock

When multiple `workmux add` commands run concurrently (e.g. via
background shell jobs), they all write to .git/config and race on
git's internal config.lock file, causing "could not lock config file"
errors.

Add a repo-scoped advisory file lock (.workmux.lock in the git common
dir) that serializes the config-writing portion of worktree creation:
git worktree add, set_branch_base, and set_worktree_meta. The lock is
acquired before the first config write and released immediately after
the last, keeping the critical section tight so non-git operations
(prompt files, tmux setup, hooks) run without contention.

Uses nix::fcntl::flock (already a dependency) so no new crates needed.
The lock is RAII-guarded and released automatically on drop or panic.

fix: zsh completions not working with fpath autoloading

The previous architecture defined _workmux (clap-generated) and
_workmux_dynamic (wrapper), relying on `compdef _workmux_dynamic workmux`
inside the autoloaded function to swap the completion handler. This
reassignment didn't reliably take effect for subsequent completions
when loaded via zsh's fpath autoloading mechanism.

Restructure so the dynamic wrapper IS the _workmux function:

- Post-process clap's zsh output via prepare_zsh_base() to rename
  _workmux -> _workmux_base and strip clap's autoload/eval block
- The dynamic wrapper is now _workmux itself, delegating flag
  completion to _workmux_base and positional args to the dynamic
  helpers (_workmux_handles, _workmux_git_branches)
- _comps[workmux] stays _workmux throughout -- no compdef swap needed

Works correctly with both `eval "$(workmux completions zsh)"` and
file-based fpath autoloading.

fix: zsh completions fall back to file completion for handle/branch args

Commands like open, remove, merge, add only accept worktree handles or
branch names, never file paths. Previously _workmux_base was called
alongside the dynamic completers, which dragged in _default (file
completion) via clap's generated _arguments positional specs.

Stop calling _workmux_base for positional args on these commands. Flag
completion still delegates to _workmux_base when the current word
starts with -.

fix: phantom whitespace completion when no candidates exist

\`"${(@f)$(cmd)}"\` on empty command output produces a single-element
array containing an empty string. compadd then offers that empty string
as a completion candidate, resulting in phantom whitespace.

Filter empty strings from the array with \`${handles:#}\` and skip
compadd entirely when there are no candidates.

remove stale worktree locks before pruning during cleanup

git worktree prune silently skips locked worktrees. If git worktree add
was interrupted, it leaves a "locked" file (containing "initializing")
in $GIT_COMMON_DIR/worktrees/<name>/ that never gets cleaned up. This
caused wm rm to fail with "cannot delete branch used by worktree"
because prune didn't remove the metadata.

Before pruning, the cleanup now resolves the worktree admin directory
(by reading the .git file's gitdir pointer, with a fallback to the
conventional path) and removes any lock file. This applies to both
the synchronous and deferred cleanup paths. Relative gitdir paths
are normalized to absolute, and parse failures are logged.

add auto_name.command config field

Allow users to configure a custom command for LLM-based branch name

Implementation splits the monolithic generate_branch_name into a

prefix fork PR local branch names with owner to avoid conflicts

When checking out a fork PR with `--pr` whose branch is named "main" (or
any other name that conflicts with an existing local branch), the worktree
creation would fail because the local branch name was set directly to the
PR's head_ref_name without any prefix.

The `owner:branch` syntax already handled this by prefixing with the fork
owner (e.g., `sundbp-main`), but `resolve_pr_ref` did not apply the same
logic for fork PRs.

`forkowner-main`), consistent with the `owner:branch` behavior. A shared
`fork_local_branch_name()` helper is used by both code paths. Custom
branch names via `workmux add custom-name --pr 123` are still honored.

add container memory and cpu config for Apple Container

Apple Container VMs default to 1 GB RAM which causes OOM kills for
real workloads (e.g. cloning node_modules). Since --memory sets a
ceiling (not upfront allocation), a generous 16G default is safe.

Add container.memory and container.cpus fields to ContainerConfig.
Apple Container gets --memory 16G by default when unconfigured.
Docker/Podman skip these flags unless explicitly set by the user.
Empty string values are treated as unset to prevent invalid args.

strip ANSI escape sequences from auto-name generator output

kiro-cli emits ANSI color codes and bell characters in its output even
when piped (e.g. "\x1b[38;5;141m> \x1b[0m...branch-name\x07"). This
caused sanitize_branch_name to mangle the escape bytes into the branch
name, producing names like "38-5-141m-0minvestigate-zero-report".

add delay between paste and enter in paste_multiline

When sending multiline content to an agent via bracketed paste, the

to be swallowed. The user would have to manually press Enter.

fix structured theme block corruption in save_theme_scheme

The previous logic used a flawed alphanumeric check to detect structured
theme blocks, which always evaluated false for "theme:" since "theme"
contains alphanumeric characters. This meant indented sub-keys (scheme:,
mode:) were never removed, producing invalid YAML like:

  theme: glacier-signal
    scheme: emberforge
    mode: dark

Rewrite to use a peekable iterator that correctly detects block-style
theme config (bare "theme:" with nothing after the colon) and skips
all indented sub-keys before inserting the new flat value.

fix theme save edge cases and add comprehensive tests

Fix three issues found in code review:

1. Save now preserves explicit mode override. When config had
   theme: { scheme: X, mode: dark }, cycling would lose the mode
   and emit a flat theme: Y. Now emits structured block when mode
   is explicitly set.

2. Prefer uncommented theme: over # theme: when both exist. The
   previous matcher treated commented examples as equivalent to
   active config entries, which could activate a comment and leave
   the real entry as a duplicate.

3. Skip blank lines within structured theme blocks. A block like
   theme:\n  scheme: X\n\n  mode: dark would leave orphaned keys
   after rewrite.

Extracts save logic into a pure update_theme_in_config() function
for testability. Adds 16 persistence tests covering: simple/structured
blocks, blank lines in blocks, mode preservation, commented vs active
lines, empty files, default commenting-out, and trailing newline
handling. Adds 12 config deserialization tests covering: string scheme,
legacy dark/light, structured maps, unknown values, full config files,
and missing theme defaults.

add --prompt-file-only flag for embedded agent workflows

Strip ANSI escapes in the preview fallback path to prevent raw
control sequences from corrupting the terminal when into_text()
parsing fails.

Use Fill(1) instead of Min(0) in footer horizontal layouts for
consistent constraint behavior.

dashboard: disable PR spinner in worktree background fetch

Pass fetch_pr_status=false to workflow::list() when called from the
dashboard background thread. The dashboard fetches PR status
separately via spawn_pr_status_fetch(), and workflow::list's
spinner::with_spinner() writes progress characters to stderr which
shares the terminal with the TUI, corrupting the display.

dashboard: unify background channels into AppEvent with input thread

Replace 4 separate mpsc channel pairs (git_tx/rx, pr_tx/rx,
worktree_tx/rx, worktree_log_tx/rx) with a single AppEvent enum
and event channel. Move terminal input to a dedicated background
thread that forwards crossterm events as AppEvent::Terminal.

The main loop now blocks on recv_timeout() instead of
event::poll(), waking instantly when any background thread sends
data. This eliminates polling entirely: git status, PR status,
worktree list, and git log preview all appear on the next frame
as soon as they're ready instead of waiting for a 2-second refresh
cycle.

Background events are coalesced by draining the channel after the
first event wakes the loop, preventing redundant redraws when
multiple threads complete simultaneously.

dashboard: skip rendering empty worktree table to avoid blink

Don't render the table headers when the worktree list is empty.
The first frame after switching tabs has no data yet (background
fetch is in flight), and rendering headers with default column
widths causes a visible jump when the data arrives and column
widths adjust. A blank area that fills with the complete table on
the next frame is visually seamless.

dashboard: add divider line between tab header and table

Render a thin horizontal rule below the Agents/Worktrees tab
labels to visually separate the tab bar from the table content.
The tab header area grows from 1 to 2 lines to accommodate the
divider.

dashboard: add space between agent icon and spinner in worktree view

The agent status column in the worktree table was rendering the
robot emoji and spinner dots without spacing, unlike the agents
view which separates them.

dashboard: improve worktree table columns

Remove the redundant Branch column since it's identical to the
Worktree handle for most rows. When the branch differs (e.g. the
main worktree), show it inline with an arrow: "workmux ->main".

Add a Git column with diff stats, reusing format_git_status from
the agents view, including the spinner indicator during fetches.

Hide the PR column when no worktree has a PR, matching the agents
view behavior. This avoids a column of dashes taking up space.

dashboard: make 1-9 keys jump to worktree instead of selecting

In the agents view, number keys jump to the agent and close the
dashboard. The worktree view was only selecting the row. Now it
calls jump_to_selected_worktree() for consistent behavior.

dashboard: rename worktree preview title to "Git Log"

The preview pane in the worktree view shows git log output, not a
terminal capture. Label it accordingly.

dashboard: fetch git status for worktrees without agents

The git status fetch only included agent pane paths, so worktrees
without a running agent showed a perpetual spinner in the Git
column. Include worktree paths in the fetch so all worktrees get
their diff stats resolved.

dashboard: show Tab key in agents footer

Replace Commit and Merge shortcuts with Tab Worktrees in the agents
footer bar. This makes the tab switching action discoverable and
matches the worktree footer which already shows Tab Agents. The commit
and merge actions remain accessible via their keybindings.

dashboard: replace x delete with r remove and context-aware modal

Replace the simple x/delete worktree action with r/remove that always
shows a confirmation modal, even for clean worktrees. The modal is
context-aware and shows different states:

- Clean: y to remove, k to toggle keeping the branch
- Unmerged commits: warning shown in dimmed text
- Uncommitted changes: danger-colored warning, requires f to arm
  force mode before y becomes available
- Main worktree: r is a no-op (blocked)

The RemovePlan struct tracks handle, path, dirty/unmerged state,
keep-branch toggle, and force-armed flag. This replaces the previous
pending_delete_worktree which was just an Option<PathBuf> with a
simple y/n confirmation that silently removed clean worktrees without
any confirmation.

The underlying removal still calls workflow::remove which handles
the full lifecycle: kill agent, remove worktree, delete branch, and
clean up tmux window/session.

dashboard: show branch name for main worktree

The main worktree's handle is the repo directory name which is the
same as the project column, making the display redundant (e.g.
"workmux  workmux →main"). Show just the branch name ("main") for
the main worktree since that is what identifies it.

dashboard: add R key for bulk sweep cleanup of worktrees

Adds a sweep modal (R key) in the worktree view that identifies
worktrees ready for cleanup and lets the user bulk-remove them.

Candidates are detected by four signals in priority order:
- PR merged (from GitHub API)
- PR closed (from GitHub API)
- Upstream gone (remote tracking branch deleted)
- Merged locally (no upstream, branch fully merged into base)

The modal shows a selectable list with checkboxes. Non-dirty
candidates are pre-selected. Dirty worktrees appear greyed out
and cannot be selected. Navigation with j/k, Space to toggle,
Enter to remove all selected, Esc to cancel. Shows an empty
state message when no candidates are found.

dashboard: open worktree window on Enter when no agent exists

Previously, pressing Enter on a worktree with no agent pane or existing
mux window did nothing. Now it falls back to workflow::open which
creates the tmux window/session if needed, matching the behavior of
`workmux open <handle>`. The agent pane is still preferred when one
exists for direct pane targeting.

dashboard: add Mux column to worktree table

Shows whether each worktree has an active tmux window/session with a
green dot indicator. Helps identify which worktrees need a window
opened before jumping to them.

dashboard: make sweep (R) available from agents view

The sweep modal operates on worktree data which is independent of the
active tab. Binding R in the agents view too makes it accessible
without switching tabs first. If worktree data hasn't been loaded yet
(user never visited worktree tab), triggers a background fetch
on-demand rather than polling every 5 seconds regardless of tab.

dashboard: improve sweep empty state message

Change "Nothing to sweep." to "No merged or gone worktrees found."
so the user understands what sweep looks for when no candidates
are detected.
release v0.1.145

changelog: add dashboard prefix to v0.1.145 entries

The v0.1.145 changelog entries for worktree view, bulk sweep, kill
agent, and worktree remove were all dashboard features but lacked
a clear scope prefix. Added "dashboard:" to each entry so readers
can immediately tell these are dashboard-specific changes.

dashboard: add Age column to worktree table

Show worktree creation time as a compact relative string (e.g. "2h",
"3d", "1w") using filesystem birthtime. Adds created_at field to
WorktreeInfo populated via std::fs::metadata().created(). Derives
Clone on WorktreeInfo and AgentStatusSummary to support the
all_worktrees baseline pattern used by sorting.

dashboard: add s key to cycle worktree sort mode

Adds sort mode cycling (Natural/Age) to the worktree view with s key.
Natural shows git worktree list order, Age sorts newest first by
directory creation time. Sort mode persists to settings.json.

Uses an all_worktrees baseline (like agents have all_agents) so
apply_worktree_filters always starts from the full unmodified list.
This ensures switching from Age back to Natural instantly restores
the original order instead of keeping the previous sort.

dashboard: fetch PR status per branch instead of bulk

Replace the slow `gh pr list --state all --limit 200` (fetching all
PRs in a repo) with `gh pr list --head <branch> --limit 1` for each
worktree/agent branch. For large repos like epicenter with thousands
of PRs, this is dramatically faster (~1s per branch vs timing out).

Also collects branches from worktrees (via main worktree paths) so
PR status is fetched for projects without running agents. Returns
bool from spawn_pr_status_fetch so the timer only resets when a
fetch actually starts.

dashboard: show PR status in worktree table

Merge PR data from the dashboard's own PR fetching into the worktree
list. Previously, workflow::list was called with fetch_pr_status=false
to avoid spinner corruption, so worktree pr_info was always None.

Now apply_worktree_filters merges pr_statuses into worktrees by
matching branch names. PrStatus events trigger a worktree filter
re-apply so new PR data appears immediately. Worktree fetch runs
at startup so repo roots are available for the first PR fetch.

Also moves the PR column to appear right after Git (before Mux/Age)
for better visual grouping.
dashboard: show R Sweep in worktree footer bar

dashboard: batch PR status lookups with GraphQL

Replace N separate `gh pr list --head <branch>` calls with a single
GitHub GraphQL API query using aliased pullRequests fields. For a
project with 12 worktrees this reduces PR status fetching from 12
process spawns to 1.

The GraphQL function builds one alias per branch, pipes the query
as JSON via stdin to `gh api graphql --input -`, and deserializes
the batched response. Owner/name are passed as GraphQL variables
(not string-interpolated) to avoid injection. Repo context and
GHES hostname are resolved via `gh repo view` so fork conventions
and `gh repo set-default` are respected.

Falls back to per-branch REST calls if GraphQL fails.

dashboard: add close mux window action (c) to worktrees view

Pressing `c` on a worktree row closes its tmux window/session without
removing the git worktree or deleting the branch. Useful for stopping
an agent while keeping the worktree around for later.

The action is a no-op on the main worktree or worktrees without an
active mux window. After closing, triggers a refetch so the Mux column
updates immediately.

dashboard: add project picker to worktree view

Add a 'p' key in the worktree view that opens a project picker modal,
allowing users to switch which project's worktrees are displayed without
leaving the dashboard.

The picker shows all known projects (discovered from cached repo roots),
supports type-to-filter, and highlights the currently active project.
Selecting a project sets an override that scopes the worktree list to
that repo's worktrees only.

Required adding workdir-aware variants of git functions
(list_worktrees_in, get_all_worktree_modes_in, etc.) and a new
workflow::list_in that accepts an optional repo path.

dashboard: split worktree preview into info panel and styled git log

Replace the plain git log preview in the worktree view with a two-panel
layout: an info panel on the left showing worktree metadata, and a
styled git log on the right.

The info panel displays branch name, base branch with ahead/behind
counts, committed and uncommitted diff stats, PR status with CI checks,
agent status, and mux window state. All data comes from already-cached
state so no extra fetches are needed.

The git log uses a structured format (%h, relative date, subject) parsed
and rendered with colored spans instead of plain --oneline output.

dashboard: polish project picker and worktree preview

Resolve repo roots before applying the session scope filter so the
project picker discovers all projects even when session filtering is
active. Add 'p Project' to the worktree footer bar. Remove the brief
"(loading...)" flash from the git log panel.

remove unused list_prs_in_repo function

The GraphQL-based list_prs_for_branches (with REST fallback) fully
replaced the old bulk PR fetching approach. list_prs_in_repo fetched
up to 200 PRs with `gh pr list --state all --limit 200` which was
too slow for large repos. No callers remain.

dashboard: highlight current worktree in worktree table

Apply the same current_worktree_fg highlight used in the agents view
to the worktree table. Compares each worktree path against the
directory the dashboard was launched from, with canonicalized path
comparison to handle symlinks.
release v0.1.146

dashboard: parallelize PR status fetching with priority ordering

PR fetches were sequential across repos, causing slow updates when
multiple projects were configured. Now uses bounded thread pool (max 4
workers) with a shared queue. The current project's repo is fetched
first so its PR data appears sooner.

Also fixes stale PR state: clears pr_statuses when a repo returns no
PRs, and clears all_worktrees on project switch so the PR re-fetch
triggers correctly for the new project.

fix sweep popup showing "---" for dirty worktrees

The sweep modal used "---" as a prefix for dirty (non-selectable) worktree
entries, which looked like a broken placeholder symbol. Replace it with "[ ]"
to be visually consistent with the checkbox used for selectable entries.
The dimmed styling and "(dirty)" label already communicate that these
entries cannot be toggled.

Before: > --- test (merged locally, dirty)
After:  > [ ] test (merged locally, dirty)

dashboard: split app.rs into focused submodules

The 1961-line app.rs monolith was difficult to navigate and maintain.
Split it into an app/ module directory with 8 focused files while
preserving all behavior:

- mod.rs: App struct definition, new(), refresh()
- types.rs: AppEvent, DashboardTab, ViewMode, sweep/picker/remove types
- agents.rs: agent filtering, sorting, navigation, kill, display helpers
- worktrees.rs: worktree tab navigation, removal, sweep, project picker
- appearance.rs: theme cycling, persistence, update_theme_in_config + tests
- background.rs: background thread spawning for git/PR status fetches
- preview.rs: preview pane update, refresh, scrolling, sizing
- events.rs: AppEvent dispatching

Uses inherent impl App blocks in child modules (not extension traits)
since Rust's module visibility lets children access parent-private
fields naturally. This avoids trait import churn in actions.rs and
mod.rs while keeping the same flat access pattern.

dashboard: pre-select current project in project picker

The project picker always started with the cursor at the top of the
list regardless of which project was active. Now it finds the current
project's position in the sorted list and sets the initial cursor
there, so the user immediately sees which project they're on.

dashboard: add open PR in browser action

Add `o` keybinding in both Agents and Worktrees views to open the
associated pull request in the default browser.

- Add `url` field to PrSummary, fetched via GraphQL and REST queries
- Use platform-appropriate browser opener (open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux)
- Show status message in footer when no PR exists or URL isn't loaded yet
- Report spawn errors instead of silently swallowing them
- Add transient status_message field to App with 3-second auto-clear
release v0.1.147

crossterm 0.29.0 panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in
parse_csi_sgr_mouse when a terminal sends mouse coordinate 0. This
started happening after updating to tmux 3.6a.

Patches crossterm via a fork that uses saturating_sub(1) instead of
plain subtraction for mouse coordinates, preventing the u16 underflow.

See: crossterm-rs/crossterm#590
docs: clarify rust target directory caveat

dashboard: add open PR checks in browser action

When PR checks fail, you often want to open the checks page to see why.
Add `O` (shift-o) keybinding to open {pr_url}/checks in the browser,
complementing the existing `o` to open the PR itself.

Refactored open_pr_for_selected into a shared open_pr_url helper that

Available in both agents and worktrees views.

use live tmux pane title during agent reconciliation

The reconciliation code already prefers live session and window names
over stale stored values, but was ignoring the live pane title. Claude
Code dynamically updates pane titles with task descriptions, so the

dashboard: add base branch picker to worktree tab

Press `b` in the worktree tab to open a filterable modal picker that

local branches sorted alphabetically with the current base pinned to
the top and highlighted.

Implementation details:
- New git helpers: `list_local_branches_in(workdir)` and
  `set_branch_base_in(branch, base, workdir)` for worktree-scoped ops
- `BaseBranchPicker` modal follows the same pattern as `ProjectPicker`
- `base_branch` field added to `WorktreeInfo`, populated from git config
- On confirm, both `WorktreeInfo` and `GitStatus` caches are updated
  immediately so the UI reflects the change without waiting for the
  background refresh cycle
- Guards against main worktree, detached HEAD, and branch-list failures

dashboard: make base branch picker work from agents tab too

The `b` shortcut now opens the base branch picker from both the agents
and worktrees tabs. In agents view, the branch is resolved from the
selected agent's working directory via git.

Also fixes the picker popup to use a fixed height (based on total branch
count, up to 15) with a scrolling window, so the UI doesn't shift as
the filter narrows results.

list: show worktree age in wm ls output

Add an AGE column to the list command showing how old each worktree is

add --continue flag to workmux open

When passed, injects the appropriate "continue last conversation" flag
for the configured agent CLI:

- gemini, kiro: --resume
- vibe, unknown agents: ignored (with warning)

release v0.1.150

dashboard: fix immediate exit on startup from stray Enter key

When launching `workmux dashboard` from the shell, the Enter keypress
used to execute the command could linger in the terminal input buffer.
The input thread would consume this stray Enter before the user saw
anything, triggering JumpToSelected on the auto-selected first agent
and immediately switching tmux to that agent's window.

Fix by reordering startup: create App state and apply CLI overrides
before spawning the input thread, then drain any buffered terminal
events with a non-blocking poll loop. This ensures stray keypresses
from the shell launch are discarded before the TUI starts processing
input.
release v0.1.151

show animated spinner for pending PR checks

Replace the static pending check icon with an animated braille spinner
that cycles on each dashboard tick (250ms). This gives clear visual
feedback that CI checks are still running.

- Use existing spinner_frame counter from App state for the animation
- Pass spinner_frame through format_pr_status and format_pr_details
- Apply spinner in all three locations: agent table, worktree table,
  and worktree info panel
- Remove unused pending field from CheckIcons since it's replaced by
  the spinner
- Use palette.accent instead of palette.warning for pending color

tests: use adaptive polling in poll_until()

Replace fixed 0.1s polling interval with adaptive backoff schedule
[0.0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1]. This checks the condition immediately
on the first call (0.0s), then ramps up the interval. Most poll_until
calls resolve quickly (file exists, pane has output), so the immediate
check and fast initial intervals avoid unnecessary waiting.

Also switches from time.time() to time.monotonic() for more reliable
timeout tracking.

The poll_interval parameter is kept for API compatibility but the
adaptive schedule is always used.

Baseline: 97.95s -> 97.63s (modest, main gains expected from sleep removal)

replace time.sleep() with deterministic readiness checks

Replace all fixed time.sleep(1.5) and time.sleep(0.5) calls in test
files with polling-based readiness checks. This eliminates arbitrary
waits that are either too long (wasting time) or too short (causing
flakes under load).

Add wait_for_window_ready() helper to conftest.py that polls until a
tmux window exists and has visible pane content, replacing the pattern
of sleeping 1.5s after run_workmux_add().

Specific replacements:
- 16x time.sleep(1.5) after run_workmux_add -> wait_for_window_ready()
- 1x time.sleep(0.5) after echo -> wait_for_pane_output()
- 1x time.sleep(0.5) between status updates -> removed (redundant)
- 1x time.sleep(DEFERRED_SCRIPT_WAIT) -> poll_until(worktree removed)

Files changed: test_agent_state, test_workmux_capture, test_workmux_run,
test_workmux_send, test_workmux_status, test_workmux_wait,
test_session_navigation, conftest

cache template git repo across test session

Create a session-scoped template git repository that is initialized once
and copied per test, replacing 5 git subprocess calls (init, config x2,
add, commit) with a fast filesystem copy.

The git config (user.name, user.email) is stored in .git/config and
survives the shutil.copytree, so copied repos work identically to
freshly initialized ones.

fix flaky agent tests with absolute paths and increased timeouts

Two integration tests (test_add_with_agent_flag_overrides_default and
test_global_agent_starts_in_default_pane) intermittently failed because
the fake agent's output file wasn't created within the 5s timeout.

The handshake mechanism signals readiness before exec'ing the login
shell, so agent commands are sent while the shell may still be
initializing. On macOS, /etc/zprofile runs path_helper which reorders
PATH, and the shell initialization timing is variable under load.

Fix by using absolute paths for both agent commands and output files,
removing dependencies on PATH resolution and working directory. Also
increase timeouts from 5s to 10s for these tests to handle slow shell
initialization under parallel test load.

suppress noisy success output from just check

Quiet the check pipeline so it only prints meaningful output:
- Add @ prefix to suppress recipe echoing for fmt, ruff, clippy
- Add --quiet to clippy and ruff check to suppress progress/success lines
- Buffer unit-tests output, only show summary line (full output on failure)
- Buffer pyright output, filter "0 errors" success line (full output on failure)
- Remove "All docs have descriptions" echo from docs-check

On success, `just check` now produces a single line (test summary)
instead of 28+ lines of progress noise.

merge clippy-fix and clippy into single pass

The rust pipeline previously ran clippy twice: once with --fix to
auto-fix warnings, then again with -D to fail on remaining warnings.
This is redundant since a single invocation with both --fix and -D
will fix what it can and fail on the rest, eliminating a full
duplicate build/lint cycle.

dashboard: add 'a' hotkey to create worktree in worktrees view

Add an "a" hotkey in the worktrees tab that opens a two-phase modal:
1. Name input for the new worktree/branch name
2. Optional base branch picker (Esc to skip, Enter to select)

The worktree is created via workflow::create in a background thread,

dashboard: refactor add-worktree to unified fzf-style picker

Replace the two-step flow (name input -> base branch picker) with a

- Cursor 0 shows "Create <query>" when filter is non-empty

dashboard: add tab completion cycling in add-worktree picker

Tab fills the first matching branch into the input. Subsequent Tab

Occupied branches (already have worktrees) are shown at the bottom

dashboard: add emacs keybindings to add-worktree inputs

dashboard: show add worktree hotkey in footer bar

Add "a Add" to the worktrees view footer alongside the other

Group actions first (Add, Remove, Sweep, Close, PR), then navigation

Replace substring matching with fuzzy subsequence matching so that
typing "mergefail" matches "merge-fail-delete" (each character must
appear in order in the target). Applied to branch filter, PR filter,
and tab completion.

dashboard: add contextual hints to add-worktree modal

Show a dimmed hint line above the footer describing the current
action: "New branch from main" when creating, or "Worktree for
existing branch 'name'" when selecting an existing branch.

add workmux resurrect command with crash-safe reconciliation

Adds a new `resurrect` command that restores worktree windows after a
tmux or computer crash. Uses persisted agent state files to detect which
worktrees had active agents before the crash.

Key implementation details:

- Reads raw (non-reconciled) agent state files and matches workdir to
  git worktrees using canonical descendant path matching
- Calls workflow::open directly with focus_window=false (no focus stealing)
  and continue_session=true (resumes agent conversations)
- Partial failure handling: continues on error, reports all results
- Repo-scoped: only considers worktrees in the current git repo

Crash-safe reconciliation via per-state boot IDs:

- Adds server_boot_id() to Multiplexer trait (tmux: #{start_time})
- Each AgentState now stores the server's boot_id when written
- Reconciliation skips deletion when boot_id doesn't match current
  server, preserving state files for resurrect to use
- Legacy state files without boot_id get deleted as before
- Eliminates the need to run resurrect before list/dashboard

Also fixes workflow::open to respect focus_window option on the
existing-target fast path (previously called target.select()
unconditionally).

resurrect: add tracing for plan and execution phases

Logs each agent state file processed (pane_id, workdir, boot_id,
status), the action determined per handle (restore/skip and why),
and the outcome of each restoration attempt. Enables debugging
with RUST_LOG=workmux=info when resurrect doesn't work as expected.

cli: group commands by category in help output

The flat list of 20+ commands was overwhelming for new users.
Replace the default clap-generated command list with a custom
help_template that organizes commands into logical groups:

- Worktree lifecycle (add, remove, merge, open, close, resurrect)
- Monitoring (dashboard, list, path, status)
- Setup and configuration (init, setup, config, sandbox, sync-files, claude)
- Agent interaction (send, capture, wait, run)
- Help and updates (docs, changelog, update, completions)

Clap doesn't support multi-heading subcommand groups natively,
so this uses a manual help_template. The tradeoff is that command
descriptions are duplicated between doc comments and the template,
but the list rarely changes and the UX improvement is significant.
release v0.1.152

docs: add multiple Claude configurations section

Document how to use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with direnv to maintain
separate work/personal Claude configurations. Also covers the
wrapper script approach using .direnv/bin/claude for full control
over per-project Claude launch behavior. Added in response to
PR #95 discussion about managing multiple agent profiles.

reduce log spam for preserved resurrect agents

The "preserving agent from previous server lifecycle" message logged at
info level on every reconcile tick for each stale agent, causing massive
log spam. Downgrade to debug since this is expected recurring state that
persists until `workmux resurrect` is run.

show spinner on PR column header while fetching

When PR statuses are being refreshed in the background, the PR column
header now shows a braille spinner animation, matching the existing
Git column behavior. This gives users a visual indicator that PR data
is being updated.

use static pending icon instead of spinner in info panel PR line

The info panel was showing two spinners for pending checks: one on the
PR line and another on the detail line below with elapsed time. Added a
dedicated pending icon to CheckIcons (nerdfont: timer_sand, fallback:
◷) and use it on the PR line, keeping the animated spinner only on the
detail line where it shows elapsed time.

fix nix build: add outputHashes for crossterm git dependency

The nix build was failing because flake.nix didn't include outputHashes
for the git dependency crossterm-0.29.0 (from raine/crossterm fork).
Nix requires explicit hashes for git dependencies when using cargoLock.

Adds the SRI hash for crossterm-0.29.0 at commit f99eeae4.

add `r` hotkey to remove worktree from agents tab

The `r` key previously only worked in the worktrees tab. Now it also
works in the agents tab by finding the worktree matching the selected
agent's path and triggering the same removal flow (confirmation modal,
dirty check, force arm). If no matching worktree is found (e.g. orphaned
agent), the key press is silently ignored.

Also adds the key to the agents tab help overlay.

fix incorrect guest home directory with Lima 2.1.0

Lima 2.1.0 changed the guest home directory from
/home/<user>.linux to /home/<user>.guest. workmux had
the .linux suffix hardcoded, so mounts targeted the wrong
path and Claude couldn't find .claude.json.

Detect the installed Lima version via `limactl --version`
and use .guest for >=2.1.0, .linux for older versions.
Falls back to .linux if limactl isn't available.

Existing VMs need to be recreated for the fix to take effect.

Closes #92
release v0.1.153

add Codex status tracking support

Codex hooks API supports the same event structure as Claude Code,
enabling working/done status tracking via UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse,
and Stop hooks. No waiting state is possible since Codex has no
permission prompt event.

The setup command detects ~/.codex/, merges hooks into
~/.codex/hooks.json (with deduplication), and auto-enables the
codex_hooks feature flag in ~/.codex/config.toml. If the flag was
already set to false, it gets replaced rather than duplicated.

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2109
release v0.1.154

include .codex/hooks in cargo package

The Codex hooks config is embedded at compile time via include_str!
and needs to be in the published crate tarball.
release v0.1.155

include waiting agents in last-done navigation

The last-done command now considers both "done" and "waiting" agents,
navigating to whichever was most recently updated. This lets users
quickly jump to agents that need their input, not just ones that
have finished. Repeated invocations cycle through all matching agents
in reverse chronological order as before.

fix PR status fetch delayed 30s on dashboard open

spawn_pr_status_fetch() iterated self.agents to collect branches, but
on the first call to refresh(), self.agents was still empty because
apply_filters() (which populates it from all_agents) runs at the end
of refresh(). The fetch found no branches, returned true (resetting
the 30-second timer), and the real first fetch was delayed by a full
interval.

Two fixes:
- Iterate self.all_agents instead of self.agents so branches are
  collected before apply_filters() has run. The name/stale UI filters
  should not affect which PRs get fetched.
- Return false when repo_branches is empty so the caller does not
  reset the timer. This allows retry on the next 2-second tick once
  git statuses or worktree data arrive from their background threads.

use configured main_branch for dashboard diff base detection

When main_branch is set in .workmux.yaml, the dashboard now uses it as
the preferred fallback for diff base detection instead of auto-detecting
via refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. This fixes spurious diffs on the main
worktree when the configured main_branch differs from the remote's
default branch (e.g. using dev/latest instead of main).

The fallback chain is now: per-branch workmux-base > configured
main_branch > auto-detected default branch > "main". The same fix
applies to both git status calculation and the diff modal's base branch
resolution. Empty main_branch values are treated as unset.
