reduce update notification frequency

Update notifications were showing once per day indefinitely, which
could feel nagging especially with frequent releases. Now uses a
burst/cooldown pattern: 3 consecutive notifications, then a 7-day
cooldown, repeating until the user updates. When a new version is
discovered the burst counter resets.
release v0.1.165

better identify worktrees from session or path

Previously, if tmux session and window names were generic (like '0' or 'zsh'), the worktree name could incorrectly default to 'main'.

Now, worktree identification is more robust:
- Prioritize explicit, non-generic names from tmux windows or sessions.
- As a last resort, derive the worktree name from the agent's directory path.

This ensures more accurate and meaningful worktree labels in the dashboard and sidebar, especially when agents are running in conventionally named worktree directories but generic tmux sessions.

use path components instead of basename for worktree name fallback

The previous derive_worktree_name_from_path used path.file_name() (basename)
to determine the worktree name. This breaks when the agent's cwd is a
subdirectory of the worktree, e.g. /project__worktrees/fix-bug/src/lib would
return "lib" instead of "fix-bug".

Replace with path component scanning that walks components in reverse looking
for __worktrees or .worktrees patterns, correctly extracting the worktree name
regardless of cwd depth.

Also remove the tmux name heuristic (is_generic_mux_name). Plain window/session
names are user labels, not repository metadata. The path is the authoritative
source for worktree identity.

update dependencies

Bump version requirements in Cargo.toml to match latest compatible
releases: clap 4.6, clap_complete 4.6, minijinja 2.18, ctrlc 3.5,
nix 0.31.2, tempfile 3.27, getrandom 0.4.2, terminal-light 1.8.
Also updates 81 transitive dependencies via cargo update.

signal-hook left at 0.3 since crossterm and signal-hook-mio depend
on the same major version.

fix codex binary not found in Apple Container sandbox

The codex tarball extracts as `codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (not `codex`),
and the gnu build requires glibc 2.38+ while Debian Bookworm ships 2.36.

Switch to the musl (statically linked) build, rename the extracted binary to
`codex`, detect arch via `uname -m` instead of relying on TARGETARCH build arg
(which Apple Container doesn't populate), and add a build-time smoke test.

Fixes #106.

suppress sidebar daemon signal error in tmux hooks

The dirty_cmd hook fires kill -USR1 to signal the sidebar daemon on
window/session/pane changes. When the daemon PID is transiently empty
or stale (e.g. daemon not yet started, or after a restart), kill exits
with status 1 and tmux surfaces the run-shell failure as an error in
the focused pane.

Append || true so the hook always exits 0. The signal is best-effort
by design since the daemon also has a 2-second refresh fallback.

Fixes #107

normalize relative worktree_dir paths to resolve ".." segments

When worktree_dir is set to a relative path like "../wm/", Path::join()
preserves the ".." literally, producing paths like
/repo/../wm/handle in sandbox commands. This adds a lexical
normalize_path() utility that collapses "." and ".." components without
requiring filesystem access (unlike canonicalize(), which fails for
paths that don't exist yet during worktree creation).

Applied in workflow/create.rs where worktree_dir is resolved and in
lima/mounts.rs where the worktree template is expanded.

Fixes #105
release v0.1.166

bust docker cache for agent install layers on each CI run

The agent Dockerfiles install binaries via curl (e.g. claude, codex,
gemini, opencode, workmux), but BuildKit's GHA cache reuses the old
layer since the Dockerfile text doesn't change between runs. This means
rebuilt images still contain stale agent versions.

Add a CACHE_BUST build arg (set to github.run_id) that changes every
workflow run, placed right before the install RUN in each Dockerfile.
When the arg value changes, Docker invalidates that layer and all
subsequent layers, forcing a fresh download.

For Dockerfile.gemini, the arg is placed after the Node.js install so
that heavier dependency layer stays cached.

fix sidebar daemon CPU spike and memory growth under heavy file I/O

The daemon would spike to ~97% CPU and grow memory continuously (750MB+)
when running with multiple worktrees under heavy file activity (e.g.
Claude sessions with MCP servers).

Root causes and fixes:

1. Unbounded mpsc channel for filesystem watcher events could grow without
   limit when MCP/Claude sessions generate high file I/O. Replaced with
   sync_channel(256) using try_send - drops are safe since pending events
   already guarantee a git status refresh will happen.

2. Socket accept triggered dirty_flag, forcing expensive full tmux refresh
   just to send current state to new clients. Now caches the last broadcast
   payload and sends it immediately on accept, avoiding unnecessary work.

3. Main loop spun every 10ms checking flags, burning CPU even when idle.
   Replaced with a blocking wake channel (recv_timeout) that sleeps until
   a producer signals or the next refresh timer expires.

4. Socket write timeout of 1ms was too aggressive, causing client
   disconnects under minor OS scheduling delays. Increased to 100ms.

5. Added path filtering in the notify watcher callback to skip
   high-volume directories that don't affect git status (.git/objects,
   .git/logs, node_modules) before they enter the channel.

fix review issues in socket server accept path

Address issues found during review:

- Keep a wake_tx clone alive in the main thread so that if the git
  worker panics, recv_timeout returns Timeout instead of Disconnected
  (which would spin the main loop at 100% CPU).

- Clone cached payload under lock and drop before the blocking write_all
  to avoid holding the mutex during I/O (which could stall broadcasts).

- Only push a client to the tracked list if the initial cached payload
  write succeeds, preventing broken/dead streams from accumulating.

filter gitignored paths from filesystem watcher events

Add the `ignore` crate to parse .gitignore rules per worktree root.
Events for gitignored paths (target/, node_modules/, .venv/, build/,
etc.) are now skipped in the drain loop before they trigger debounce
timers or git status refreshes.

This significantly reduces event processing cost when MCP servers or
build tools generate heavy I/O in ignored directories. The root
.gitignore covers the vast majority of noisy paths; the 30s fallback
sweep handles any edge cases from nested .gitignore files.

The hardcoded path filter in the notify callback (.git/objects,
.git/logs, node_modules) is kept as a cheap first-pass to reduce
channel pressure before the comprehensive gitignore check runs.

recover from filesystem event channel overflow

When the bounded FS event channel fills up, set an overflow flag that
marks all active worktrees as pending for an early refresh. This
prevents one noisy worktree from starving git status updates for others.

Also removes hardcoded node_modules from the notify callback pre-filter
since the gitignore matcher in the worker thread handles it properly,
and hardcoding it caused false positives for repos named node_modules.

avoid synchronous stat syscall per filesystem event

Pass false for is_dir in gitignore matching instead of calling
event_path.is_dir() which triggers a stat syscall per event. Directory-
level ignore rules still match via ancestor component checking in
matched_path_or_any_parents.

rebuild gitignore matcher when .gitignore changes

Detect changes to .gitignore files in the filesystem event stream and
rebuild the corresponding worktree's gitignore matcher so filtering
stays current without waiting for a worktree set change.

log gitignore parse errors at debug level

Aids troubleshooting when a workspace starts thrashing due to a
malformed .gitignore preventing proper event filtering.
release v0.1.167

don't show stale indicator for working or waiting agents

The stale (💤) indicator was overriding working and waiting status
icons in the sidebar. This meant an agent waiting for user input
(plan mode confirmation) or actively working would show as sleeping
after the stale threshold (60 min), hiding the actual status that
requires attention.

Now stale only applies to Done and None statuses. Working agents
that are truly stuck are already handled by the interrupted
detection (10s inactivity check).

add manual sleeping toggle for sidebar agents

Adds a `z` keybinding in the sidebar to manually mark agents as
sleeping. Sleeping agents show the 💤 icon with dimmed colors and
sort to the bottom of the list, regardless of their actual status.
Press `z` again to wake them up.

The sleeping state is stored in a tmux global option
(@workmux_sleeping_panes) so all sidebar clients stay in sync.
The daemon reads this on each tick and applies it to both sorting
and the snapshot broadcast. Dead pane IDs are pruned automatically.

Unlike auto-stale (which skips Working/Waiting agents), manual
sleeping always applies, letting users explicitly deprioritize
any agent they don't need to monitor.

use read-modify-write for sleeping pane toggles

Read the current sleeping set from the tmux global option before
writing back, so concurrent toggles from different sidebar clients
don't clobber each other.

fix git diff stats freezing in linked worktrees

Two bugs introduced by the recent gitignore filtering commits:

1. Worker thread panic in linked worktrees: filesystem events from the
   shared gitdir (outside the worktree root) caused strip_prefix to fail,
   then matched_path_or_any_parents received an out-of-root absolute path
   which panics in the ignore crate. This killed the git worker thread
   silently, freezing diff stats permanently.

2. Debounce starvation under continuous file I/O: the pending_worktrees
   timestamp was reset on every event (.and_modify), so the 300ms debounce
   never cleared during sustained activity. The 30s fallback sweep also
   skipped pending worktrees, meaning a busy worktree would never refresh.

Fix: return false (don't ignore) for paths outside the worktree root,
use leading-edge debounce (first event starts the timer), and let the
fallback sweep clear pending entries instead of skipping them.
release v0.1.168
add title and description to docs index

stop recursively watching worktree roots to fix inotify CPU spike

Perf profiling showed 94.6% CPU in notify-rs inotify thread, confirming
the root cause was inotify event volume from recursive worktree watches,
not our event processing code.

With 5+ worktrees running Claude/MCP sessions, inotify generates tens
of thousands of events per second from file I/O in build dirs, node_modules,
and other high-churn paths. The kernel-level event dispatch alone pegs
the CPU before events even reach our bounded channel or gitignore filter.

Platform-aware fix:

- Linux: only watch .git metadata directories via inotify. .git/ is watched
  non-recursively (HEAD, index, MERGE_HEAD, etc.) and refs/ recursively
  (low volume). Working tree changes are detected by a 5s poll sweep.

- macOS: keep recursive worktree root watches. FSEvents aggregates events
  at the directory level in the kernel and handles heavy I/O efficiently,
  so macOS users get near-instant uncommitted change detection. The 30s
  sweep interval is kept as a safety net.

Trade-off on Linux: uncommitted file edits take up to 5s to appear in
sidebar git stats. Commits, pushes, and branch switches remain instant
via inotify metadata watches.

fix codex sandbox warnings for helper binaries and bubblewrap

Codex in sandbox containers produced two warnings:
1. "Refusing to create helper binaries under temporary dir /tmp" because
   HOME=/tmp causes codex_home to resolve to /tmp/.codex, which is under
   the system temp directory
2. "Could not find system bubblewrap on PATH" because bwrap wasn't installed

Fix the first warning by setting CODEX_HOME=/home/user/.codex in the
container environment, which is a non-temp path that Codex accepts. The
directory is pre-created in the Dockerfile with world-writable permissions
for arbitrary container UIDs. The host config mount target is updated to
match. HOME=/tmp is unchanged for all agents.

Fix the second warning by installing the bubblewrap package in the codex
image. While Codex is already sandboxed by workmux's container and
bubblewrap is redundant, installing it (45KB) cleanly silences the warning.

allow sandbox image in project config

The sandbox.image field was enforced as global-only, but the
init-dockerfile command and docs told users to set it in .workmux.yaml
(project config). This caused custom images to be silently ignored
(warning only visible in log file), falling back to the default
ghcr.io/raine/workmux-sandbox:{agent} image.

Reproduced locally: with image set only in project config, the docker
run args showed the default registry image instead of the custom one.

Unlike env_passthrough, env, extra_mounts, and rpc_host which leak host

inside the container.

186 cols), the global would be 25 (MIN_WIDTH). New windows created
later in wider sessions (427 cols) would get 25-wide sidebars instead

already does. The stale @workmux_sidebar_width global, terminal_width(),

make project name slightly less dim in sidebar tiles

Use palette.text with DIM modifier for the project name in
non-stale/non-sleeping tiles. The pane title line keeps the
original palette.dimmed color since it's tertiary information.

sidebar: add daemon lifecycle logging

Add info-level logs for daemon start, exit reasons (SIGTERM, no clients),
and periodic health (every 60s with client count). Also add debug-level
log for client connections.

Needed to diagnose why the daemon keeps dying and leaving sidebar panes
orphaned without updates. Previously the daemon had no info-level logs
so its lifecycle was invisible in workmux.log.

sidebar: fix daemon dropping all clients after 30s

Accepted Unix streams inherited O_NONBLOCK from the non-blocking
listener. This made set_write_timeout ineffective and caused write_all
to fail with WouldBlock when the payload grew after the 30s git sweep
exceeded the socket buffer. All clients got dropped simultaneously,
the daemon exited after 10s with no clients, and sidebar panes stopped
updating.

block properly and respect the 100ms timeout.

add profile.d script so shims survive login shell PATH resets

Agents like Codex run shell commands via login shell (bash -lc), which
sources Debian's /etc/profile and resets PATH to system defaults. This
loses the shim directory (/tmp/.workmux-shims/bin) that workmux prepends
to PATH, making host_commands unavailable.

image that re-adds the shim directory to PATH when it exists. Login
shells source profile.d scripts after /etc/profile, so the shim path
is restored.

This approach preserves the existing --user privilege model and avoids
changing container startup semantics.

serialize parallel .git/config writes with advisory lock

sandbox: add container.devices and container.group_add config

Adds typed `sandbox.container.devices` and `sandbox.container.group_add`
fields for issue #132, letting users expose host hardware (USB serial,
GPU, KVM, etc.) to the container sandbox without bypassing workmux's
existing config discipline.

Why not a generic custom_args passthrough: the rest of sandbox config
is typed and validated, and passthrough would become an unrestricted
escape hatch from the security model encoded in the arg builder. Typed
fields cover the reported use case cleanly.

Key decisions:

- Both fields are global-config-only, same treatment as extra_mounts,
  host_commands, env_passthrough, etc. A malicious repository must not
  be able to silently escalate its own sandbox by persisting device
  access in .workmux.yaml.
- Apple Container hard-bails when either field is set. The runtime does
  not support --device / --group-add at all; failing early is better
  than a confusing runtime error.
- Device entries support both a simple string form (`/dev/kvm`,
  `/dev/dri:/dev/dri:rwm`) and a structured form
  ({ host_path, guest_path, permissions }), mirroring ExtraMount.
- Values are validated structurally at config load (absolute paths,
  r/w/m permission tokens, no whitespace in group names).

Deny-mode privilege drop rewrite:

The big subtlety was network-deny mode. The container there starts as
root for iptables setup and drops privileges via gosu inside
network-init.sh. gosu resolves the target user via /etc/passwd and
calls setgroups() based on that lookup, which means --group-add
supplementary groups attached to the initial root process do not
survive the privilege drop: the dropped user ends up with just the
primary GID and loses membership in e.g. `dialout`, so --device alone
is useless for filesystem permission checks.

This commit replaces gosu with setpriv (util-linux) in
docker/Dockerfile.base. In deny mode, workmux now passes the
configured groups as WM_EXTRA_GIDS, and network-init.sh invokes
`setpriv --reuid ... --regid ... --groups "$WM_EXTRA_GIDS"
--inh-caps=-all`, which explicitly sets the supplementary group list
before exec. Without WM_EXTRA_GIDS, setpriv is called with
--clear-groups so the dropped process still does not inherit root's
supplementary groups (preserving the previous gosu behavior).

We deliberately pass explicit groups from Rust instead of using
`setpriv --keep-groups`: the initial root process in deny mode has
GID 0 in its supplementary list, and --keep-groups would leak that
into the unprivileged user's group list, weakening isolation. The
explicit form strips root's groups and keeps only the configured
ones.

In allow mode the container runs as --user uid:gid directly, so
Docker's --group-add is used as normal and WM_EXTRA_GIDS is not set.

Breaking change for the sandbox base image: users must rebuild and
republish `ghcr.io/raine/workmux-sandbox:*` images so they contain
setpriv (via util-linux) instead of gosu. Existing images will fail
network-init.sh at startup in deny mode until rebuilt.

sandbox: harden setpriv group list and reject whitespace in device paths

Two fixes from post-implementation review of the previous commit.

1. network-init.sh: prepend the primary GID to setpriv --groups so the
   supplementary group list matches Docker's default --user behaviour.
   With only WM_EXTRA_GIDS in --groups the dropped process had a
   supplementary list that omitted the primary GID, diverging from
   non-deny mode where Docker includes it. Building a single GROUPS_ARG
   from WM_TARGET_GID and (optionally) WM_EXTRA_GIDS also collapses the
   if/else into a single setpriv invocation.

2. ContainerDevice::validate now rejects leading, trailing, and embedded
   whitespace in both the string and struct forms. Previously a value
   like " /dev/kvm" or { host_path: "/dev/kvm " } passed validation but
   to_arg emitted the original padded string, producing a broken
   --device argument at runtime.

When sweep removed multiple worktrees, the TUI froze for 5-10 seconds
with no visual feedback. Move the removal loop to a background thread

through the existing AppEvent channel. Input is blocked during sweep

PR #142 tried to solve the deleted-head-branch problem by storing raw
URLs in branch.remote, which broke upstream tracking, remove --gone,
HTTPS users, and push.default=simple.

This change takes a different approach: keep using named remotes for
tracking (so all Git tooling works), but fetch refs/pull/N/head from
origin into the fork remote's tracking namespace via refspec:

This ensures the PR code is available even if the contributor deleted
their branch, while preserving normal Git upstream semantics.

If the PR ref doesn't exist (non-GitHub forge, local test repo), we
fall back to fetching from the fork remote directly.

host+owner+repo instead of just owner, preventing cross-forge remote
reuse bugs.

rejects container names with spaces. The handle was derived from the
raw directory basename without sanitization.

Fix: apply `slug::slugify()` (already in deps) to the handle before
building the container name. `AI Enablement` → `ai-enablement` →
`wm-ai-enablement-12345`.

fix: slugify only container name, not state store handle

The original PR fix slugified the entire `handle` variable, which is
used both for the Docker container name and as the state store key.
This caused cleanup to fail for paths with spaces: `remove` derives the
handle from the raw directory name (no slugify), so `list_containers`
looked up the wrong key and found nothing, leaving containers running.

Separate the two: keep `handle` as the raw directory basename so the
state store key is consistent everywhere, and apply slugify only when
constructing `container_name` to satisfy Docker's naming constraints.

fix(pi): remove session_shutdown status update

The handler called `workmux set-window-status` without awaiting the
subprocess. Pi exits before workmux reads `pane_current_command`, so
the state file ends up with `command=zsh`, defeating the

sidebar: resolve agent labels via candidate chain

Replaces the simple "project/worktree" sidebar label with a resolver that
walks a candidate chain (worktree → window → session → task_title →
project) and picks the first two meaningful entries as primary and
secondary labels. The worktree is always preserved: when not primary, it
is appended to the secondary as "<secondary> · <worktree>".

Why: the previous scheme failed to distinguish multiple agents on the
same worktree (e.g., several panes on `main`) and wasted screen space
repeating the project name. The chain approach surfaces the most
distinctive identity available (sticky tmux window name, named session,
or task title) while still showing the worktree.

Implementation notes:

- New resolve_labels() and sanitize_pane_title() live in agent_display.
- Window names are only promoted when AgentPane.window_cmd differs from
  the window name, since tmux's automatic_rename flag is unreliable.
  window_cmd is populated only for the tmux backend.
- Generic shell/default window names (zsh, bash, pwsh, default, ...)
  are blocklisted even when they differ from pane_current_command.
- Workmux-prefixed session/window names are ignored as not
  user-authored.
- Worktree-primary keeps project as secondary even when other
  candidates are meaningful, to keep the common feature-branch case
  stable.

sidebar: log fd count and watch lifecycle for leak debugging

Temporary instrumentation to verify whether the sidebar daemon's notify
watcher leaks file descriptors over time on macOS, as suggested by an
external bug report.

- tracing::info on every notify watch / unwatch with the running
  watch_to_worktrees size, so add and remove counts can be tallied from
  the log to detect lifecycle imbalances.
- tracing::info snapshot once a minute with fd_count (read from /dev/fd
  on macOS, /proc/self/fd on Linux), watched_paths and worktrees, so
  fd drift can be observed in steady state.

Default log level captures both. To remove later, grep for "fd-leak".

sidebar: stop promoting pane title to primary/secondary label

The pane title was a candidate in the resolver chain, so when worktree,
window, and session were all generic the agent's current task title
("Investigating flaky CI", "Document phase…") got promoted to the first
line. This made the sidebar's primary identity jump around as the agent's
work changed, and duplicated the third line that already shows the pane
title.

Drop TaskTitle from the candidate chain entirely. The chain is now
worktree → window → session → project. The pane title still renders on
its own optional third line via sanitize_pane_title in the UI layer.

Removes the now-unused task_title parameter from resolve_labels and the
is_task_title_meaningful helper.

implement sidebar template customization

Replace hardcoded compact and tile layouts with a token-based template
DSL. Users can now configure `sidebar.templates.compact` and
`sidebar.templates.tiles` to control what appears in each sidebar row.

Built-in defaults reproduce the previous rendering exactly, so existing
users see no change unless they opt in.

Key design decisions:

- `{fill}` is the only layout marker. It splits the line into left and
  right segments; the leftmost flex token on the left absorbs slack and
  truncates with ellipsis when space is tight.

- `git_stats` is a self-degrading composite token. The layout engine
  passes it an allocated width and it internally drops committed →
  uncommitted → both to fit.

- Tile chrome (stripe + 2-col icon column + gap) is drawn by the
  renderer, not described by templates. Templates only control the body
  area. This keeps line alignment automatic.

- Optional tile lines (e.g. `{pane_title}`) are dropped when all
  variable-text tokens resolve to empty strings.

- Styles are semantic only. Each token carries an intrinsic style class;
  stale/active/selected state is applied as a post-pass over spans.

Agent identity (absorbed from PR #153):

- New `{agent_icon}` and `{agent_label}` tokens classify the running
  agent using the existing profile system.

- `sidebar.agent_icons` provides per-agent override map (e.g.
  `claude: "✳"`).

- `AgentPane` gains `agent_command` populated from stored state.

- The PR #153 `sidebar.agent_identity` enum is dropped; adding
  `{agent_icon}` to a template is the public API.

clean up dead code and unused fields from template refactor

Remove methods and fields that became unused after the sidebar renderer
was rewired through the template engine:

- `SidebarApp::display_name` (superseded by template tokens)
- `RowContext::{display_name, status_icon_style, is_interrupted, is_sleeping}`
- `TokenId::{min_width, can_be_empty}` (layout solver uses natural_width instead)
- `ui::truncate_to_width` and `ui::truncate_with_ellipsis` (layout solver has its own)

sync sidebar width across all windows

When the sidebar is manually resized in one tmux window, the new width is
now propagated to all other windows running the sidebar.

Implementation:
- Store synced width in @workmux_sidebar_width tmux global option and
  persist to settings.json (same pattern as sidebar layout mode).
- Detect manual pane resize in the sidebar TUI by tracking window width:
  unchanged window width + changed pane width means manual resize.
- Debounce resize events (150ms) to avoid excessive reflows during mouse
  drag. Process pending resize on tick timeout and after event draining.
- Use startup grace period (3s) to avoid false detection from initial
  pane creation layout divergence.
- Reflow peer windows directly via layout_tree::reflow_after_sidebar_add
  instead of spawning subprocesses.
- Clamp synced width per-window to leave at least 10 columns for content.

Files changed:
- mod.rs: width resolution, read/set synced width, reflow_all_sidebars_except
- app.rs: resize detection with debounce and window-width tracking
- runtime.rs: feed resize events through debounce, deadline-aware timeout
- panes.rs: expose list_sidebar_panes, use effective_width_for
- state: add sidebar_width to GlobalSettings

sidebar: pre-resolve agent icon/label and skip I/O on render path

Move agent icon and label resolution out of the per-token getters and
into RowContext construction, where they are computed once per row and
stored as plain strings. The token getters now just clone the cached
strings.

Add resolve_profile_for_display in multiplexer::agent, an I/O-free
variant of resolve_profile that skips the tmux show-environment and
which lookups used to canonicalize bare command names. The sidebar
renders frequently and on the UI thread, so the original resolver's
shell-outs were unsuitable here. Trade-off: agents launched via a
custom symlink or wrapper whose filename does not match a known
profile name fall back to DefaultProfile in the sidebar.

Drops the agent_icons reference from RowContext since icon resolution
now happens up front.

sidebar: restore spacing between git_stats spans

The template renderer was emitting git_stats spans back-to-back, so the
result rendered as +1278-400✏+21 instead of +1278 -400 ✏ +21. The
previous hand-rolled tile renderer in main injected a space-span between
each git stat span plus a trailing space; the template port dropped
that step but kept the width accounting (calc_width still adds spans.len()
to cover those spaces), leaving a width vs. content mismatch.

Bake the separators into format_sidebar_git_stats's returned spans so
every caller gets correctly spaced output. Width is unchanged. The
background post-pass in the row renderer paints the inserted space-spans
along with the rest of the row, so selection highlight stays seamless.

sidebar: reserve 1-column right margin in tile rows

Tile body content rendered all the way to the right edge, so the elapsed
timer (and git stats on the second line) sat flush against the sidebar
border. Main has always reserved a single blank column on the right.

Shrink body_width by 1 and append a trailing space-span on each tile
line. The trailing span participates in the selection-highlight post-pass
so the highlighted background still extends to the edge.

sidebar: drop trailing space from git_stats output

format_sidebar_git_stats was emitting a trailing space after the last
git stat span, which doubled up with the row-level 1-column right margin
added when rendering tile lines. The result was an extra blank column
between the rightmost git stat and the sidebar edge.

Strip the trailing space and rework the priority-fallback logic to build
candidate span lists once and pick the first that fits, so width and
content stay in sync.

sidebar: emit flex slack as fill-spaces, not as token padding

When a left-segment flex token had less natural width than its allocation,
the layout solver padded the token in place with trailing spaces. That
shoved any tokens rendered after the flex (e.g. {pane_suffix} in
"{primary}{pane_suffix} {fill} {elapsed}") to the right edge instead of
keeping them next to the flex.

Render the flex token at min(natural, allocated) only, truncating with
ellipsis when natural exceeds allocation. The leftover slack is now
inserted as a single space-span between the left and right segments,
which is where the {fill} marker conceptually sits.

sidebar: drop joiner space from pane_suffix value

The pane_suffix value was hardcoded as " (1)" with a leading space so
the default template " {primary}{pane_suffix}" would join them
naturally. When users put {pane_suffix} on a line without {primary} in
front, the leading space made the suffix appear floating and indented.

Make the value just "(1)" and have the default templates write
"{primary} {pane_suffix}" with an explicit literal space. To avoid a
stranded space when pane_suffix is empty, the layout solver now
collapses one adjacent whitespace literal next to any field that
resolves to an empty string. This also benefits other optional fields
like {pane_title} or {agent_label} when used with literal separators.

sidebar: emit fill slack when no left flex token is present

When a template's left segment had no flex token (e.g. just
"{pane_suffix} {fill} {elapsed}" with pane_suffix empty), the layout
solver never assigned the available budget anywhere, so the right
segment rendered flush against the left edge instead of being pushed to
the right by {fill}.

Use `available` directly as the fill width in that case, matching the
spec that {fill} pushes the right segment to the right.

sidebar: live-reload templates and icons on config edits

Previously the sidebar parsed templates, agent_icons, layout, and width
once at startup. Editing the global config or a project's .workmux.yaml
required killing the daemon to take effect, which broke the iteration
loop for users tweaking their sidebar.

The daemon now spawns a dedicated notify watcher that watches the parent
directory of the global config and the parent directory of every active
project's .workmux.yaml. Watching the parent dir (not the file) catches
atomic-rename saves used by vim, claude-code's Edit/Write tools, and
most editors -- a direct file watch would lose the inode on rename and
miss subsequent edits. Events are debounced 200ms (lock-on-first; not
sliding) and pass through a basename filter so unrelated edits in the
config dir do not cause reloads. The watcher uses a bounded channel with
overflow handling that mirrors the git worker, and emits the same fd-leak
debug instrumentation on every watch / unwatch.

On a successful daemon-side reload the snapshot's config_version atomic
is incremented and broadcast. Each sidebar client compares the version
to its own and, on change, re-runs Config::load_with_location_from
anchored at its host agent's worktree path so per-project .workmux.yaml
overrides are honored. Templates that fail to parse keep the previously
valid tokens (warning logged once, cached string updated so the same
broken value is not retried on every snapshot). agent_icons swaps in
unconditionally; sidebar.width is stored on the app for future use but
no tmux resize-pane is issued from the client (would conflict with the
existing layout_tree reflow).

status_icons is intentionally NOT live-reloaded: tmux's
@workmux_pane_status holds the icon string itself, and build_snapshot
compares pane statuses to those exact strings to suppress stale
done/waiting markers. Hot-swapping the icons mid-run would cause real
status updates to be incorrectly suppressed until panes are re-stamped.

find_project_config performs filesystem walks, so per-agent results are
cached in the daemon and pruned when an agent leaves. The cache keeps
the per-tick cost flat regardless of agent count.

sidebar: fix config-watch edge cases from review

- Compute host_agent_idx from the new snapshot before reload_config_from_disk
  so the first config_version bump after a snapshot anchors at the correct
  host path (was using stale or None index).
- Skip watcher.unwatch when a project config dir collides with the global
  watched dir; otherwise removing the project would also drop the global
  watch and silently break global config reloads.
- Stop caching None results from find_project_config so a freshly created
  .workmux.yaml is detected on the next tick. Successful lookups are still
  cached.
- Bump config_version on every detected change, even if the daemon-side
  Config::load fails. Clients use their own per-project anchor, so a
  daemon-CWD load failure should not gate notifications.

docs: escape literal {{ in sidebar template guide VitePress runs rendered markdown through Vue's template compiler, so a literal `{{` token (even inside an inline code span) is parsed as the start of a mustache interpolation and fails the build with "Error parsing JavaScript expression". Wrap the literal-brace mention in {{ so the v-pre directive prevents Vue from interpreting the contents.

sidebar: classify and cache agent kind for generic interpreter panes

The {agent_icon} and {agent_label} sidebar tokens were rendering empty
for several common agents because tmux's pane_current_command for them
is not the binary name we can look up in the profile registry:

  - Claude Code reports its version, e.g. "2.1.118"
  - Codex reports a truncated binary, e.g. "codex-aarch64-a"
  - Gemini, Pi, OpenCode (when launched via npx) and Vibe run as a
    generic interpreter ("node", "Python")

Add a two-stage classifier in `src/agent_identity.rs`. Stage 1 inspects
the foreground command (version regex, codex prefix, exact stems for
known agents). Stage 2 falls back to pane title patterns when the stem
is a known generic interpreter. The result is a canonical profile
name (Option<String>), cached on AgentState the first time it becomes
non-None and preserved on subsequent ticks - titles drift over time
(non-agent processes can print "Vibe" or "◇" into the title), so we
lock in the first definitive answer rather than re-evaluating every
tick. Pane reuse is handled by the existing reconcile path, which
deletes the stored entry when pane_current_command changes.

The sidebar's resolve_agent_icon / resolve_agent_label consult the
cached agent_kind first (validated against a known set so a malformed
or future-version state file can't shadow a valid agent_command) and
fall back to today's stem-based resolve_profile_for_display when no
cached value is available. Pre-existing custom agent_icons overrides
keep working, and old state files (no agent_kind field) round-trip
cleanly via serde default.

The ✳ glyph rendered inconsistently across terminals and emoji fonts,

sidebar: centralize per-agent metadata on AgentKind enum

The sidebar's resolve_agent_icon and resolve_agent_label each carried
their own match block over the canonical profile-name string. Adding a
new variant compiled cleanly because nothing tied those string keys to
the agent set; the new agent silently rendered as the first letter of
its name.

Introduce AgentKind in src/agent_identity.rs with exhaustive default_icon
and default_label methods, plus as_str/from_str for round-tripping the
cached agent_kind string. The classifier now produces AgentKind
internally and only widens to String at the cache boundary, so the
serialized form is always derived from the enum. The sidebar resolvers
parse the cached string into AgentKind (falling back to the stem-based
profile resolver when the cache is missing or unknown) and look up
metadata through default_icon/default_label. A new variant now forces
a compile error in those methods.

Other agent-name string matches in src/sandbox/, src/config.rs, and
src/agent_setup/ are out of scope: they cover container/lima/config-dir
concerns, not sidebar metadata, and most already key off an existing
agent_setup::Agent enum or KNOWN_AGENTS list.

sidebar: split git_stats into git_committed, git_uncommitted, git_rebase

The composite {git_stats} token always rendered rebase + committed +
uncommitted as one unit, so users couldn't put committed and uncommitted
on different lines or omit the rebase indicator.

Add three new template tokens that render the segments independently:

  - {git_committed}: dimmed +N -M for branch-diff lines
  - {git_uncommitted}: bright diff icon + uncommitted +N -M
  - {git_rebase}: rebase icon

Each new token self-fits within its own allocated width using a per-
segment variant ladder (e.g. "+1278 -400" -> "+1278" -> "-400" ->
empty), mirroring the composite's degradation behaviour but at the
single-token level. This avoids the leftover layout solver fallback
producing meaningless ellipsis-truncated numbers like "+127...".

{git_stats} keeps working unchanged as a backwards-compatible composite
for users who want the all-in-one self-fitting behaviour.

Also fix a latent bug in is_empty_line: it called ctx.resolve(id) for
every field, but git-segment tokens always resolve to the empty string
(rendering goes through styled spans instead). This made any tile line
containing only {git_stats} count as empty and get dropped, even when
the git status had content. Inspect natural_width for git-segment
tokens instead.

Spacing between split tokens relies on the existing
collapse_empty_fields pass, which drops one adjacent whitespace literal
per empty field, so "{git_committed} {git_uncommitted}" joins cleanly
in all populated/empty combinations.

sidebar: support tmux-style codes inside templates

Templates accept the same `#[fg=...,bold]` directives that workmux already
uses for status icons. A directive is a stateful overlay that applies to
all subsequent literals, fields, fill spaces, and the inner spans of
composite tokens like `{status_icon}` and `{git_stats}`, until the next
directive or `#[default]`. Each line starts clean.

Why: the existing token DSL only let users compose tokens, with hardcoded
intrinsic styles. Custom colors required code changes. This lets users
highlight per-token elements (e.g. color the worktree label) and style
literal text in templates, reusing the tmux convention they already know
from workmux's status-icon configuration and tmux's own `status-format`.

Implementation:

- Expose `tmux_style::apply_tmux_directives` so the sidebar template
  parser can fold each directive into a running ratatui `Style` overlay
  without going through the higher-level span splitter.
- New `Token::Style(String)` variant. `parse_line` recognizes `#[...]`,
  emits the directive content as a token, and falls back to literal text
  for unclosed `#[...`. Lone `#` characters still parse as literals.
- `Token::Style` is zero-width in the layout engine so `{fill}`, ellipsis
  truncation, and right-segment dropping are unaffected.
- `render_with_layout` accumulates a `user_style` while iterating tokens
  and patches it onto the intrinsic style of each renderable span. Patch
  semantics mean user fg/bg/modifiers win where set; intrinsic
  attributes the user did not set survive (e.g. the active row's bold
  is preserved beneath a user `fg=red`).
- Stale rows ignore the user overlay so dim state stays authoritative.
- `collapse_empty_fields` skips over intervening style tokens when
  scanning for the joiner whitespace to drop, so styles between an empty
  field and its space don't shield the leak.
- `is_empty_line` ignores style tokens (style-only lines are still
  empty).

Default templates are unchanged; existing configs render identically.

sidebar: pop trailing non-fields before right-segment drop loop

A trailing zero-width Token::Style (e.g. `{elapsed}#[default]`) or any
non-field literal at the end of the right segment used to make the field
drop loop bail immediately, leaving right-side fields un-droppable when
the line is too narrow. Symptom: at narrow widths the right segment ate
the layout budget and the left flex token (typically {primary}) was
truncated to nothing.

Strip non-fields from the tail before each iteration so the loop can
reach the rightmost field. Locked by a regression test that compares
plain vs `#[default]`-suffixed templates at width 3.

sidebar: render split git tokens on the right side of fill

The right-segment match arm only special-cased {git_stats}; the split
{git_committed}, {git_uncommitted}, and {git_rebase} variants fell into
the generic ctx.resolve() branch which returns an empty string for those
multi-span tokens. As a result a template like `{fill} {git_committed}`
rendered an empty right segment.

Mirror the left-segment behavior by routing every git token id through
ctx.git_segment_spans(). This also makes the design's
"#[fg=red]{git_committed}" overlay work on the right side, since the
returned spans go through styled_span like every other span.

Pre-existing on this branch (the split tokens were added in 34a082f),
but exposed by the styling spec which promises overlay support on each
git token. Added a regression test that the right segment renders the
committed stats.

sidebar: preserve user bg= under selected row highlight

The selected-row post-pass overwrote every span's background with
highlight_row_bg, hiding any user bg= directive applied through a
template. The styling spec says explicit user bg= should win on the
styled span.

Only set the highlight bg on spans that don't already have one. The
selection still fills literals, fields, fill spaces, and trailing
padding (none of which carry a bg in the default template), so the
highlight remains visible everywhere except where the user actually
asked for a different background.

sidebar: log a debug message for unclosed #[ in templates

The styling design promised a single tracing::debug! per parse when an
unclosed #[ was seen, so users troubleshooting a malformed template have
something to find in the logs. The literal-fallback path now sets a
flag that emits one debug record at the end of parse_line, regardless
of how many unclosed sequences appeared.

support no<attr> negation in tmux-style directives

Add `nobold`, `nodim`, `noitalics`, `nounderscore`, `noreverse`, and
`nostrikethrough` to the tmux-style directive parser so users can
strip a modifier that the token's intrinsic style baked in.

The motivating case is sidebar templates: `{elapsed}` renders with the
DIM modifier for visual hierarchy, and there was no way to undo it
from a template directive. With this change, a user can write
`#[fg=cyan,nodim]{elapsed}` to render the elapsed time at full
brightness in cyan.

Implementation note: the parser builds the overlay on top of
`Style::default()`, so a `noX` directive ends up in the overlay's
`sub_modifier`. ratatui's `Style::patch` honors `sub_modifier`,
removing the corresponding bit from the intrinsic style's
`add_modifier`. No render path changes needed.

Use the standard tmux convention `no<attr>` rather than `-attr` or
`attr=off` for symmetry with how tmux configures status-bar styles.

docs: rename sidebar templates page to customization

The page outgrew its title: it now covers tokens, layout rules,

"Customization" describes the whole surface; "Templates" undersold the

Rename the file and the nav entry, and update the cross-link from the

sync sidebar width across all windows

When the sidebar is manually resized in one tmux window, the new width is
now propagated to all other windows running the sidebar.

- Store synced width in @workmux_sidebar_width tmux global option and
  persist to settings.json (same pattern as sidebar layout mode).
- Detect manual pane resize in the sidebar TUI by tracking window width:
  unchanged window width + changed pane width means manual resize.
- Debounce resize events (150ms) to avoid excessive reflows during mouse
  drag. Process pending resize on tick timeout and after event draining.
- Use startup grace period (3s) to avoid false detection from initial
  pane creation layout divergence.
- Reflow peer windows directly via layout_tree::reflow_after_sidebar_add
  instead of spawning subprocesses.
- Clamp synced width per-window to leave at least 10 columns for content.

allow private sandbox domains

Network-deny sandboxes previously rejected private resolved addresses even
when the user explicitly allowed the hostname. This blocked corporate VPN
registries and mirrors while leaving users with only coarse workarounds.

matching, and permits private routable address classes only for opted-in hosts

broadcast addresses. Legacy string entries keep their existing public-only

sidebar: add daemon-owned proactive layout reconciliation

Move proactive sidebar resize/layout correction into the daemon,
which runs continuously and can repair stale layouts in inactive
windows without requiring the user to visit them.

Previously, the window-resized tmux hook only reflowed the single
target window, leaving other windows with stale sidebar widths until
the user navigated to them. Inactive sidebar TUI clients sleep for
long periods and were not responsible for layout repair.

Changes:
- Add reconcile_sidebar_layouts() in mod.rs: iterates all sidebar
  panes, checks current vs desired width per window, and reflows
  stale ones via the existing layout tree reflow
- Update window-resized hook to also signal the daemon (SIGUSR1)
  after the immediate per-window reflow, so the daemon picks up
  stale layouts in other windows
- Add client-resized hook that signals the daemon, catching resize
  events that don't trigger window-resized on every window
- Add periodic layout reconciliation (every 30s) in the daemon main
  loop, owned by the existing refresh cycle
- Reflow_after_sidebar_add is idempotent: calling it on an already
  correct layout applies the same layout via select-layout, so there
  is no layout thrashing or hook-recursion risk (window-layout-changed
  is not hooked)

The existing manual resize detection in sidebar TUI clients
(SidebarApp::process_pending_resize) continues to work: it calls
reflow_all_sidebars_except, which remains the path for propagating
user-initiated width changes to other windows.

sidebar: use tmux-reported pane width for manual resize sync

When a user manually resizes the sidebar pane, the detected width was
taken from crossterm's Event::Resize cols, which comes from SIGWINCH.
This can differ from what tmux reports as the actual pane width via
#{pane_width}, especially during border drags where the terminal emulator
and tmux may disagree on the final committed size.

Instead of using the raw crossterm value, query tmux for the canonical
pane width with display-message -p "#{pane_width}" after detecting a
manual resize.  This ensures the synced width is consistent with what
reflow_after_sidebar_add will produce when applying the same width to
other windows via select-layout.

sidebar: reflow all windows on resize instead of daemon reconciliation

Replace the daemon-side periodic layout reconciliation (30s sweep) with a
simpler approach: the window-resized hook now reflows ALL sidebar windows
instead of just the one that fired. This ensures inactive windows get their
sidebar widths corrected immediately on any resize event, without involving
the daemon or a background timer.

What changed:
- Add _sidebar-reflow-all hidden command that iterates all sidebar panes,
  scopes correctly, and reflows stale layouts
- window-resized hook now calls _sidebar-reflow-all instead of per-window
  reflow + daemon signal
- Remove the 30s daemon sweep, client-resized hook, and SIGUSR1 signaling
  from the resize path — all redundant now
- Keep the manual pane-width query fix in process_pending_resize (queries
  #{pane_width} instead of using raw crossterm cols)

sidebar: use tmux-reported pane width for manual resize detection too

The process_pending_resize comparison used crossterm's Event::Resize
cols value to decide whether a manual resize occurred.  During a pane
border drag, the kernel coalesces SIGWINCH signals, so a single event
can fire mid-drag with an intermediate width.  If that intermediate
value happens to be within 3 columns of the expected width, the
detection silently fails and the new width is never propagated.

Query #{pane_width} from tmux after the debounce period instead, when
the drag is guaranteed to be stable.  Use the same tmux-reported width
for both the comparison and the stored synced width, making the
detection consistent with the value that gets propagated.

sidebar: sync any tmux-reported manual resize

Manual sidebar drags could be ignored when the final tmux-reported pane
width differed from the expected width by three columns or fewer. Since
manual resize detection now queries tmux for the authoritative pane width,
any difference from the expected width should be treated as a real resize.

Increase the debounce window so drag updates settle before syncing the new
width to other sidebar windows.

isolate pi agent's bin/ directory in sandbox mounts

release v0.1.211

tests: share CWD_LOCK across modules to fix parallel race

The two tests verifying that workmux respects an explicit repo path
argument over the process cwd each defined their own private
`static CWD_LOCK: Mutex<()>`:

- src/git/worktree.rs::tests::create_worktree_in_uses_explicit_repo_not_process_cwd
- src/workflow/create.rs::tests::workflow_create_uses_explicit_repo_not_process_cwd

Because cargo runs tests in parallel by default, the two tests serialise
against *different* mutexes. Each calls `std::env::set_current_dir` on
the process-wide cwd, so when they run concurrently they race: the
workflow test's `set_current_dir(non_repo)` (".../not-a-repo") can land
while the worktree test is mid-assertion checking that cwd still equals
its own `repo_a`. That produces the failure seen on v0.1.211:

    assertion `left == right` failed
      left:  ".../.tmpHcehrO/not-a-repo"
      right: ".../.tmpcsa1oy/repo-a"

Move the lock to a new crate-wide `test_support` module (gated with
`#[cfg(test)]`) and have both test modules import it. Any future test
that mutates the process cwd must use the same lock.

Verified with 5x repeated runs of both tests at --test-threads=8: 0
failures. Full suite: 1199 passed.

use process state guard in tests

The shared cwd lock fixed the immediate parallel race, but tests still
restored process-global state manually. A panic before cleanup could leave
cwd or environment variables changed for the rest of the test process.

Replace the raw test lock with an RAII guard that serializes process-state
mutation, restores cwd on drop, and snapshots environment variables before
mutation. Migrate all tests that mutate cwd or process env through the
shared guard so future failures do not leak state across parallel tests.

avoid global process mutation in tests

The previous guard serialized cwd and environment mutation, but those globals
were still observable by concurrent test threads. Move the affected tests to
explicit seams instead: env-dependent logic now accepts deterministic inputs,
the close RPC test injects a connected client, and the hostile-cwd regression
checks run in isolated child processes.

This keeps coverage for explicit repo path handling while removing shared
process-state mutation from the parent test runner.

make pi skills test deterministic

The Pi skills directory test still read the real process environment, so a
user or CI setting for PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR could change the branch under test.
Use the explicit env seam added for the Claude override test so the expected
path is fixed and independent of the surrounding shell.

use canary for isolated test execution

The isolated test helper checked libtest summary text to detect stale test
filters. That made the helper depend on harness output wording instead of the
child test body itself.

Have child tests print an explicit canary and assert that marker in the parent
process so the helper verifies execution without parsing libtest summaries.

keep resolve name helper private

The close command is a child module, so it can call the parent helper without
widening visibility to the whole crate. Keep the helper private to avoid
exposing an internal parsing seam beyond the command module.

add reap-agents command

Provide a dry-run-first cleanup command for tracked agent panes that have
not reported state updates within the configured age threshold. The command
uses reconciled agent state, falls back to status timestamps when needed,
and removes agent state after successful forced pane exits.

Document the new command in the README and command reference so users know
that dry runs still reconcile stale workmux state.

keep panes when reaping agents

Reaping should stop the stale agent process without changing tmux layout.
Sending interrupt and EOF through the pane preserves the pane and only removes
workmux state after the foreground command exits.

Update the CLI and docs wording to describe process cleanup instead of pane
closure.

fix stale tmux windows on remove

Make remove detect self-cleanup from the command pane instead of the active
tmux client, then prefer stable tmux IDs when closing deferred targets. This
prevents an external remove from being mistaken for a self-remove and avoids
name-based target misses that could delete the worktree while leaving the
window alive.

Update remove tests so from-window cases execute inside the target pane and
wait for the deferred cleanup result before asserting filesystem state.

resurrect: preserve agent override

Resurrect rebuilt crashed worktrees with the current default agent instead of
using the agent that originally ran in the stale pane state. A worktree
created with a non-default agent like Codex could therefore come back as
Claude and receive Claude-specific resume arguments.

Store a validated remembered agent on resurrect candidates and pass it through
workflow::open to pane setup. Prefer cached agent kinds, fall back only to
known agent profiles, and choose deterministically when multiple stale panes
match the same worktree.

Oh My Pi supports PI_CONFIG_DIR and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR for users who keep agent state outside the default ~/.omp/agent tree. Use unique temp filenames for atomic state writes (#188)

* Use unique temp filenames for atomic state writes

The shared `.json.tmp` path meant concurrent status writes for the same
pane could clobber each other's temp file before the atomic rename. Give
each writer a unique temp filename (pid + nanos) so only the rename is
shared, and relax the test assertion to catch any leftover `.tmp` suffix.

* use shared atomic write helper

The state write fix needs a temp file strategy that is unique across
concurrent writers and consistent across every atomic write path. The pid and
clock based name still allows same-process collisions on systems with coarse
clock resolution, and each copied helper needs the same cleanup behavior.

This adds a shared write_atomic helper backed by tempfile so temp names are
created exclusively in the target directory. The helper removes stale temp
files matching its target-specific prefix, writes and flushes the content, and
persists the temp file over the target. Agent state, Codex status, run result,
and GitHub PR cache writes all use the shared helper.

The focused tests cover target replacement, temp cleanup after successful
writes, and preservation of fresh temp files.

fix sandbox tests with isolated state roots

The Nix build sandbox exposes host paths with restricted write access, so unit
tests that exercise Pi sandbox mounts can fail while building their expected
argument lists. Those tests only need deterministic mount sources, not the
user's real XDG state tree or agent config directories.

Add test-only entry points for container and Lima mount generation that accept a
state root supplied by the test. The affected Pi and OMP tests use temporary
agent config and state directories, keeping their filesystem writes inside the
test tempdir while preserving the production path resolution behavior.

isolate git-backed tests from ambient environment

Git subprocesses used by sandbox git config injection and project config
lookup now clear ambient git repository and config variables before reading
the target path. This keeps inherited GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, and
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT values from redirecting lookups away from the temp repos
created by tests.

The test helpers use the same sanitized environment for repo setup, and the
project config tests compare canonical paths so macOS temp path aliases do not
make exact path assertions fail.

clear git hook environment before checks

Git exports repository-local environment variables while running hooks. The
pre-commit hook runs the full check suite, and unit tests create temporary Git
repositories with their own local config. Inherited GIT_DIR and related values
can redirect those subprocesses back to the real repository config, causing
config lock contention and test identities to leak into commits.

Capture the repository root first, clear Git's local environment variables, and
run the checks from the repository root so subprocesses discover the intended
repository from their working directory.

fix lima mount tests without user home

missing, so Lima guest home resolution falls back to the configured agent path.
The Pi and OMP mount tests asserted hard-coded guest suffixes and missed the
mounts in that environment.

Look up the configured parent mount by host path, then compare overlay paths
relative to the resolved guest path. This keeps the tests focused on mount
ordering and overlay behavior without depending on ambient user environment.

wake sidebar daemon on navigation signals

Sidebar navigation sends SIGUSR1 after switching the tmux client, but the
sidebar daemon only observed that signal on its 100 ms polling cycle. This made

while rapid signals remain coalesced by the bounded channel and existing 50 ms
refresh debounce. Closing the signal handle also preserves clean daemon
shutdown without periodic signal polling.

* fix: relax zellij stacked pane focus

* remove duplicate sidebar width tests

A merge left three sidebar width test functions defined twice in the same
module, preventing Rust test targets and clippy from compiling.

Keep one copy of each assertion so the existing coverage remains intact and
the full repository check suite can run successfully.

* fix zellij status hooks with stripped environments

Agent hook runners can omit Zellij's pane and session variables. Cwd-based
recovery is ambiguous whenever an agent shares its worktree with auxiliary
panes, which causes status updates to disappear.

Attach a Workmux-owned backend, session, and pane identity to each Zellij
agent command. Status hooks validate and use that exact target before any
heuristic fallback. Bind Zellij backend commands to the recorded session so
state uses the correct instance and remains reliable with multiple sessions.

Malformed or stale explicit targets fail closed and emit a warning instead of
updating an unrelated pane. Existing cwd resolution remains available for
agents launched without the identity variables.

* fix concurrent zellij pane recovery

Zellij can return empty stdout for command-bearing pane creation. Recovery
previously selected the highest new terminal pane ID, which could bind pane
commands and names to an unrelated pane created concurrently in the same tab.

Match new panes against the unique handshake command when stdout lacks an ID.
Use the sole new pane only when recovery is otherwise unambiguous, and fail
closed when multiple candidates cannot be distinguished.

Retry transient malformed or empty JSON from list-tabs and list-panes so brief
successful commands without output do not abort worktree creation. The retry
remains bounded to five attempts with short delays.

* fix zellij pane focus fallback

Stacked layout creation can tolerate targeted focus failures, but final pane
selection still depended on current-tab-info. When targeted focus was
unavailable, that query could provide no focused tab and fail the completed
layout.

Resolve the target pane's tab directly from list-panes, switch to that tab,
and navigate from its recorded focused pane. This keeps the fallback bound to
the requested pane even when another tab also reports a focused pane.

fix sidebar daemon idle cpu loop

The PR worker woke the sidebar daemon every time it received an empty path
list, even when its published cache was already empty. Each wake triggered a
full refresh after 50 ms, which fed another empty list back to the worker and
kept the daemon refreshing continuously while idle.

This preserves the refresh needed for a nonempty-to-empty transition while
repeated empty inputs remain idle. Add coverage for empty, populated, and
repeated cache clears.

show codex permission prompts as waiting

Codex supports PermissionRequest hooks, but the embedded workmux hook config
predated that event and the nested-run aggregator collapsed waiting updates to
working. Permission prompts therefore stayed indistinguishable from active
work.

Install a waiting hook for PermissionRequest and track waiting run IDs alongside
active runs so user attention takes precedence without allowing subagent events
to erase it. Treat legacy hook sets as incomplete so setup can merge the missing
hook while preserving user configuration.

Update the status documentation and cover hook upgrades, payload detection,
concurrent run behavior, runtime persistence, and old runtime-state decoding.
There are no breaking configuration changes.

add automatic base branch configuration

Allow base_branch to use the reserved auto value so a global configuration can
start independent worktrees from each repository's effective main branch. This
avoids accidentally stacking unrelated work on the currently checked out
feature branch while preserving current-branch creation when the option is
omitted.

Resolve auto through the same configured main_branch and local Git default
branch detection used by workflow contexts. Apply the resolved branch in both
the CLI and dashboard paths, preserve explicit --base and remote checkout
precedence, and store the concrete branch in workmux metadata.

Document that detection uses local Git state without fetching. Add coverage for
configured and detected main branches, global config, CLI precedence, dry-run
output, dashboard creation, and resolved base metadata. Existing literal and
current-branch behavior remains unchanged.
release v0.1.228

Kata containers backend (#198)

* feat(sandbox) - add oci_runtime passthrough for container backend

Let the container sandbox backend run under an alternative OCI runtime via
`docker`/`podman run --runtime <x>`, selected with a new
`sandbox.container.oci_runtime` option. Unset keeps the runtime default
(runc), so existing behavior is unchanged. Pointing it at a VM-based runtime
such as Kata Containers gives each sandbox a hardware-VM boundary while
reusing the entire tested container path (image, mounts, user mapping, RPC).

The flag is threaded into `build_docker_run_args` immediately after the `run`
subcommand, so both agent panes and `workmux sandbox shell` pick it up. Like
`devices`/`group_add`, `oci_runtime` is global-only: it changes the isolation
boundary, so a project `.workmux.yaml` cannot set (or downgrade) it and a
warning is emitted if it tries.

No new SandboxBackend variant and no supervisor/multiplexer changes.

* feat(sandbox) - add container.cap_add and security_opt passthroughs

Global-only, default empty (no behavior change when unset). Emits
docker/podman run --cap-add / --security-opt.

Enables docker-in-docker under the kata oci_runtime without --privileged,
which fails on kata (injects host device nodes that collide with the
guest's: 'Creating container device /dev/full EEXIST'). Granting caps +
security_opt instead boots cleanly and keeps the daemon confined to the VM.

* fix(sandbox) - skip oci_runtime and security opts on apple container

Address PR #198 review feedback.

build_docker_run_args_inner emitted `--runtime`, `--cap-add`, and
`--security-opt` before the outer runtime was known, so a global
`oci_runtime: kata` (or cap/security opts) produced
`container run --runtime kata ...` on macOS, where Apple Container is
auto-preferred. Apple Container misreads these Docker/Podman flags and
fails to start the sandbox, contradicting the docs that promised the
setting is ignored there.

Compute the runtime first and skip these Docker/Podman-only flags on
Apple Container, matching the documented "ignored" behavior and letting a
single global config target Kata on a Docker host while still running on
macOS.

Docs: correct the unset default (engine default -- runc on Docker, crun
on Podman -- not a hardcoded runc), make the Kata example Docker-first,
and note Kata does not officially support Podman.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EvyFzQAKuwhy1DUPLdTBd2

* fix container runtime compatibility guidance

Remote Podman clients do not expose the local engine's --runtime flag, so
configured OCI runtime overrides failed with an opaque unknown-flag error.
Reject known remote Podman environments with an actionable message while
preserving support for local Podman on Linux.

Describe unset OCI runtime behavior as deferring to the engine's configured
default in both generated and source documentation. Document cap_add and
security_opt syntax, runtime support, global-only scope, and the isolation
impact of permissive values used without a VM-based runtime.
