release v0.1.229

run full checks on every branch

Run the complete checkle group and the tmux-backed Python integration suite in separate GitHub Actions jobs. Every branch push gets coverage for formatting, linting, unit tests, type checks, documentation, and integration behavior. Pull request events provide the same checks for contributions from forks, and manual dispatch supports selected-branch reruns.\n\nExpose the Python virtual environment tools to checkle, make the fork fixture create its main branch independently of Git's global defaults, and detach the session-removal helper from pane hangups so CI can reliably capture its result.

prevent merge from deleting main worktree

Merging a branch checked out in the main worktree could pass the root
repository path into shared cleanup. Cleanup then renamed the repository and,
inside a matching multiplexer target, permanently deleted the renamed path.

Centralize canonical main-worktree detection in WorkflowContext. Reject the
main worktree as a merge source before merge side effects, and enforce the same
invariant inside cleanup as protection for every caller. The remove workflow
uses the shared check while retaining its existing behavior.

Add regression coverage for implicit and explicit source resolution, --keep,
linked-worktree invocation, path aliases, and missing-path comparisons. Root
worktree merges are rejected even when cleanup would otherwise be skipped.
release v0.1.230

refresh sidebar after acknowledging agent status

Window selection can signal the sidebar daemon before tmux runs the queued
pane-focus hook. The daemon may then publish the completed or waiting state
while tmux clears only the status-bar marker.

Signal the sidebar daemon from the pane-focus hook after both pane and window
status options are handled. This makes status acknowledgement and sidebar
refresh follow the same ordered command sequence for every focus path.

Add regression coverage for the generated hook command and its ordering.
release v0.1.231

improve dashboard selection and elapsed time

Make the selected row easier to locate by replacing the chevron with a
theme-colored accent bar in both dashboard views.

Keep elapsed time in the familiar HH:MM:SS format while coloring it by age.
Dim zero-valued hours and minutes so the active clock units carry more visual
weight without changing the table layout or keyboard behavior.

Document the time treatment and cover its age colors and unit emphasis with
focused tests.

show branch checks in status views

Status check data was coupled to pull request summaries, leaving branches
without a pull request unable to populate sidebar and dashboard check
indicators. This made check visibility depend on PR creation rather than the
branch commit itself.

Query branch refs alongside pull requests in a batched GraphQL request and
carry checks through dedicated caches and status fields. Prefer PR checks when
available, then fall back to the remote branch tip. Main and master branches
show failures while successful and pending checks stay hidden.

Keep daemon polling bounded to one batched status request per active repository
every 30 seconds, with an immediate refresh only when its branch set changes.
Group linked worktrees by their shared git directory and cache repository
resolution once per process to avoid duplicate GitHub calls.

Render the same checks in sidebar and dashboard views, and include the indicator
in the default tile and horizontal templates. Local-only and unpushed branches
leave the check indicator empty.

add mouse support to dashboard

Make dashboard controls usable with direct pointer interactions while
preserving all existing keyboard navigation. Rows, tabs, preview scrolling, diff
file navigation, and visible footer commands route mouse events to the same app
actions used by keybindings. Agent and worktree rows expose contextual actions
through right-click menus that support pointer and keyboard selection.

Track the rendered terminal area for accurate hit testing and keep routing
logic separate from rendering and application state. Add focused tests for
mouse event routing, hit regions, bounded scrolling, double-click activation,
context menus, footer actions, diff navigation, and balanced terminal control
sequences.

Guard terminal setup with cleanup that disables mouse capture, bracketed
paste, raw mode, and the alternate screen on normal and error exits. Document
mouse controls in the README and dashboard guide. This introduces no breaking
keyboard behavior.

run integration tests across supported shells

The Python integration suite discovers installed shells and parametrizes shell-
specific cases accordingly. GitHub's Ubuntu runner only exposed bash, leaving
zsh, fish, and Nushell behavior outside the CI suite even though local developer
machines commonly exercise those variants.

Install zsh and fish from Ubuntu packages and provision a pinned Nushell release
before running the integration tests. This makes CI exercise the same four-shell
matrix used on fully configured development machines.

prevent zsh completion prompt in integration tests

Ubuntu's global zsh configuration runs compinit when an interactive shell
starts. GitHub's runner contains completion directories that compaudit considers
insecure, so zsh prompts for confirmation and consumes commands sent by the test
harness before they reach the shell.

Remove group and world write permissions from the directories reported by
compaudit after installing zsh. This keeps startup noninteractive and allows the
zsh variants to exercise the intended commands.

add GitHub-hosted binary installation

Release builds can consume substantial CPU and battery when installed from a
working tree. Add an install-ci recipe that pushes the current committed branch
without running the local pre-push gate, dispatches a read-only GitHub Actions
build for its exact commit, and installs the verified artifact atomically.

The helper rejects dirty and detached working trees, follows the exact workflow
run returned by GitHub, and validates the artifact commit and checksum. The
dedicated workflow builds only the Apple silicon binary and retains its artifact
for one day.

reduce CI installation progress noise

GitHub CLI's default watch display redraws every build step on each polling
interval, producing excessive terminal output during a release build. Use its
compact display and a ten-second interval while retaining live status and
failure propagation.

fix dashboard session scope in tmux popups

Tmux popups can carry pane environment context that differs from the attached
client's active session. The dashboard used that pane context as its launch
identity, causing session scope to select the wrong agents or skip filtering
when the pane could not be resolved.

Resolve dashboard scope from the active client's session, with pane-based
identity as a fallback for contexts without client information. Session scope
also fails closed when session identity is unavailable instead of exposing all
agents.

Add focused coverage for unrelated projects, grouped worktree paths, stale
agent records, missing session identity, all scope, and scope cycling.

dim long-running dashboard times

Reduce the visual weight of elapsed times after one hour while retaining the
accent hue that distinguishes long-running agents from fresh and intermediate
states.

Apply the DIM modifier to the accent style at the one-hour boundary and extend
the color progression test to verify both the hue and modifier.
release v0.1.232

readme: clarify aven description

Use aven's canonical audience description in the promotional callout. The
shorter wording describes both human and agent users without an unnecessary
terminal qualifier.
remove disable-model-invocation from coordinator skill

preserve agent state on uncertain tmux pane queries

Individual tmux pane lookups treated every display-message failure as proof
that the pane was absent. Reconciliation could therefore delete recoverable
agent state after a transient command failure or malformed response.

Classify failed lookups with a structured list-panes query that checks exact
pane identifiers. Return absence only when that query succeeds and omits the
target. Propagate errors when the pane remains present, confirmation fails, or
either response is malformed, so reconciliation cannot use uncertainty as a
deletion trigger.

Document the existing Result<Option<_>> contract and cover successful lookup,
confirmed absence, transient failures, failed confirmation, and malformed
output with focused unit tests.

GitHub issue: #209

add agent identity to status json

Status JSON rows previously exposed worktree context and pane IDs but omitted
reconciled agent identity, which made multiple agents in one worktree difficult
to attribute reliably.

Include each agent's working directory, kind, session, window name, and last
update timestamp while preserving the top-level array and human-readable table.
Represent unavailable optional identity values as null so consumers receive a
stable additive schema.

Cover both unfiltered and filtered construction paths, optional agent kinds,
and attribution of two agents sharing one worktree in integration tests.

Refs #210.

preserve valid auto-generated branch names

Auto-name output passed through a slugifier that flattened slash-separated Git
branch prefixes. This made generated names behave differently from equivalent
explicit branch names.

Validate cleaned generator output with Git and preserve it when it already
forms a valid branch name. Invalid output retains the existing slug fallback.
Generated names always identify local branches so a prefix matching a remote
cannot change their meaning.

Add unit and dry-run integration coverage for nested slash names, invalid refs,
and remote-like prefixes. Document that valid generated Git names are
preserved.

Issue: #206
release v0.1.233

handle generators that close stdin early

Custom auto-name commands may produce output and exit without reading the prompt
from stdin. Writing the prompt then returns a broken-pipe error even though the
command completed successfully and provided a valid branch name.

Treat broken pipe as an expected closed-input condition, then collect and
validate the command's exit status and output as usual. Apply the same handling
to the built-in llm subprocess path and add regression coverage with a command
that exits immediately.

skill: single idempotent form for cross-project session setup

The cross-project worktree section gave two separate snippets, one for when
the target tmux session exists and one for when it does not, which forces
the caller to check first. `tmux new-session -d` exits non-zero on an
existing session, so discarding that failure collapses both cases into one
pair of commands that is safe to run either way.

Also note that workmux commands resolve the current git repo, since a
dispatcher's working directory is often outside the target project and
every subcommand fails there.

fix stale tmux pane reconciliation

Tmux reports a successful display-message query with empty pane fields when the
target pane no longer exists. Treating that response as malformed prevented
reconciliation from deleting stale agent state and caused one orphaned file to
abort every agent view.

Send successful but unparseable pane responses through the existing list-panes
confirmation path. Confirmed absence returns no live pane, while malformed
responses for panes that remain listed and failed confirmations still preserve
the original error. Add focused tests for each outcome.

document direct parent session dispatch

Add the existing parent-session and target-name flags to the workmux skill
reference. Replace temporary tmux bootstrap windows in both dispatch skills
with direct workmux invocation from the target repository.

Workmux already creates a missing parent session and its managed window, so
the previous cross-project guidance added an unnecessary intermediate window
and obscured the actual workmux result.

preserve explicit parent session names

Explicit parent tmux sessions are identifiers supplied by the caller, but add
and open passed them through the target-name slugifier. Mixed-case sessions
therefore resolved to a different lowercase name, which could create an
unintended session and persist incorrect lifecycle metadata.

Validate parent sessions separately and return valid names unchanged. Reject
empty names, control characters, target separators, and tmux exact-target or
session-ID prefixes while retaining target-name and worktree normalization.

Cover add and open against existing mixed-case sessions, verify exact metadata
persistence and normalized target names, and confirm missing mixed-case parent
sessions are created and reused with their requested spelling.

sidebar: add {window_index} template token

Shows the tmux window number (e.g. 3 for 3:wm-feature-auth) in sidebar
rows, so the displayed number matches native tmux navigation (prefix+N,
status bar) instead of the sidebar-order {idx}.

The index is read from the daemon's existing list-panes poll as a
trailing format field and stamped onto agents in build_snapshot,
mirroring window_id. It refreshes every tick, so renumbered or moved
windows stay accurate. Backends without window indexes render it
empty.

sidebar: add sort config option (recency|window)

'window' orders rows by session and tmux window index, keeping the
list stable while agents work and matching the tmux window list.
Pairs with {window_index}. Default remains 'recency'.

sidebar: ignore Access events in config watcher

On Linux the notify backend also reports reads (open/access/close) of
watched files, and a config reload reads the very file being watched:
every reload scheduled the next one, bumping config_version and
re-rendering every sidebar client once per debounce interval (5/s),
forever. Filter out EventKind::Access so only mutations (create,
modify, remove, rename) trigger a reload.

filter filesystem access events at the source

The config watcher still allowed ignored access events to fill its bounded
channel and trigger reloads through overflow. The git status watcher also
subscribed to read events, so each status refresh could schedule another one
without producing a visible sidebar update.

Configure both mutation-driven watchers with notify's CORE event mask and
filter irrelevant config events before enqueueing them. Preserve rescan events
as reload signals because their path lists may be incomplete.

Cover the Linux access event shapes, atomic rename paths, rescan recovery, and
the shared watcher mask in regression tests.
release v0.1.234

use stable tmux window identities for teardown

Tmux window names can change after creation, which allowed cleanup to leave
renamed windows behind or kill an unrelated window that reused the expected
name.

Assign each worktree a persistent random window token and attach it to every
tmux window at creation time. Resolve those owned windows to stable tmux IDs
for close, remove, duplicate cleanup, mode conversion, dashboard operations,
and deferred teardown. Primary and duplicate markers preserve existing close
semantics, while exact-name matching remains the compatibility path for
legacy windows and other multiplexer backends.

Add integration coverage for explicit renames, name reuse, self-close,
renamed parent sessions, and renamed duplicate cleanup.

fix sidebar redraw after terminal resize

Tmux can reflow a sidebar pane during resize and change the visible terminal
contents behind ratatui's back. Ratatui then emits only its buffered diff,
leaving fragments of the previous layout mixed into the current rows.

Clear the terminal whenever crossterm reports a resize so ratatui resets its
back buffer and paints every cell. Keep ordinary snapshot and spinner updates
incremental, and cover the resize redraw request with a unit test.

fix sidebar self-exit pane targeting

Sidebar last-pane cleanup resolved its kill target from tmux's active pane,
which could terminate unrelated user processes when focus was in another
window. Snapshot pane counts could also trigger cleanup without validating
live tmux state.

Capture the sidebar pane, window, and session identities through an explicit
tmux target at startup. Use those stable identities for silent pane cleanup
and global shutdown bookkeeping. Confirm last-pane snapshots with a targeted
live pane query, and fail closed when the sidebar cannot prove it is the sole
pane in its host window.

Add regression coverage for identity parsing, exact kill command targeting,
and sole-pane validation.
release v0.1.235

fix status updates when hook pane environment is missing

Claude Code background sessions can invoke status hooks without TMUX_PANE.
The cwd fallback rejected the update whenever agent, shell, and sidebar panes
shared the same working directory, leaving an active agent with a stale idle
time in the sidebar.

Use persisted agent registration to disambiguate equally close cwd matches.
The fallback remains conservative when multiple registered agents share the
same path, so an ambiguous hook cannot update the wrong pane.

fix: animate agent status in Zellij tabs (#220)

* fix: update agent status in Zellij tabs

* docs: preserve Zellij source-build warning

* fix: animate Zellij working status

* use static agent icons in Zellij tabs

Zellij status animation required a background process per working tab and
continuously spawned CLI commands to read and rename tabs. This imposed
substantial process, IPC, redraw, and lifecycle overhead for a cosmetic effect.

Render the configured working, waiting, and done icons when status hooks fire,
matching tmux behavior. Keep stable tab-ID targeting, marker-based suffix
replacement, tmux style stripping, and canonical tab-name handling. Remove the
spinner command, runtime state, socket validation, and animation process.

Zellij waiting and done icons remain visible until the next status update
because Zellij does not provide an equivalent to tmux's focus hook.

reject ambiguous tmux window placement

Window-mode creation silently delegated to tmux when TMUX_PANE was absent or
stale. On servers with multiple attached sessions, tmux could then choose the
session of another client, placing a worktree window outside the project session
selected by the coordinator.

Resolve placement through the invoking pane when it is live. A server with one
session remains a deterministic fallback, while multiple sessions produce an
actionable error before any worktree state is created. Explicit parent-session
targets bypass inference and remain authoritative.

Cover both window placement modes, the single-session fallback, ambiguous
multi-session rejection, and explicit targeting. Document that repository
selection and tmux placement are independent and recommend explicit targets for
background coordinator dispatch.

docs: align add options table

Keep the add command reference table aligned after documenting deterministic
tmux parent-session targeting.

coordinator: require explicit parent sessions

Coordinator subprocesses may lack TMUX_PANE even when their working directory
belongs to a specific project. Without an explicit target, that makes tmux
window placement ambiguous on servers with multiple sessions.

Teach every spawn example and the coordinator rules to pass --parent-session.
Also clarify that repository selection and tmux placement are independent and
that coordinators should ask when the intended session is unknown.

coordinator: retry ambiguous spawns explicitly

Most coordinator spawns have enough pane context for workmux to select their
tmux session automatically. Requiring an explicit parent on every command asks
the coordinator to know information that may not be available.

Restore the concise default spawn commands. When workmux rejects ambiguous
placement, direct the coordinator to retry with a known parent session or ask
for one rather than guessing.

infer tmux session from matching pane paths

Background agent commands can lose TMUX_PANE even when a live pane in the
project identifies the intended tmux session. Requiring an explicit parent in
that common case is safe but unnecessarily interrupts coordinator dispatch.

Before falling back to a sole server session or reporting ambiguity, compare the
command cwd with live pane paths. Accept only the closest matches when they all
belong to one session. Keep rejecting ties across sessions, and preserve
explicit parent-session authority.

Cover closest-ancestor scoring, multiple panes in one session, ambiguous session
ties, both placement modes, and isolated multi-session creation. Document the
complete resolution order for add and open.

simplify codex subagent status hooks

Codex dispatches dedicated SubagentStop events for thread-spawned children,
so child completion can keep the pane working while the root-only Stop event
marks it done. This removes the per-pane run aggregation and payload inference
that guarded against child Stop events ending the shared pane status early.

Configure SubagentStop as working and retain Stop as done. Setup normalizes
existing workmux SubagentStop commands so repeated installation remains
idempotent and preserves unrelated user hooks.

This relies on the SubagentStop interface available since Codex 0.133.0.
release v0.1.236

docs: reuse hero screenshot in guide

Use the homepage screenshot in the guide introduction so the primary workflow
image includes the agent sidebar. Reposition the worktree callout for the
shared image and remove the unused older screenshot asset.

make status json observations self-describing

A bare empty array could represent a genuinely empty tracked-agent set, a
backend or instance mismatch, or agents removed by repository scoping. This
left unattended consumers unable to distinguish completion from an incomplete
observation.

Return a versioned envelope with context, scope, state-file census values,
target errors, and the pre-scope reconciled agent count. Keep observation
read-only, preserve invalid evidence, and fail closed when backend, instance,
multiplexer, repository, state, or requested Git evidence cannot be trusted.

Frame and validate strict tmux snapshots without changing tolerant legacy
callers. Support fleet queries outside Git, bare repositories, empty targets,
and partial multi-target results while retaining a nonzero exit for incomplete
requests.

Document the breaking JSON shape, recovery behavior, and the limitation that
agents without tracking state remain invisible.

drop unresolved global list placeholders

A project-level <global> entry reached hook execution when the matching global
list was absent. Shells interpreted the token as redirection syntax, causing
create, merge, and remove operations to fail instead of running project hooks.

Resolve placeholders against an empty list when no global value exists while
preserving project entries and ordering. Add merge-level coverage for every
supported list, integration coverage for post-create and pre-remove hooks, and
document hook inheritance consistently.

accept escaped tmux pane separators

Ubuntu's tmux emits control separators from format strings as octal escape
sequences. The strict pane snapshot parser treated the resulting rows as
malformed, which broke status and agent-state integration tests in CI.

Recognize both raw control separators and their octal-escaped forms while
retaining the tab-delimited fallback used by tolerant callers.

changelog: reference status json issue

Link the Unreleased status JSON observation entry to issue #210 so readers can
find the original automation requirements and remaining resurrection scope.
release v0.1.237

remove status json schema version

The status JSON envelope is the command's direct output contract and does not
need a separate schema version field. Keeping it unversioned matches the chosen
interface and avoids implying support for parallel versioned formats.
release v0.1.238

migrate documentation to Astro Starlight

Replace the VitePress documentation stack with Astro 7 and Starlight while
preserving the guide, command reference, and changelog route hierarchy. This
keeps the public documentation stable while using a maintained content and
search pipeline.

canonical links, asides, tabs, and a root changelog symlink. Rebuild the custom
homepage as scoped Astro components, add responsive image generation, and port
accessible image zoom and progressive video controls.

Add Pagefind search, source-verified llms.txt generation, raw Markdown routes,
and progressively enhanced copy-page links. The build validates links, hashes,
content conventions, formatting, and Astro types.

Adopt Bun for local and CI documentation tooling and update the GitHub Pages
workflow to publish the Astro output. Canonical documentation URLs use trailing
slashes, and search uses the generated Pagefind index instead of Algolia.

docs: add homepage documentation link

The Starlight splash page did not expose the documentation navigation at
mobile widths because its header has no sidebar menu and hides the shared

Add a Docs link to the shared header links and expose that group on splash

menu, while hiding it in the constrained splash header. Tighten mobile
spacing and preserve the theme selector as an accessible compact control so
the logo, search, Docs link, and theme picker fit at narrow widths.

Documentation pages retain their existing sidebar and responsive menu
behavior. The change does not alter documentation routes or content.

restore homepage visual parity

Restore the compact pre-migration homepage presentation so the Starlight
migration retains the site's established character instead of using an

Match the VitePress typography, text colors, content width, section rhythm,
responsive gutters, icons, copy density, terminal framing, testimonials, and

Grotesk for display text and self-host the matching Inter roman and italic

Keep the Starlight header and navigation, responsive Astro images, accessible
headings and media descriptions, keyboard focus styles, dark theme behavior,
and contrast-safe controls. Desktop and mobile layouts keep the headline within
the viewport and avoid horizontal scrolling.

fix homepage text layout

Astro trims template whitespace around inline elements, which joined several

Remove the remote display font that swapped in after initial rendering and

remove sidebar new badge

The sidebar feature is established documentation, so the navigation badge adds

Starlight appends each content entry path to the edit URL base. Point the base

Give the homepage heading the target expected by Starlight's skip link. This

fix homepage media and changelog output

Enable accessible image zoom for the homepage hero and dashboard screenshots
while keeping zoom wrappers flush inside terminal frames. Load the hero image

The root changelog contains Starlight frontmatter instead of a body title.
Reconstruct the standalone heading for CLI output without exposing site

center terminal window titles

The inherited line height made the title text sit low within terminal window

crop hero screenshot edge padding

The source terminal capture contains dark edge rows that read as empty space

Keep the crop stable before and after the zoom enhancement wraps the image so

fix documentation screenshot framing

Image zoom inserts a button around documentation screenshots. Reset that

Restore the homepage image without cropping. The reported spacing belonged to

remove screenshot frame gap

Starlight's content flow adds a top margin between sibling elements, including

The Pages build requested Bun 1.4.0, which has no published release and caused

detect outdated agent extensions

Status setup treated any existing Pi or Oh My Pi extension file as configured,

replace stale implementations. Cover matching, outdated, and absent extension
states with focused tests.
fix OpenCode subagent status aggregation

GitHub issue #239 reports that Kitty pane layouts always use the backend's

command. This makes layouts that produce equal panes in tmux render unevenly in

build the pane-focus hook from constants

The auto-clear hook body no longer carries the status icon. The icon reaches
tmux only as an option value, which tmux does not re-expand as a command,
matching how the same value is already passed as a discrete argument to
`set-option`.

The hook compares the window status against `@workmux_ack_status`, a pane
option holding the icon awaiting acknowledgement. It is set only for
statuses that clear on focus and unset for the rest, so a hook left
installed by an earlier `waiting` status does not acknowledge a later
`working` status. The option is tested for emptiness rather than truth,
because tmux treats the literal "0" as false and that is a usable icon.

The tests set `status_icons` through project config and check the installed
hook body. The test tmux server has no attached client, so tmux never
delivers pane-focus-in; the tests source the hook body against the pane
instead, which evaluates the same command string with the same pane-scoped
formats.

Sessions started before an upgrade keep installing the hook shape they were
built with, so they need restarting to pick this up.

harden git metadata sandbox boundaries

Sandbox guests could modify shared Git configuration and arrange for later

The frozen loader fails closed for missing or malformed snapshots and bypasses

This keeps ordinary host commands on the existing live config behavior. New

add codex support to `workmux add --fork`

Conversation forking previously only worked with Claude Code, so
`workmux add --fork` with `agent: codex` failed with "Agent 'codex' does
not support conversation forking". Codex forks conversations natively,
so the same interface can drive it.

Workmux resolves the session to fork before creating the worktree, then
launches `codex fork -C <worktree> <session-id>` there. Both details
matter:

- Resolving first, rather than deferring to `codex fork --last`, because
  `--last` filters candidate sessions by the working directory it runs
  in. Pointed at a fresh worktree it finds nothing and silently starts an
  empty conversation.
- `-C <worktree>`, because Codex otherwise asks whether to run the fork
  in the directory the parent session recorded or the current one, and
  defaults to the parent. Accepting that default would put the forked
  agent back in the repository the fork was started from.

Session resolution reads Codex's rollout store under
`$CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<timestamp>-<uuid>.jsonl`:

- Bare `--fork` prefers `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, which Codex exports into the
  commands it runs, and otherwise picks the most recently modified
  rollout recorded for the current worktree.
- Only `cli` and `vscode` sessions are candidates. `exec`, subagent, and
  other internal sources are recorded but cannot be forked.
- `--fork=<id>` matches an exact session ID or an unambiguous prefix, and
  reports the candidates when a prefix is ambiguous.

Codex writes the forked conversation itself, so the parent rollout is
left untouched. The forker trait method is now `prepare_fork`, since
copying transcripts is specific to agents without cross-project resume,
and `resume_args` takes the worktree the agent will run in.

fix deny-mode proxy connection exhaustion

The HTTP CONNECT proxy inherited the RPC server's 16-connection ceiling even
though pooled HTTPS tunnels stay open for their full TCP lifetime. Once the
ceiling was reached, accepted sockets closed without an HTTP response, making
proxy saturation appear as remote TLS and connection failures.

Give the proxy a configurable global-only connection limit with a default of
128, and return a complete HTTP 503 response when capacity is unavailable.
Use RAII permits so handler failures cannot leak slots, enforce bounded request
reads with an absolute handshake deadline, and reduce each tunnel from three
threads to two.

The new network.max_connections setting accepts values from 1 through 1024.
Over-capacity clients receive an explicit proxy error instead of an empty
response.

fix detached shell argument transport

The shared Kitty, WezTerm, and Zellij detached runner embedded a shell script

escape tmux run-shell format input

Tmux expands format expressions in run-shell arguments before invoking the
shell. Literal format text in generated commands could therefore change or
start a tmux format job.

restores the original script. Exercise a real isolated tmux server to verify

protect deferred git cleanup

Start deferred cleanup from the trusted running Workmux image before target
teardown and pass structured arguments directly to the hidden worker. The
worker waits for the captured target identity to disappear, then uses
repository-scoped protected Git constructors so host-side prune, branch
deletion, and metadata operations suppress repository hooks.

Capture filesystem and repository identity before teardown. Reject symlinks,
non-directories, and substituted worktrees before cleanup, quarantine the
validated directory, verify it after rename, and remove it with the standard
recursive filesystem primitive. Missing worktree paths receive synchronous
protected Git cleanup.

Report scheduled cleanup separately from completed cleanup, persist detached
worker errors, propagate lock and metadata failures, and preserve successful
merge results when later cleanup or close scheduling fails. Carry scheduled
state through merge, bulk removal, and dashboard handling.

Cover hook suppression, target substitution, hostile arguments, stable target
IDs, timeout and partial failure reporting, missing paths, force and

fix sidebar git worker path resolution

reduce redundant sidebar broadcasts

The daemon sent a complete snapshot to every sidebar client on each refresh,
even when only cache freshness changed. At large client counts this forced

Cache the latest typed snapshot and framed payload, compare every snapshot
field using sidebar-visible Git semantics, and suppress unchanged publication.
Exhaustive destructuring and derived agent equality make snapshot evolution
fail loudly when comparison coverage needs attention.

Order acceptance against publication with a generation check so each client
either joins a broadcast or receives the corresponding cached generation.
Keep bounded socket writes outside the shared lock, reap closed or malformed
clients, and block in accept instead of polling the listener every 50 ms.

cache-timestamp churn and associated cloning.

and malformed clients.

reduce idle sidebar git refreshes

keeps independent missed-event recovery while spreading verification across
roots, and Linux retains its full polling fallback.

Track watch completeness so partial registration keeps polling and retrying.
Coalesce overflow and rescan recovery, bound noisy roots with a refresh floor,
and fall back to polling after watcher errors. Cache repository resolution and
project root status onto nested or shared agent paths so focus, recency, and
membership changes avoid unrelated Git subprocesses.

and keep cache pruning and shutdown behavior intact.

decouple sidebar refresh scheduling

The daemon previously treated every worker wakeup and tmux event as a complete
refresh. That coupled cached Git, GitHub, and config publication to an expensive
all-pane observation and to inactivity captures, while observation failures also
skipped heartbeat and maintenance work.

Give observation, pane capture, publication, runtime heartbeat, and maintenance
independent deadlines. Keep startup and periodic observations immediate and at
two-second intervals, coalesce external events for 50 ms, and keep captures on
their own fixed two-second cadence. Worker and config changes build snapshots
from the last reconciled inventory without issuing tmux observations or pane
captures. Failed observations retain the last good cache and do not block
heartbeat retries, client expiry, or health logging.

Track tmux server lifecycle and pane PID in the inactivity tracker so recycled
pane IDs and respawns receive a fresh inactivity window while interruption stays

Use the resolved tmux socket for daemon state and mutation notifications,

wait for deferred metadata cleanup in integration test

preserve sidebar status on nested github query errors

revalidate cached sidebar repository roots

An agent path can gain or lose a nested Git repository while remaining active.

branch and dirty state, even when filesystem events keep refreshing that root.

recheck sidebar cleanup when startup grace expires

A sole-pane snapshot can arrive during startup grace and remain unchanged.

Keep the latest host pane count and schedule a one-shot grace deadline in the

Cover grace expiry without another snapshot, stale counts, and live verification.
Verify real tmux behavior for sole panes and content added during startup grace.

bound historical agent state

Keep the sidebar refresh path proportional to the active multiplexer context by
caching parsed state with replacement-aware filesystem identities. Unchanged
records avoid content reads and JSON parsing, while additions, repairs,
replacements, and deletions remain visible on the normal refresh cadence.

Compact known prior boot generations into durable per-context recovery
manifests with one resurrection-equivalent candidate per exact working
directory. Preserve current, foreign, malformed, and uncertain records, and use

and resurrection cleanup.

Strengthen tmux boot identity with the server PID, preserve existing state
formats and command behavior, and keep recovery candidates usable across
repeated restarts until successful resurrection consumes them.

preserve agent state across upgrades and recovery cleanup

This preserves agent session bindings without confusing distinct compound
server identities or archiving an ordinary same-process metadata update.

Consume a compacted flat snapshot only when the recovery entry's complete
source history is covered by the plan. Keep entries containing unplanned
sources or earlier aggregated history so concurrent additions survive cleanup.
Use durable manifest writes for finalization as well as publication, preserving

Add StateStore::clear_agent_status, which resets only the status fields
(status, status_ts) of the exact pane key and refreshes updated_ts, keeping
pane identity and metadata (PID, command, title, window/session, agent kind,
agent session, activity timestamp) intact. Because state is stored per pane
key, other panes and other multiplexer instances are untouched.

Wire it into the explicit clear path in apply_status_update and the sandbox
RPC clear handler so both host and guest clears persist the reset.

Cover the store semantics with unit tests and add a tmux integration test
that drives an explicit target through working then clear and asserts the
persisted status is reset while identity fields survive.

allow linked git hooks outside container sandboxes

Shared repository discovery rejected linked hooks even when no sandbox was

Move hook-layout validation into the container metadata boundary while
retaining config and pointer validation and host Git hook suppression.

Cover valid and dangling symlinks, hard links, and symlinked hook directories
from main and linked worktrees. Verify protected commits suppress hooks and
Docker, Podman, and Apple Container boundaries still reject linked layouts.
Keep malformed config and worktree pointer rejection covered.

fix session navigation when closing worktrees from tmux popups

Commands invoked from tmux popups lack TMUX_PANE, so session-mode remove
and close could destroy the displayed session without relocating clients.
Untargeted queries and delayed previous-session switches also followed
bystander activity or reversed a user's later focus change.

keeping strict pane ownership and status attribution unchanged. Close the
captured session ID with source-local detach-on-destroy disabled, allowing
tmux to relocate remaining viewers without changing global options. Restore
the original local value or inheritance if closure fails.

Prefer an available managed merge or main destination, then each source
viewer's previous session. Guard every explicit client switch inside tmux
against changed focus, server identity, and TTY alias shadowing. Leave
clients already elsewhere alone and retain native relocation as the fallback
for unavailable or ambiguous destinations. Preserve deferred Git and
filesystem safety checks and existing window-mode behavior.

Add attached-client popup regressions, stacked-merge destination checks,

the session-mode guide and changelog to describe the final behavior.

record pr target branch as review base

PR checkouts stored the remote head ref (for example `origin/feature`) as
`branch.<local>.workmux-base`. The dashboard review diff then compared the
head against itself and showed "No commits on this branch yet" even when
the PR contained changes.

Separate the ref used to populate the worktree from the ref recorded for
review. PR resolution now carries the target branch reported by the forge
(`baseRefName` on GitHub, `target_branch` on GitLab), so the create
workflow checks out the PR head while storing the target as the review
base. This also flows through the dashboard PR checkout path.

The target branch is refreshed from the target repository (`origin`)
before it is recorded, covering non-default targets, fork PRs, and
remote-tracking refs that are missing or stale. A fetch failure falls back
to an existing local ref with a warning, and a target that is missing
entirely fails with a clear error.

Ordinary branch and remote checkouts keep their previous base metadata.

Issue: #276

prevent fragmented deferred cleanup failure logs

Deferred cleanup failures append to the same log used by concurrent tracing
writers. Formatting directly into the file produces multiple writes, allowing
other records to split the failure fields and break exact log assertions.

Format each failure record in memory before appending it, retaining the
synchronous durability flush. Add a regression test requiring one write and
include the actual log when the substitution integration test times out.

The original CI failure did not reproduce in repeated Linux runs, so this
addresses a plausible logging race without relaxing the safety assertion or
increasing its timeout.

Pi and Oh My Pi can resolve their extension directories to the same path when

Remove OMP's blanket assistant message-end waiting transition. Tool-calling
assistant messages are immediately followed by execution, so the old handler
caused a brief false waiting state on every tool round. Waiting is now reported

The Nix build intermittently failed with ETXTBSY while executing a temporary
script immediately after creating it on the build filesystem. Exercise the
same configured executable and appended command behavior through the stable
system shell instead, avoiding filesystem-specific executable races without
reducing the assertion coverage.

The OMP status extension no longer handles message_end because that transition
briefly reported waiting before ordinary tool execution. Update the setup
integration test to require the handler's absence while retaining coverage for
the ask-tool waiting behavior.

fix lifecycle hook project root

Post-create hooks treated the selected config directory as the repository root.
Configs outside the repository therefore made WM_PROJECT_ROOT unusable for Git
commands, while nested configs exposed a subdirectory instead of the main
worktree.

Pass the workflow's main worktree root explicitly into provisioning and reserve
the config source directory for file operations. Preserve hook working
directories, WM_CONFIG_DIR, and config-relative file copying. Document the path
contracts and cover external and nested configuration cases.

Add an optional literal tmux session destination for clients viewing a closing

Honor the preference during remove, merge, and both synchronous and deferred

release v0.1.263
add completion generation step in brew formula (#284)

keep pi status working through compaction

The delegated-activity integration treated a zero-child snapshot as authority
over the parent's aborted continuation state. Codex compaction deliberately
aborts at a turn boundary, so this briefly reported done before its continuation
started and reset the elapsed status timer.

Preserve aborted parent activity when combining it with child activity. A later
successful continuation still reports done, while child snapshots continue to
control delegated activity independently.

detect node lockfiles one directory below the project root

The automatic node_modules fast-cleanup on worktree removal only triggered
when pnpm-lock.yaml, package-lock.json or yarn.lock sat directly at the
project root. Monorepos that keep the lockfile in a package directory, for
example dashboard/pnpm-lock.yaml, never got the default pre_remove hook and
had to vendor a copy of the cleanup script themselves to make `workmux rm`
return immediately.

Detection now also checks the immediate subdirectories of the project root.
The walk stops at depth 1 and skips hidden directories and node_modules,
which keeps it to a handful of directory reads: measured at 0.2-0.9 ms on a
miss and near zero on a hit at the root, since the root check runs first.
Going deeper is what gets expensive, mostly from build directories such as
target/debug, so depth stays at 1.

An explicit `pre_remove` in the config still wins, and `pre_remove: []`
still disables the hook entirely.

add <cleanup-node-modules> placeholder for pre_remove

The built-in node_modules fast-cleanup script was only reachable as an
automatic default: it is injected when a project defines no pre_remove
commands at all. Adding any hook of your own, such as copying test artifacts
out of the worktree, silently replaced it and made `workmux rm` slow again in
Node projects. The same happened to every Node project at once when a single
pre_remove entry was set in the global config, since the default is applied
after the global and project configs merge.

`pre_remove` entries equal to "<cleanup-node-modules>" now expand to the
built-in script, so the cleanup can be combined with other hooks and placed
at a chosen point in the list. Expansion runs after the merge, so the
placeholder also works when spliced in from the global config via "<global>".

This also gives projects an escape hatch when lockfile autodetection does not
fire, for example when the lockfile sits deeper than one directory below the
root or is not committed at all. Previously the only workaround was copying
the script out of the repository, which then drifts from the version shipped
in the binary.
changelog: link lifecycle hooks guide from cleanup placeholder entry

scale the dashboard worktree column with the pane (#281)

The Worktrees tab renders the worktree cell as `<handle> ->` plus the
branch when the two differ, but both the cell text and the column width
were capped at a hardcoded 25 columns. The cap ignored the terminal, so
the branch was cut off at any width -- rendering the tab with
`worktree_columns: [worktree]` alone in a 300-column pane still truncated
at 25, and the freed width went to the `git` column instead.

Derive the bound from the table area instead: half its width, clamped to
25..80. The lower bound is the old value, so narrow panes render exactly
as before; the upper one keeps a single long branch from crowding out the
other columns.

Issue: #293
release v0.1.264

fix sidebar resize reflow storm

A terminal resize emits one tmux window-resized hook for every affected
window. Each hook previously reflowed every sidebar, while every sidebar TUI
also started another global reflow. With many windows this multiplied into
quadratic layout work and made tmux temporarily unresponsive.

Target each resize hook at its own window and let the hook own terminal resize
reflow instead of duplicating it in every TUI. Keep global reflow for manual
sidebar width synchronization, and skip select-layout when the computed layout
already matches tmux state.

This preserves manual resize propagation while making terminal resize work
linear in the number of affected windows.

sidebar: add an opt-in grouped presentation with stale folding

A sidebar watching many repositories at once turns into a long
undifferentiated list, and most of it is agents nobody is waiting on.
This adds a second presentation that splits the list into sections and
folds the idle rows away.

It is off by default. Grouping suits a sidebar spanning many projects
and gets in the way of one watching a single project, so it is a
preference rather than a fix, and nothing changes for anyone who does
not ask for it.

What the grouped presentation does:

- One section per project or session, headed by the group's name and
  count. Headers are labels: navigation skips them, they cannot be
  selected, and they are not numbered. Their labels are indented two
  columns so a header reads as a heading over its rows.
- Each group's stale agents fold behind one dimmed toggle row. Stale
  means sleeping, or an hour with no progress and no working or waiting
  status: the same agents `dim_stale` already dims.
- Enter, a click, `h`/`l` or `s` folds and unfolds a group, and `S` does
  every group at once. Unfolded agents take one line instead of a full
  tile.
- A group left with no live work collapses into its own header row, and
  those groups sort below the rest under a rule marking where live work
  ends.
- The expanded set lives in a tmux global, so every sidebar pane agrees
  on it and the choice survives a tmux restart.

Turning it on:

    sidebar:
      group_by: project   # or session

`t` switches presentation at runtime without touching config, as does
`workmux sidebar group [MODE]`. Because a runtime choice is read before
config and outlives the session that made it, `workmux sidebar group
--clear` drops it so the config file decides again; without that, one
press of `t` would silently shadow `group_by` forever.

Templates:

A section header already names the project, so the stock tile row
repeating it as the secondary label would say it twice. Templates gained
a `grouped` block holding `compact`, `tiles` and `header`, and
`templates.group_header` moves to `templates.grouped.header`. While
grouped, a field there wins, then the ungrouped template of the same
name, then the built-in grouped default, so templates written before
grouping existed carry over and the block is only needed to make the two
presentations differ.

`{group_status}` is a new header token, tallying a group's agents by
status so a folded group can still say whether anything in it is
waiting. It is not in the default header: a count answers the common
question, and the tally costs width every group pays for.

Default templates now show the pull request number beside the checks
that were already there. A sidebar that reports a branch's checks but
not which pull request they belong to makes the reader go looking.

Numbering:

The daemon owns grouping, the staleness verdict and the folding decision
and publishes them with each snapshot; clients never resolve them from
their own config. Whoever owns the published pane list owns what folds,
so `{idx}`, `{jump_key}` and `workmux sidebar next|prev|jump <N>` always
address the rows on screen.

Jumping is for reaching work in progress, so a stale agent is not a
target and the numbers close up behind it. That holds wherever it is
drawn: folded away, shown from an opened fold, or sitting under a live
agent in a flat list.

Discovery:

Grouping is off by default, so nobody would find it. On the first
sidebar after the update, a footer bar offers it once, naming the `t`
that turns it on, and retires itself when answered or after a fortnight.
It appears only where it would help, when the sidebar is watching more
than one project.

Also adds `?`, a key overlay listing what the sidebar responds to. It
has never listed its keys anywhere, and with grouping off by default the
`t` that reveals it appears nowhere a user would look.

docs: show the sidebar's layouts and grouping

The sidebar guide described three presentations without showing any of

sidebar: keep stale agents on the hotkeys in a flat list

Jumping skipped stale agents everywhere, which is right while grouped:
there the sidebar already sorts them into a tail per group and offers to
fold it away, so it treats them as work nobody is waiting on.

A flat list makes no such distinction. It draws one row per agent with
nothing marking any of them as set aside, so skipping some when counting
hotkeys leaves a row the numbers cannot reach and no way to tell which.
Every agent a flat list shows now keeps its number.

release v0.1.267

prevent background hooks from stealing pane status

Claude background workers share the process ancestry of the interactive
session that started their supervisor. Ancestry alone therefore cannot tell an
attached /bg continuation from an unrelated claude --bg session, and the latter
could overwrite the interactive pane's status and session binding.

Prefer existing session bindings before ancestry. For Claude background hooks,
accept an ancestry candidate only when the previous session transcript records
an exact continued-in relationship to the incoming session. Registration now
captures the validated session ID so later hooks use the binding directly.
Other pane-less agents retain the existing ancestry behavior.

Add unit coverage for hook parsing, transcript validation, path constraints,
and ancestry ownership. Add a tmux integration test that accepts an attached
continuation while refusing an unrelated background session.
